meanings.note: Similar to 'b-sāḥitnā' but referring to a space belonging specifically to the speaker.

examples.trans: I like to drink coffee in my yard.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على بساحتي.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with بساحتي.

meanings.note: Commonly used to describe going on trips, usually international or long-distance.

examples.trans: Every summer I travel to Aqaba.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على بسافر.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with بسافر.

meanings.note: The word 'بسامح' (بسامح) means 'بسامح'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: رح ناخذهم التلاتة طوالي لـ مازن؛ ذوقه الصعب عمره ما بسامح أي غلطة.
examples.trans: We take all three straight to Mazen; his tough palate never forgives a mistake.
This is بسامح.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: بسطات.

examples.trans: Turn left at the stair landing.
The landing is wide and bright.

meanings.note: General term for any kind of sweet, dry baked good like a cookie or biscuit.

examples.trans: I ate biscuits with tea.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على بسكوت.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with بسكوت.

meanings.note: The word 'بسلاسة' (بسلاسة) means 'بسلاسة'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: صينية رقم تنين عليها كريمة ليمون حامضة. السكينة عم تمشي فيها بسلاسة.
examples.trans: Tin Two has a sharp lemon icing. The knife glides through nicely.
This is بسلاسة.

meanings.note: The word 'بسوق' (بسوق) means 'بسوق'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: التلطيخة الزرقا مش مكون بنباع بسوق السبت يا سعاد!
examples.trans: Blue smudge is not an ingredient sold at the Saturday market, Suad!
This is بسوق.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: بسيطة, plural: بسيطين).

examples.trans: Explain the matter to me in simple words.
The problem is minor and easy to fix.

meanings.note: Indicates location within a street or on a specific road.

examples.trans: I saw you on University Street.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على بشارع.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with بشارع.

meanings.note: The word 'بشاي' (بشاي) means 'بشاي'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: حلو كتير! ماشي يا مدير، نظف تمك بشاي أسود وجرب صينية رقم تنين!
examples.trans: Too sweet! Okay, Boss, wash your palate with black tea and try Tin Two!
This is بشاي.

بشكل.gloss: in a way / in a shape

meanings.en: in a way / in a shape
meanings.note: Often used as a prefix for adverbs, e.g., 'bi-shakil ʿām' (generally).

examples.trans: We need to work in a faster way.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على بشكل.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with بشكل.

meanings.note: The word 'بصبر' (بصبر) means 'بصبر'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: أنا راكضة! دفي الكيكة يا سلمى، وقولي لـ مازن يستنى بصبر!
examples.trans: I am running! Keep the cake warm, Salma, and tell Mazen to wait patiently!
This is بصبر.

meanings.note: The word 'بصراحة—هل' (بصراحة—هل) means 'بصراحة—هل'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: وهلق يا مازن؟ احكيلنا بصراحة—هل هالكيكة بتستاهل تنحط على طاولة الذكرى يوم السبت؟
examples.trans: Well, Mazen? Tell us honestly—is that worthy of our Saturday anniversary table?
This is بصراحة—هل.

meanings.note: Collective noun for onions; a single onion is بصلة.

examples.trans: We used the word بصل.
This is another بصل.

meanings.note: Refers to vocalization, often used in phrases like 'b-ṣōt ʿālī' (with a loud voice).

examples.trans: Don't speak with a loud voice.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على بصوت.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with بصوت.

meanings.note: The word 'بضل' (بضل) means 'بضل'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: أكيد! العسل الدافي بضل طري وبيلمع من غير ما يحمض أو يصير قاسي متل الحجر!
examples.trans: Of course! Warm honey stays soft and glossy without turning sour or rock hard!
This is بضل.

meanings.note: Plural of 'biṭāqa', can mean playing cards, identity cards, or event tickets.

examples.trans: I bought tickets for the match.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على بطاقات.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with بطاقات.

meanings.note: Singular form for any type of card (ID, credit, ticket, etc.).

examples.trans: My bank card is lost.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على بطاقة.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with بطاقة.

meanings.note: Most often heard in understated Jordanian praise: مش بطال ('not bad at all!').

examples.trans: Not bad for a first week of work!
The weather today is not bad at all.

meanings.note: Inner lining of a coat or the tiny wool-felt bushing inside a piano hinge.

examples.text: بطانة اللباد جوا المفصلة بدها تبديل بسيط.
examples.trans: The felt bushing inside the hinge just needs a small adjustment.

examples.text: هاد المعطف الشتوي إله بطانة صوف دافية.
examples.trans: This winter coat has a warm wool lining.

بطاولة.gloss: at a table / with a table

meanings.en: at a table / with a table
meanings.note: Indicates physical interaction or location relative to a table.

examples.trans: I bumped my leg against a table.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على بطاولة.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with بطاولة.

meanings.note: The word 'بطريقة' (بطريقة) means 'بطريقة'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: العسل الدافي مبين دبق وبلزق بطريقة بتجنن، بس هل هو وصفة محلية قديمة؟
examples.trans: Warm honey sounds delightfully sticky, but is it an old-fashioned local recipe?
This is بطريقة.

meanings.note: Form II verb (battal) used in imperatives like بطلي حركاتك ('cut out your antics').

examples.trans: Stop talking like that.
We stopped going there.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: بطلات.

examples.trans: You are the heroine of the kitchen today!
She ran fast like a champion.

meanings.note: The word 'بطنجرة' (بطنجرة) means 'بطنجرة'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: أي كتاب؟ سلمى رح تذوبها بطنجرة أول ما أركض من بوابة الساحة!
examples.trans: What book? Salma is melting it in a pot the second I sprint through the courtyard gate!
This is بطنجرة.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: بطيئة, plural: بطيئين).

examples.trans: Downtown traffic at noon is slow.
A slow step is better than rushing.

بطّل.gloss: to stop (doing); no longer be able

meanings.en: to stop (doing); no longer be able
meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (ببطل, بيبطل).

examples.trans: My knees stopped holding me up from the shock!
The rain stopped falling in the morning.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (ببعت, بيبعت).

examples.trans: Last week I sent him a postcard.
She sent a kind thank-you note.

meanings.note: Means 'after' (بعد المطر) and with a future span 'in' (بعد أربعين دقيقة 'in forty minutes').

examples.trans: He arrives in forty minutes.
How lovely the sun is after the rain!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for 'then, next, afterwards' (وبعدين 'and then').

examples.trans: Lift the handle first, and then push.
Have some tea and then we will talk.

meanings.note: The most fundamental way to state personal knowledge or awareness.

examples.trans: I know what happened.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على بعرف.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with بعرف.

meanings.note: The word 'بعصر' (بعصر) means 'بعصر'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: تلات كيكات اختبار بعصر يوم أحد؟ هادا هو البحث التاريخي اللي بدعمه!
examples.trans: Three test cakes on a Sunday afternoon? Now THAT is historical research I support!
This is بعصر.

meanings.note: After a plural verb, بعض means 'each other' (بننادي بعض 'we call each other').

examples.trans: We call each other by first name here.

examples.text: ما حكينا مع بعض من زمان.
examples.trans: We have not spoken with each other in a long time.

meanings.note: The word 'بعمود' (بعمود) means 'بعمود'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: لحظة—في حلقة حديد مطروق مربوطة دغري بعمود البلوط الثقيل!
examples.trans: Hold on—there is a forged iron ring bolted straight into the heavy oak post!
This is بعمود.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: بعيدة, plural: بعاد).

examples.trans: The shop is not far from the gate.

examples.text: الطاولة تحت الشجرة بعيد عن الباب.
examples.trans: The table is under the tree away from the door.

meanings.note: Specifies location inside a room of a building.

examples.trans: The boy is sleeping in the guest room.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على بغرفة.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with بغرفة.

بغطا.gloss: with a cover / in a cover

meanings.en: with a cover / in a cover
meanings.note: Refers to a lid, cap, or a blanket covering something.

examples.trans: Close the pot with a lid.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على بغطا.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with بغطا.

meanings.note: A highly versatile prefix used as a preposition of place or instrument.

examples.trans: We went to work by car.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على بـ.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with بـ.

meanings.note: Expresses the action of astonishing or surprising someone.

examples.trans: I always surprise my friends on their birthdays.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على بفاجئ.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with بفاجئ.

meanings.note: Refers to the lowest part of a container, the sea, or any deep object.

examples.trans: The key fell at the bottom of the pool.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على بقاع.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with بقاع.

meanings.note: Used to indicate something is rhymed.

examples.trans: He wrote the poem with a nice rhyme.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على بقافية.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with بقافية.

meanings.note: Everyday Levantine word for parsley.

examples.trans: We used the word بقدونس.
This is another بقدونس.

meanings.note: Used to indicate authorship or the instrument used.

examples.trans: This article is by a famous writer.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على بقلم.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with بقلم.

meanings.note: Used to refer to something made of or covered with fabric.

examples.trans: He covered the table with a red cloth.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على بقماش.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with بقماش.

meanings.note: The word 'بقوة' (بقوة) means 'بقوة'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: خلينا ناخده طوالي لـ سلمى بغرفة تسعة قبل ما حدا يتنفس بقوة!
examples.trans: Let us carry it straight to Salma in Room Nine before anyone breathes too hard!
This is بقوة.

meanings.note: Everyday word for 'tomorrow' (بكرا الصبح 'tomorrow morning').

examples.text: بكرا الصبح رح نسبق المي الباردة!
examples.trans: Tomorrow morning we will beat the cold water!
We booked a quiet dinner — will you join us tomorrow?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for 'tomorrow' (أشوفك بكرة! 'See you tomorrow!').

examples.trans: We have an exam tomorrow morning.
See you tomorrow at school!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for expressing the price or cost of an item or service.

examples.trans: This project costs a lot of money.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على بكلف.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with بكلف.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (ببكي, بيبكي).

examples.trans: The poor gentleman looks about to cry.
We laughed and nobody cried in the end.

meanings.note: Signature Levantine word for 'early'.

examples.trans: You arrived ten minutes early.
We wake up early every day.

meanings.note: The word 'بكيكات' (بكيكات) means 'بكيكات'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: لا. الليمون عم يتخانق بقوة مع التوت المستوي. لازم يكونوا بكيكات مختلفة.
examples.trans: No. The lemon fights aggressively with the ripe berries. They belong in different cakes.
This is بكيكات.

meanings.note: Everyday Levantine preposition meaning 'without' or 'let's skip / no…' (قهوة بلا سكر 'coffee without sugar').

examples.text: بشرب الشاي بنعنع وبلا سكر لو سمحت.
examples.trans: I drink mint tea without sugar, please.

examples.text: بلا عجلة، قدامنا تلات أيام كاملة.
examples.trans: No rush—we have three full days ahead of us.

meanings.note: Everyday masculine loanword for plastic wrap, sleeves, or containers.

examples.text: غلّفت الوصفة ببلاستيك عشان ما تتبلل.
examples.trans: She sealed the recipe in plastic so it would not get wet.

examples.text: ما بنحب نحط الشاي بكاسات بلاستيك.
examples.trans: We do not like serving tea in plastic cups.

meanings.note: Collective masculine noun for stone, ceramic, or courtyard tiles; single tile is بلاطة.

examples.trans: We wiped the courtyard tiles with water this morning.

examples.text: بلاط المطبخ بارد على الرجلين بالشتاء.
examples.trans: The kitchen tile is cold on the feet in winter.

meanings.note: Plural of بلاطة, the everyday Arabic word for a paving stone or floor tile.

examples.trans: We used the word بلاطة.
This is another بلاطة.

meanings.note: In Amman, وسط البلد or simply البلد refers to downtown Amman.

examples.trans: We went down to downtown in the morning.
Town is quiet on Friday.

meanings.note: From بلد ('country, town'); prized on Jordanian market stalls for local olive oil, honey, lemons, and thyme.

examples.text: عسل بلدي من جبال عجلون ريحته بتشهي.
examples.trans: Local honey from the Ajloun hills smells delicious.
We bought yellow local lemons for tea.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: بلديات.

examples.trans: He works in the contracts office at the municipality.
The municipal building is next to the square.

meanings.note: Everyday Levantine verb for starting something or starting a fight (هي اللي بلشت 'she's the one who started it').

examples.trans: Class started a little while ago.
Who started the problem?

meanings.note: The word 'بلكونة' (balkoonet) means 'balcony'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: وشوفوا لفوق على بلكونة الساحة الخشبية بالطابق التاني—نجمة حمرا فاقعة مرسومة!
examples.trans: And look up on the second-floor wooden courtyard balcony—a bright red painted star!
This is بلكونة.

meanings.note: The word 'بلكي' (balki) means 'perhaps'. It is a common adv in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: بلكي المغلف الصغير المختوم بالشمع بجيبتك فيه الجواب يا نور!
examples.trans: Perhaps the small wax-sealed envelope in your pocket has the answer, Nour!
This is بلكي.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: The table is made of oak wood.
Oak trees are old and strong.

meanings.note: The word 'بلوك' (blokkaat) means 'blocks'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: اطنعشر دقة! أكيد هادا برج الساعة البلدي القديم تلات بلوكات لفوق!
examples.trans: Twelve chimes! That has to be the old municipal clock tower three blocks up!
This is بلوك.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (ببلش, بيبلش).

examples.trans: The brass pipe started heating up right away!
The clock tower started chiming twelve.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (ببلغ, بيبلغ).

examples.text: في حدا بلغ عن شنتة زرقا؟
examples.trans: Has anyone reported a blue suitcase?
We gave the office the phone number.

meanings.note: The word 'بمختبر' (بمختبر) means 'بمختبر'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: أهلا فيكم بمختبر كيكة التوت تبع يوم الأحد يا متدربين! غسلتوا إيديكم ورفعتوا أكمامكم؟
examples.trans: Welcome to the Sunday Berry Cake Laboratory, apprentices! Hands washed and sleeves rolled?
This is بمختبر.

meanings.note: The word 'بمعلقتين' (بمعلقتين) means 'بمعلقتين'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: خليني أشوف من نظاراتي: ادهني الكيكة الدافية بمعلقتين من... تلطيخة زرقا!
examples.trans: Let me look through my glasses: Brush warm cake with two spoons of... blue smudge!
This is بمعلقتين.

meanings.note: Indicates a location or a specific spot.

examples.trans: I put it in a safe place.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على بمكان.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with بمكان.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: بنايات.

examples.trans: The stone building is eighty years old.
The building owner sent a letter.

meanings.note: The word 'بنباع' (بنباع) means 'بنباع'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: التلطيخة الزرقا مش مكون بنباع بسوق السبت يا سعاد!
examples.trans: Blue smudge is not an ingredient sold at the Saturday market, Suad!
This is بنباع.

meanings.note: Singular بنت, definite البنت, plural بنات / البنات ('AlRawabi School for Girls' = مدرسة الروابي للبنات).

examples.trans: She is a very bright girl.
The girls are standing in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: بنود.

examples.trans: Read clause four in the contract.
This clause protects the tenant.

meanings.note: Standard Levantine collective word for tomatoes (from Italian pomodoro).

examples.trans: The roasted tomato soup smells mouthwatering.

examples.text: اشترينا كيلو بندورة حمرا من سوق السبت.
examples.trans: We bought a kilo of ripe red tomatoes at the Saturday market.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (ببنشر, بيبنشر).

examples.trans: The dairy van got a flat tyre outside town.
The tyre went flat on the road this morning.

meanings.note: The word 'بنطلع' (بنطلع) means 'بنطلع'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: لعد يوم الجمعة الصبح بنطلع عالبلكونة بحبل متين وبنختبر كل عقدة!
examples.trans: Then Friday morning we climb onto that balcony with sturdy cord and test every knot!
This is بنطلع.

meanings.note: The word 'بنعرف' (بنعرف) means 'بنعرف'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: لا تخاف يا مدير؛ احنا بنعرف أساس الكيكة، عشان هيك مطبخي رح يختبر تلات طبقات تلميع!
examples.trans: Do not panic, boss; we know the cake base, so my kitchen will test three glazes!
This is بنعرف.

meanings.note: Reflexive pronoun used for second person plural.

examples.trans: You must do this thing by yourselves.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على بنفسكم.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with بنفسكم.

meanings.note: Commonly used in Jordanian Arabic to mean "it is acceptable" or "it works".

examples.trans: This solution works for us.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على بنفع.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with بنفع.

meanings.note: Used to say "we are walking" or "let us go".

examples.trans: Come on, let's walk now.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على بنمشي.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with بنمشي.

meanings.note: Everyday verb بنى (to build).

examples.trans: We used the word بنى.
This is another بنى.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: بنية, plural: بنيين).

examples.trans: The brown leather notebook is on the desk.
A clean pair of men's brown shoes.

meanings.note: Used in Levantine dialects to mean "like this" or "with this kind of".

examples.trans: In such a case, we must be careful.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على بهيك.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with بهيك.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: بوابات.

examples.trans: The courtyard gate is open for guests.
The taxi stopped outside the gate.

meanings.note: Refers to a gate belonging to a group (us).

examples.trans: Our gate is closed today.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على بوابتنا.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with بوابتنا.

meanings.note: Used for navigation or metaphorically for direction.

examples.text: ضاع بالصحراء لأنه ما كان معه بوصلة.
examples.trans: He got lost in the desert because he didn't have a compass.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على بوصلة.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with بوصلة.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: بياعين.

examples.trans: The shopkeeper gave me a receipt and change.
I asked the clerk about the size.

meanings.note: The musical instrument.

examples.trans: He plays the piano every day.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على بيانو.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with بيانو.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: بيوت.

examples.trans: The old house has a lovely courtyard.
The neighbourhood houses are built of stone.

meanings.note: The word 'بيتنا' (بيتنا) means 'بيتنا'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: قوة ملاحظة يا مازن! مكتوب بالرصاص بالزاوية نفس رقم بيتنا من تلاتين سنة!
examples.trans: Good eye, Mazen! Pencilled in the corner is our exact house number from thirty years ago!
This is بيتنا.

meanings.note: Describes the action of baking bread or pastries.

examples.text: هو بيخبز خبز طازج كل الصبح.
examples.trans: He bakes fresh bread every morning.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على بيخبز.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with بيخبز.

meanings.note: Feminine/masculine noun used in the beloved Levantine proverb سرك ببير ('your secret is in a well' = safe with me).

examples.trans: Do not worry, your secret is safe with me.
Well water is cold in summer.

meanings.note: Loanword from English 'bass', referring to the bass line, bass guitar, or upright bass.

examples.text: خط البيز هو اللي بيمسك إيقاع الأغنية.
examples.trans: The bass line is what holds the rhythm of the song.

examples.text: صوت البيز كان واطي شوي بالبروفة.
examples.trans: The bass sound was a bit low in the rehearsal.

meanings.note: Collective plural بيض ('eggs'), singulative بيضة ('one egg'), dual بيضتين ('two eggs').

examples.trans: I fried two eggs for breakfast.
Hot eggs are delicious with bread.

meanings.note: Plural form of egg, commonly used when counting eggs.

examples.trans: I bought five eggs from the shop.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على بيضات.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with بيضات.

meanings.note: Describes a group of people laughing.

examples.trans: The boys are laughing loudly.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على بيضحكوا.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with بيضحكوا.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: The building is not up for sale.
The bill of sale is ready in the office.

meanings.note: Used to explain or clarify a point.

examples.text: هذا الاشي بيعني انه احنا خلصنا.
examples.trans: This thing means that we are finished.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على بيعني.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with بيعني.

meanings.note: Preposition 'between, among'.

examples.trans: Today you are mending things between two brothers!
The table is between the window and the door.

meanings.note: Used to contrast two different situations or actions happening at the same time.

examples.text: هو كان بدرس بينما أنا كنت بلعب.
examples.trans: He was studying while I was playing.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على بينما.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with بينما.

meanings.note: The word 'بيوم' (بيوم) means 'بيوم'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: طنين طنين بيوم أحد هادي—هاد الرنين المزدوج أكيد غرفة أربعة.
examples.trans: Buzz-buzz on a quiet Sunday—that double ring is definitely Room Four.
This is بيوم.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (ببين, بيبين).

examples.text: لما بدهم يبينوا هاديين بيتأخروا دقيقتين.
examples.trans: When they want to play it cool, they arrive two minutes late.
The truth came out at the end of the week.

meanings.note: Imperative ابعدوا ('step back!'); distinct from preposition بعد ('after').

examples.trans: Step back from the window, all of you!
He moved the chair slightly away from the door.

meanings.note: As a noun after على (على بعد عشر أمتار 'at a distance of ten metres'); distinct from preposition بعد ('after').

examples.trans: The shop is five minutes away.
The stop is a hundred metres away.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بتأخر, بيتأخر).

examples.trans: Tell me I am not late for the lesson!
The bus was not even a minute late.

meanings.note: Past tense Arabic verb meaning 'to make sure' or 'verify', conjugated for a woman.

examples.trans: We used the word تأكد.
This is another تأكد.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بتأكد, بيتأكد).

examples.trans: I am just checking safety.
Make sure the size is twenty millimetres.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: تابلتات.

examples.trans: The tablet screen is clear and large.
I left the tablet on the desk.

meanings.note: The word 'تاخد' (تاخد) means 'تاخد'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: استنتاج بسيط! صينية رقم واحد رح تاخد طبقة سكر وفانيليا دافية؛ هادا تشطيب كلاسيكي.
examples.trans: Simple deduction! Tin One gets a warm vanilla sugar glaze; that is a classic finish.
This is تاخد.

meanings.note: Baked fruit or custard tart, especially تارت الليمون ('lemon tart').

examples.text: تارت الليمون بقشرة اللوز طلع أطيب واحد.
examples.trans: The lemon tart with the almond crust turned out to be the tastiest one.

examples.text: خلينا قطعة تارت صغيرة لطارق بالمطبخ.
examples.trans: We saved a small slice of tart for Tariq in the kitchen.

meanings.note: Means both a calendar 'date' (تاريخ البطاقة 'the date on the card') and 'history'.

examples.trans: Write today's date at the top of the page.

examples.text: هاد البيت القديم إله تاريخ حلو بعمان.
examples.trans: This old house has a lovely history in Amman.

meanings.note: Nisba adjective from تاريخ (history), agreeing with الساحة.

examples.trans: We used the word تاريخي.
This is another تاريخي.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: تاسعة, plural: تاسعين).

examples.trans: We found a ninth brass key in the box.

examples.text: الباب التاسع كان مخفي ورا الحيط.
examples.trans: The ninth door was hidden behind the wall.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: تكاسي.

examples.trans: A yellow taxi pulled up at the pavement.
We took a taxi to the bus station.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: تالتة, plural: تالتين).

examples.trans: The attic room is on the third floor.
He used to sit on the third step.

meanings.note: The word 'تام' (تام) means 'تام'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: بدون حكي من موظفين المطبخ، لو سمحتوا. التذوق المضبوط بده هدوء تام.
examples.trans: No talking from the kitchen staff, please. A proper tasting requires complete silence.
This is تام.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: تانية, plural: تانيين).

examples.trans: Room four is on the second floor.
There is a second sheet behind the letter.

meanings.note: The word 'تانية' (تانية) means 'تانية'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: أخد لقمة تانية! يا سلمى، ما عمل كشرة تلميع النحاس!
examples.trans: He took a second bite! Salma, he did not make the brass-polish face!
This is تانية.

meanings.note: Refers to making a substitution or changing something.

examples.trans: We need to do a changing of clothes.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على تبديل.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with تبديل.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بتبدل, بيتبدل).

examples.trans: A blue suitcase got swapped at the bus station.
The keys were never mixed up.

meanings.note: The word 'تبرد' (تبرد) means 'تبرد'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: معنا عشر دقايق بالزبط قبل ما تبرد الكيكة وترفض أي طبقة تلميع دافية!
examples.trans: We have exactly ten minutes before the cake cools down and rejects any warm glaze!
This is تبرد.

meanings.note: Form II verbal noun of برّد (to cool down).

examples.trans: We used the word تبريد.
This is another تبريد.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian and Levantine word used as a possessive marker, similar to "of" or "'s".

examples.trans: My brother's car is broken.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على تبع.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with تبع.

meanings.note: The feminine form of the Levantine possessive marker.

examples.trans: Reem's bag is lost.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على تبعت.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with تبعت.

meanings.note: The word 'تبعتي' (تبعتي) means 'تبعتي'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: بالزبط يا زياد. وصينية رقم تلاتة رح تاخد الورقة الرابحة تبعتي: دهنة خفيفة من العسل الدافي.
examples.trans: Exactly, Ziad. And Tin Three gets my wild card: a thin brush of warm honey.
This is تبعتي.

meanings.note: The word 'تبعون' (تبعون) means 'تبعون'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: شوفوا بالزبط بين هدول الغصنين الناشفين تبعون نعناع الحديقة والمليسة.
examples.trans: Look right between these two dry sprigs of garden mint and lemon balm.
This is تبعون.

meanings.note: The word 'تبعونه' (تبعونه) means 'تبعونه'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: وهادا القاضي مازن لابس نظارات القراءة تبعونه، ومبين جدي كتير الصراحة.
examples.trans: And here is Judge Mazen with his reading glasses on, looking very serious indeed.
This is تبعونه.

meanings.note: Used to indicate first-person possession.

examples.trans: This book is mine, not yours.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على تبعي.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with تبعي.

meanings.note: The word 'تبلشوا' (تبلشوا) means 'تبلشوا'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: استنوا... خلوا الزلمة يمضغ منيح قبل ما تبلشوا تحتفلوا إنتو التنتين.
examples.trans: Wait... let a man chew properly before you two start celebrating.
This is تبلشوا.

meanings.note: Form V intransitive verb meaning 'get wet / soaked in the rain'.

examples.text: دخلنا الشيش جوا قبل ما يتبلل الخشب.
examples.trans: We brought the shutters inside before the wood got soaked.
My sleeves got a little wet from the rain.

meanings.note: The word 'تتحركي' (تتحركي) means 'تتحركي'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: لا تتحركي عن مقعد البيانو يا سعاد؛ الكيكة الحقيقية رح تجهز بعد خمس دقايق!
examples.trans: Do not move from that piano bench, Suad; the real cake is five minutes away!
This is تتحركي.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: تجارية, plural: تجاريين).

examples.trans: Converting the house into commercial offices is forbidden.
This is a residential street, not commercial.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: تجارب.

examples.trans: The trial week went by fast.
It was a very sweet experience.

meanings.note: Formed from تجريد ('abstraction'). Feminine singular: تجريدية.

examples.trans: Abstract art has bold colours.
This painting is very abstract.

meanings.note: The word 'تجهز' (تجهز) means 'تجهز'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: لا تتحركي عن مقعد البيانو يا سعاد؛ الكيكة الحقيقية رح تجهز بعد خمس دقايق!
examples.trans: Do not move from that piano bench, Suad; the real cake is five minutes away!
This is تجهز.

meanings.note: Often a colloquial pronunciation or a typo of "تجبري" (tijibri), meaning to force someone or set a broken bone.

examples.text: ما بتقدري تجيبري حدا على شي ما بده ياه.
examples.trans: You cannot force anyone into something they don't want.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على تجيبري.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with تجيبري.

meanings.note: Indicates physical location beneath something.

examples.trans: The cat is hiding under the table.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على تحت.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with تحت.

meanings.note: Levantine relational adjective formed from تحت ('under/below') + -aani; opposite of فوقاني.

examples.trans: The tuning wrench is in the bottom drawer.

examples.text: نور مسحت الألواح التحتانية للشباك الكبير.
examples.trans: Nour wiped the lower panes of the tall window.

meanings.note: The word 'تحتفلوا' (تحتفلوا) means 'تحتفلوا'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: استنوا... خلوا الزلمة يمضغ منيح قبل ما تبلشوا تحتفلوا إنتو التنتين.
examples.trans: Wait... let a man chew properly before you two start celebrating.
This is تحتفلوا.

meanings.note: Preposition with the third-person masculine singular suffix attached.

examples.trans: The box has something under it.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على تحته.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with تحته.

meanings.note: Preposition with the third-person feminine singular suffix attached.

examples.trans: The carpet has money under it.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على تحتها.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with تحتها.

meanings.note: With progressive عم (عم بتتحديني؟), Layan asks 'are you challenging me right now?'.

examples.trans: Nobody challenges her at school.
Are you challenging me?

meanings.note: Describes the action of protecting or guarding a place.

examples.trans: She guards the building at night.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على تحرس.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with تحرس.

meanings.note: Intransitive 'move': ما بتتحرك خطوة بدونهم ('she doesn't move a step without them').

examples.trans: The bus started moving.
Move over a little, please.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بتحرك, بيتحرك).

examples.text: في قطعة معدن تحركت جوا الصندوق!
examples.trans: A piece of metal shifted inside the box!
The car pulled away from the door.

meanings.note: Verbal noun of حضّر ('to prepare'). Plural: تحضيرات.

examples.trans: Coffee prep takes ten minutes.
All preparations for the party are ready.

meanings.note: Everyday praise word for anything beautifully crafted (تحفة فنية 'a work of art'). Plural: تحف.

examples.trans: Your lettering on paper is a work of art!
This old chair is a real treasure.

meanings.note: Construes with بـ or في: بتحكموا فينا ('you boss us around / control us').

examples.trans: I don't like anyone bossing me around.
Try to control your nerves.

meanings.note: Covers enduring mistreatment (يتحمل الظلم) and taking responsibility (نتحمل المسؤولية).

examples.text: ما بقدر أتحمل أكتر من هيك.
examples.trans: I can't put up with more than this.
We must take responsibility.

meanings.note: Form V verb (بيتحمّل / تحمّلت). Used for enduring stress, weight, or a surprise inspection.

examples.text: قلبي ما بيتحمّل تفتيش تاني اليوم!
examples.trans: My heart cannot survive another inspection today!
This brick endures rain and heavy weight.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: تحويلات.

examples.trans: Converting the building into offices is prohibited.
We read the conversion request in the morning.

meanings.note: Feminine noun from حوّل ('to divert/turn'): a side turn in a road or trail, or a call extension.

examples.text: خد التحويلة اللي على إيدك اليمين.
examples.trans: Take the turnoff on your right-hand side.

examples.text: في تحويلة جديدة على طريق المطار.
examples.trans: There is a new detour on the airport road.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: تحيات.

examples.trans: Here is to all our kind neighbours!
He returned the greeting with a warm smile.

meanings.note: The word 'تخاف' (تخاف) means 'تخاف'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: لا تخاف يا مدير؛ احنا بنعرف أساس الكيكة، عشان هيك مطبخي رح يختبر تلات طبقات تلميع!
examples.trans: Do not panic, boss; we know the cake base, so my kitchen will test three glazes!
This is تخاف.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بتخانق, بيتخانق).

examples.trans: We used to argue over the corner piece!
We fell out over selling the old house.

meanings.note: Used for the action of concealing something.

examples.trans: Why are you hiding the truth?

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على تخبي.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with تخبي.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بتخبى, بيتخبى).

examples.trans: Why did you hide behind a mysterious note?

examples.text: القطة تخبت تحت الطاولة من المطر.
examples.trans: The cat hid under the table from the rain.

meanings.note: Everyday Levantine word for a bed (from Persian takht).

examples.trans: The wooden bed is very comfortable.
I put the clean sheet on the bed.

meanings.note: The word 'تخلي' (تخلي) means 'تخلي'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: ورشة من قشر البرتقال المبروش بتعطي نكهة لتوت الصيف من غير ما تخلي مازن يكشر!
examples.trans: And a pinch of grated orange peel brightens the summer berries without puckering Mazen!
This is تخلي.

meanings.note: Often used to refer to dough rising due to yeast.

examples.trans: The dough fermented and became ready for baking.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على تخمر.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with تخمر.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بتخيل, بيتخيل).

examples.trans: Imagine how the whole story started!
I never imagined finding the train here.

meanings.note: Form V verb تدرّب (to practise/rehearse), pairing with على before the thing practised.

examples.trans: We used the word تدرّب.
This is another تدرّب.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun.

examples.trans: The heating is working in all the rooms.
The heating pipe is warm now.

meanings.note: The word 'تدهنيها' (تدهنيها) means 'تدهنيها'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: استني—لا تدهنيها لحالها سادة! اقرأي كتاب النباتات بالأول!
examples.trans: Wait—do not just brush it on plain! Read the botanical book first!
This is تدهنيها.

meanings.note: Masculine noun for a memento or keepsake (plural: تذكارات). From the same root as تذكّر ('remember').

examples.text: كل واحد حط تذكار صغير بالعلبة.
examples.trans: Everyone put one small keepsake in the tin.

examples.text: هاي الخريطة أحلى تذكار من أستاذنا.
examples.trans: This map is the loveliest keepsake from our teacher.

meanings.note: The word 'تذكر' (tdhakkart) means 'you remembered'. It is a common verb in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: تذكرت تنزل نظارات القراءة تبعتك قبل ما تختار هاللّفة يا رامي؟
examples.trans: Did you remember to pull your reading glasses down before choosing that turn, Rami?
This is تذكر.

meanings.note: Train, bus, or concert ticket.

examples.text: حجزت تذكرة قطار ليوم السبت الصبح.
examples.trans: I booked a train ticket for Saturday morning.

examples.text: حطيت التذاكر بجيبتي عشان ما تضيع.
examples.trans: I put the tickets in my pocket so they wouldn't get lost.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بتذكر, بيتذكر).

examples.trans: Remember your three simple sentences.
I can remember them easily.

meanings.note: The word 'تذوبها' (تذوبها) means 'تذوبها'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: أي كتاب؟ سلمى رح تذوبها بطنجرة أول ما أركض من بوابة الساحة!
examples.trans: What book? Salma is melting it in a pot the second I sprint through the courtyard gate!
This is تذوبها.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: Heritage law protects old houses.
Amman has beautiful architectural heritage.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: تراثية, plural: تراثيين).

examples.trans: He works on restoring heritage buildings in Amman.

examples.text: هاد بيت تراثي عمره تمانين سنة.
examples.trans: This is a historic house eighty years old.

meanings.note: Verbal noun of رتّب ('to tidy, arrange'); بترتيب means 'neatly, in neat order'.

examples.trans: We lined the chairs up neatly beside the wall.

examples.text: ترتيب الطاولات بالساحة ما أخد عشر دقايق.
examples.trans: Arranging the tables in the courtyard did not take ten minutes.

meanings.note: Verbal noun of رحّب (to welcome), central to Jordanian hospitality.

examples.trans: We used the word ترحيب.
This is another ترحيب.

meanings.note: Nisba adjective from ترحيب ('welcoming'). Feminine: ترحيبية (لوحة ترحيبية 'welcome sign').

examples.text: كتبنا لوحة ترحيبية للضيف قبل ما يوصل.
examples.trans: We wrote a welcome sign for the guest before he arrived.
A welcoming smile is the most important thing at the front desk.

meanings.note: Form V verb meaning 'be promoted to a higher post or role'.

examples.text: نور ترقت وصارت موظفة استقبال رسمية.
examples.trans: Nour got promoted to permanent receptionist.
We got promoted today to café taste testers!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بترك, بيترك).

examples.text: مين ترك هاد المغلف جنب الجرس؟
examples.trans: Who left this envelope by the bell?
Thank you for not leaving me in the rain.

meanings.note: The word 'تركتها' (تركتها) means 'تركتها'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: تركتها من غير طبقة تلميع بالمرة! مرطبان العسل بالمونة كان فاضي عالاخر!
examples.trans: I left it completely unglazed! The honey jar in the pantry was totally empty!
This is تركتها.

meanings.note: The word 'تركتيها' (تركتيها) means 'تركتيها'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: استنوا—وين صينية رقم تلاتة؟ تركتيها قاعدة على شبك الفرن الدافي يا سلمى؟
examples.trans: Wait—where is Tin Three? Did you leave it sitting on the warm stove rack, Salma?
This is تركتيها.

meanings.note: Verbal noun of رمّم, standard term for architectural restoration of heritage buildings.

examples.trans: We used the word ترميم.
This is another ترميم.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for waiting for someone or something.

examples.trans: You must wait your turn in line.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على تستنى.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with تستنى.

meanings.note: The number 9.

examples.trans: I have nine books on the shelf.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على تسعة.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with تسعة.

meanings.note: The word 'تسعطعش' (tisa3Ta3sh) means 'nineteen'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: خمسة، عشرة، خمسطعش... ثمنطعش، تسعطعش، وعشرين خطوة عالرصيف بالزبط!
examples.trans: Five, ten, fifteen... eighteen, nineteen, and twenty paces right to the kerb!
This is تسعطعش.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian numeral 'nineteen' before a counted noun.

examples.trans: I wrote nineteen reasons on the sheet!
He is nineteen years old.

تشرّف.gloss: to be honoured (تشرفنا nice to meet you)

meanings.en: to be honoured (تشرفنا nice to meet you)
meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بتشرف, بيتشرف).

examples.trans: Lovely to meet you, Salma!
I am honoured to have met you all.

meanings.note: The word 'تشطيب' (تشطيب) means 'تشطيب'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: استنتاج بسيط! صينية رقم واحد رح تاخد طبقة سكر وفانيليا دافية؛ هادا تشطيب كلاسيكي.
examples.trans: Simple deduction! Tin One gets a warm vanilla sugar glaze; that is a classic finish.
This is تشطيب.

meanings.note: The word 'تشم' (تشم) means 'تشم'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: وثقي فيي! قولي لـ سعاد تشم الورقة محل ما كان كرت الوصفة محطوط!
examples.trans: Trust me! Tell Suad to smell the paper where the recipe card rested!
This is تشم.

meanings.note: Colloquial Form II verbal noun coined from Arabicized شيّك ('to check', from English). Used for quick safety or list checks.

examples.text: نعمل تشييك سريع عالأغراض قبل ما نطلع.
examples.trans: Let's do a quick check on the things before we head out.

examples.text: تشييك الكهربا أخد خمس دقايق بس.
examples.trans: The electrical check took only five minutes.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بتصالح, بيتصالح).

examples.trans: Thank goodness the two brothers finally made peace!
We reconciled and drank tea together.

meanings.note: Used with manner phrases like بشكل طبيعي ('in a normal way') or بطبيعتك ('naturally').

examples.trans: I acted calmly in front of everyone.
Act naturally.

meanings.note: Form II verbal noun from صلّح ('to repair'). Plural تصليحات refers to repair jobs.

examples.text: السكة محتاجة تصليح بسيط قبل الظهر.
examples.trans: The track needs a small repair before noon.
We took the radio to the repair shop.

meanings.note: Standard Arabic noun for 'design', derived from صمّم ('to design').

examples.trans: We used the word تصميم.
This is another تصميم.

meanings.note: The word 'تضرب' (تضرب) means 'تضرب'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: سما صافية، ليالي دافية، وهبات هواء ربيعية نشطة رح تضرب البلد يوم الجمعة.
examples.trans: Clear skies, warm evenings, and brisk spring wind gusts sweeping across town on Friday.
This is تضرب.

meanings.note: Used to say stay, remain, or keep doing something.

examples.trans: You must stay here and not move.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على تضل.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with تضل.

meanings.note: The word 'تضوي' (تضوي) means 'تضوي'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: جيب سلمي الخشب الساعة تسعة بالزبط—هاي الساحة رح تضوي متل ضو النهار!
examples.trans: Bring my wooden ladder at nine sharp—this courtyard is going to glow like daylight!
This is تضوي.

meanings.note: The word 'تطلب' (تطلب) means 'تطلب'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: أها! كشفناك عم تطلب كمان شقفة يا حضرة القاضي الصعب!
examples.trans: Aha! Caught you asking for seconds, Mr Tough Judge!
This is تطلب.

meanings.note: Core Levantine verb for 'look (at)' taking على or في.

examples.text: تطلعي من الشباك شوفي لون الشيش الأخضر!
examples.trans: Look out the window and see the green colour of the shutters!

examples.text: ليش بتطلعوا علي هيك؟ هلا بمسح الدهان!
examples.trans: Why are you staring at me like that? I'll wipe the paint right now!

meanings.note: Refers to moving upwards, outside, or appearing.

examples.trans: I want you (pl.) to go outside.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على تطلعوا.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with تطلعوا.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: تطورات.

examples.trans: That is excellent progress at work.
We heard the latest developments in the morning.

meanings.note: An imperative-only word: تعال to a man, تعالي to a woman, تعالوا to a group. Other tenses use إجا.

examples.trans: Come and sit next to me.
Come to the kitchen, all of you!

meanings.note: Imperative command telling a group of people to come over.

examples.trans: Come, let's visit my grandfather's house.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على تعالوا.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with تعالوا.

meanings.note: Universal everyday Jordanian adjective for 'tired' (feminine: تعبانة, plural: تعبانين).

examples.text: أنا تعبان شوي من رحلة الباص الطويلة.
examples.trans: I am a little tired from the long bus trip.

examples.text: صوتي تعبان اليوم، بس قلبي فرحان.
examples.trans: My voice is tired today, but my heart is glad.

meanings.note: Past tense Levantine Arabic verb meaning 'to get filled up'.

examples.trans: We used the word تعبّى.
This is another تعبّى.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: تعديلات.

examples.trans: The old wire needs a small adjustment.
We made a small adjustment to the schedule.

meanings.note: Wooden or iron garden trellis supporting climbing jasmine, grapevines, or ivy.

examples.text: رفعنا عرق اللبلاب شوي شوي عالتعريشة.
examples.trans: We lifted the ivy vine gently onto the trellis.

examples.text: القعدة تحت تعريشة الياسمين بالصيف بترد الروح.
examples.trans: Sitting under the jasmine trellis in summer refreshes the soul.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بتعرف, بيتعرف).

examples.text: هادي كانت خطتي قبل ما أتعرف عليكم.
examples.trans: That was my plan before I got to know you all.
We met kind neighbours in the quarter.

meanings.note: Feminine noun from علّق ('to hang'): a wall peg, hook, or hanging tag.

examples.text: المفتاح معلق على أول تعليقة جنب الباب.
examples.trans: The key is hanging on the first hook beside the door.
Put the apron on the hook once you finish.

meanings.note: The word 'تعليمات' (تعليمات) means 'تعليمات'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: اقرأي تعليمات الخبز بصوت عالي عشان أنسخهم بشكل نظيف يا سلمى.
examples.trans: Read the baking instructions aloud so I can copy them cleanly, Salma.
This is تعليمات.

meanings.note: Form V passive/intransitive counterpart to علّق ('to hang something up').

examples.trans: The lantern will hang above the door.
The sign was hung in the hall.

meanings.note: Form V reflexive of علّم ('to teach').

examples.text: نور بتتعلم شغل الاستقبال بسرعة كبيرة.
examples.trans: Nour is learning the front-desk work very quickly.
I learned to play the piano when I was young.

meanings.note: Verbal noun of عيّن ('to appoint, hire to a post').

examples.text: فرحنا كتير بخبر تعيين نور بالنزل.
examples.trans: We were delighted at the news of Nour's permanent appointment at the inn.
The manager signed the appointment letter in the morning.

meanings.note: Form V defective verb from غداء ('lunch'). Past uses -ee- before consonant endings (تغديت).

examples.trans: We are going to have lunch in the garden under the tree.
Did you have lunch or are you still waiting for Tariq?

meanings.note: Form II verbal noun of غلّف ('to wrap/package'). ورق تغليف means 'wrapping paper'.

examples.text: فكينا ورق التغليف البني عن اللوحة.
examples.trans: We removed the brown wrapping paper from the painting.
Good wrapping keeps cake fresh.

meanings.note: The word 'تغيروا' (تغيروا) means 'تغيروا'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: عم يكتب بحروف كبيرة... عشرة من عشرة، لا تغيروا ولا إشي!
examples.trans: He is writing in capital letters... TEN OUT OF TEN, DO NOT CHANGE A THING!
This is تغيروا.

meanings.note: Form V intransitive counterpart to غيّر ('to change something').

examples.trans: The appointment changed a moment ago.
The weather changes quickly in spring.

meanings.note: Expresses being caught off guard (بدل ما أتفاجأ هيك 'instead of being surprised like this').

examples.trans: I was surprised when I saw you here.
Don't be surprised by the news.

meanings.note: Collective تفاح ('apples'), singulative تفاحة ('an apple').

examples.trans: I bought red apples from the shop.
Apple jam is delicious at breakfast.

meanings.note: Action of opening a door, book, or shop.

examples.trans: Can you open the window a little bit?

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على تفتح.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with تفتح.

meanings.note: Action of a group of people opening something.

examples.trans: Do not open the door for a stranger.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على تفتحوا.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with تفتحوا.

meanings.note: Verbal noun of فتّش ('to inspect, check officially').

examples.text: لجنة التفتيش من البلدية جاية يوم الأربعا.
examples.trans: The inspection team from City Hall is coming on Wednesday.
The whole kitchen is clean and ready for inspection.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بتفرج, بيتفرج).

examples.trans: Nobody gawks at the guests here!

examples.text: كنت ناوي تتفرج من الشارع المقابل؟
examples.trans: Were you planning to watch from across the street?

meanings.note: The word 'تفضلوا' (تفضلوا) means 'تفضلوا'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: تفضلوا، هادا كتاب أعشاب الحديقة المغلف بقماش من رف مكتبة الكتب المستعملة بـ شارع الياسمين!
examples.trans: Here is the cloth-bound garden herb book from the second-hand bookshop shelf on Jasmine Street!
This is تفضلوا.

meanings.note: Used as a polite offering, invitation to enter, or handing something to a female.

examples.trans: Here you go, the coffee is ready.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على تفضلي.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with تفضلي.

تفضّل.gloss: to please come in / sit / go ahead / here you are

meanings.en: to please come in / sit / go ahead / here you are
meanings.note: Essential Jordanian hospitality verb used mostly in the imperative: تفضل (to a man), تفضلي (to a woman), تفضلوا (plural).

examples.trans: Please have a seat, ma'am!
Here you go, hot mint tea.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بتفقد, بيتفقد).

examples.text: أنا بس بتفقد الطقس من الشباك!
examples.trans: I am just checking the weather from the window!
Tariq checked on the heater in the morning.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: Quick thinking solved the problem.
That is smart, logical thinking.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: Add the green mint right before serving.
The presentation is neat and lovely.

meanings.note: Form V verb; passive/reflexive of قدّم ('serve food/drink').

examples.text: الشوربة السخنة بتتقدم مع خبز محمص.
examples.trans: The hot soup is served with toasted bread.

examples.text: قهوة الصبح بتتقدم بالساحة الساعة تمانية.
examples.trans: Morning coffee is served in the courtyard at eight.

meanings.note: The word 'تقريبا' (taqreeban) means 'almost'. It is a common adv in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: صارت الضهر تقريبا! خلينا نسأل مازن إذا وصل أي طرود.
examples.trans: It is almost noon! Let us ask Mazen if any packages arrived.
This is تقريبا.

meanings.note: Everyday masculine noun for a written or official report (تقرير التراث 'the heritage report'). Plural: تقارير.

examples.text: تقرير البلدية مدح ساحتنا يوم الأربعا.
examples.trans: The city report praised our courtyard on Wednesday.

examples.text: كتبت تقرير مختصر عن حالة المبنى.
examples.trans: I wrote a brief report on the condition of the building.

meanings.note: Verbal noun of قسم; تقسيم الغرف refers to the school-trip room assignments.

examples.trans: I didn't like the group assignments.
The room assignment list is ready.

meanings.note: Form II verbal noun of قطّع (to chop into pieces); لوح تقطيع is a cutting board.

examples.trans: We used the word تقطيع.
This is another تقطيع.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: تقيلة, plural: تقال).

examples.trans: This suitcase is very heavy today.
Take off your heavy coat and sit down to rest.

meanings.note: Used to describe a heavy object or a burdensome person.

examples.trans: This bag is very heavy for me.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على تقيلة.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with تقيلة.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: تقييمات.

examples.trans: The guests wrote an excellent review.
We read all the reviews on the page.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian Form II verb from تقيل ('heavy'), matching Classical ثقّل.

examples.trans: Do not weigh the basket down with items.
Water weighs cloth down a lot.

meanings.note: The number 3 when followed by a counted noun.

examples.trans: I have three cars in the garage.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على تلات.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with تلات.

meanings.note: The standalone form of the number 3.

examples.trans: Count to ten: one, two, three.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على تلاتة.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with تلاتة.

meanings.note: The number 30.

examples.trans: His age is now thirty years.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على تلاتين.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with تلاتين.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: تلاجات.

examples.trans: The cold milk is inside the fridge.
Open the fridge and check the butter.

meanings.note: Small hill (plural تلال tilaal); familiar across hilly Amman.

examples.text: عمان مبنية على تلال حلوة بتطل عالسما.
examples.trans: Amman is built across lovely hills looking out at the sky.

examples.text: لما نقسم الشغل الكبير لتلال صغيرة بصير سهل.
examples.trans: When we break a big job into small hills, it becomes easy.

meanings.note: Fraction denoting one out of three parts.

examples.trans: I ate a third of the pizza by myself.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على تلت.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with تلت.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: تلوج.

examples.trans: The water is cold as ice.
Snow fell on the hills of Amman.

meanings.note: The word 'تلحقي' (تلحقي) means 'تلحقي'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: ول يا نور! عم تلحقي حرامي، ولا حدا أكل فليفلة حارة نية بالغلط؟
examples.trans: Whoa, Nour! Are you chasing a thief, or did someone accidentally eat a raw hot pepper?
This is تلحقي.

تلخبط.gloss: to get mixed up; get confused

meanings.en: to get mixed up; get confused
meanings.note: Colloquial quadriliteral reflexive verb meaning to become jumbled, tangled, or confused.

examples.text: تلخبطت الأوراق لما فات الهوا من الشباك.
examples.trans: The papers got mixed up when the wind came through the window.

examples.text: ما تتلخبط بالأرقام، اكتبها وحدة وحدة.
examples.trans: Don't get confused with the numbers—write them down one by one.

meanings.note: The word 'تلطيخة' (تلطيخة) means 'تلطيخة'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: خليني أشوف من نظاراتي: ادهني الكيكة الدافية بمعلقتين من... تلطيخة زرقا!
examples.trans: Let me look through my glasses: Brush warm cake with two spoons of... blue smudge!
This is تلطيخة.

meanings.note: Spoken contraction of على التلفون ('on the telephone').

examples.trans: We used the word تلفون.
This is another تلفون.

meanings.note: Form II verbal noun of لمّع ('to polish wood, brass, or shoes').

examples.text: بقي بس تلميع دواسات النحاس بقماشة ناعمة.
examples.trans: All that's left is polishing the brass pedals with a soft cloth.

examples.text: بعد التلميع رجع خشب الجوز يلمع زي المراية.
examples.trans: After polishing, the walnut wood shone like a mirror again.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: تليفونات.

examples.trans: The phone rang on the reception desk.
I wrote the phone number in the notebook.

meanings.note: Everyday Levantine word for mouth, or the pouring spout of a pitcher/teapot.

examples.trans: The pitcher's spout is a little wide.
He laughed wholeheartedly.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian all-purpose word for 'all set, fine, spot-on!'.

examples.trans: Everything has to be spot-on!
Alright, I can remember the sentences.

meanings.note: Used to emphasize absolute completion or exactness.

examples.trans: I agree with you completely.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على تماما.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with تماما.

meanings.note: Adverbial form of تمام meaning 'precisely' or 'completely'.

examples.trans: We used the word تماماً.
This is another تماماً.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian numeral 'eight'; short form تمن (taman) before a plural noun (تمن غرف 'eight rooms').

examples.text: عندنا تمن غرف وتمن مفاتيح نحاس.
examples.trans: We have eight rooms and eight brass keys.
He arrives at eight in the evening.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian numeral 'eighty'.

examples.text: خشب بلوط أصلي عمره تمانين سنة.
examples.trans: Solid oak wood eighty years old.
This house has lived through eighty winters!

meanings.en: to sway back and forth gently
meanings.note: Form VI verb from مال ('to lean / tilt'), expressing gentle rhythmic swaying.

examples.trans: The branches sway with the breeze.
The lanterns are swaying calmly.

meanings.note: Form V verb taking على for practicing music or a craft.

examples.trans: Can I practice the whole song on the piano?

examples.text: مدام سعاد تمرنت ساعة كاملة قبل شاي المساء.
examples.trans: Madam Suad practiced for a full hour before evening tea.

meanings.note: Verbal noun of مرّن ('to train / practice'). Plural: تمارين.

examples.trans: We have piano rehearsal at four o'clock.
This exercise is easy and useful.

meanings.note: The word 'تمشي' (تمشي) means 'تمشي'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: صينية رقم تنين عليها كريمة ليمون حامضة. السكينة عم تمشي فيها بسلاسة.
examples.trans: Tin Two has a sharp lemon icing. The knife glides through nicely.
This is تمشي.

meanings.note: The word 'تمك' (تمك) means 'تمك'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: حلو كتير! ماشي يا مدير، نظف تمك بشاي أسود وجرب صينية رقم تنين!
examples.trans: Too sweet! Okay, Boss, wash your palate with black tea and try Tin Two!
This is تمك.

meanings.note: Followed directly by a subjunctive verb without أن in spoken Arabic (بتتمنى تكون 'wishes to be').

examples.trans: I hope we'll be in the same class.
Every girl wishes to succeed.

meanings.note: The word 'تمنية' (tmanye) means 'eight'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: شوفوا سطر المرسل عاليسار—هادا من رسام الخرايط تبع غرفة تمنية!
examples.trans: Look at the sender line on the left—it is from our Room Eight mapmaker!
This is تمنية.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بتمنى, بيتمنى).

examples.trans: We hope every guest feels comfortable with us.
We wished them a happy trip.

meanings.note: Formal administrative verb تمّ used with verbal nouns like الموافقة to mean 'approved!'.

examples.trans: We used the word تمّ.
This is another تمّ.

meanings.en: harmony; moving or sounding in unison
meanings.note: Built from نغمة ('musical note / tone'). Used for music, colours, or coordinated motion.

examples.trans: The lanterns move in lovely harmony.
There is clear harmony in the playing.

meanings.note: Form II verbal noun from نبّه ('to alert/warn'). Used for announcements, reminders, and warning signs.

examples.text: شكرا عالتنبيه، لحقنا نرتب كل شي.
examples.trans: Thanks for the notice—we managed to sort everything out.

examples.text: حطوا ورقة تنبيه على باب المطبخ.
examples.trans: They put a reminder notice on the kitchen door.

meanings.note: The word 'تنحط' (تنحط) means 'تنحط'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: وهلق يا مازن؟ احكيلنا بصراحة—هل هالكيكة بتستاهل تنحط على طاولة الذكرى يوم السبت؟
examples.trans: Well, Mazen? Tell us honestly—is that worthy of our Saturday anniversary table?
This is تنحط.

meanings.note: Form V verb from نفس ('breath').

examples.text: فتحت الشباك عشان أتنفس هوا نضيف.
examples.trans: I opened the window to breathe fresh air.

examples.text: بعد ما رتبنا القائمة، قدرت أتنفس براحة.
examples.trans: Once we organized the list, I could breathe easily.

meanings.note: The number 2.

examples.trans: I only want two pieces, two are enough.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على تنين.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with تنين.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: توائم.

examples.trans: The two suitcases are just like twins.
His twin brother lives next to him.

meanings.note: The word 'توازن' (توازن) means 'توازن'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: صينية رقم تنين رح تاخد كريمة ليمون حامضة عشان توازن التوت الحلو المستوي، صح؟
examples.trans: Tin Two gets a tart lemon icing to balance the sweet ripe berries, yes?
This is توازن.

meanings.note: Collective masculine noun for berries/mulberries (singulative توتة 'one berry').

examples.trans: The berry and almond cake turned out delicious!
We have an old mulberry tree in the neighbourhood.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بتوتر, بيتوتر).

examples.trans: When I get nervous, my sentences turn long!

examples.text: لا تتوتر، كل شي رح يمشي تمام.
examples.trans: Do not get nervous, everything will go fine.

meanings.note: Loanword from English, for toasted sliced bread.

examples.trans: Do you want toast with the cheese?
The toast burned a little.

meanings.note: Verbal noun of وصّل ('to deliver, drop off; connect wires'); سيارة توصيل means 'delivery van'.

examples.trans: The delivery van pulled up in front of the gate.

examples.text: التوصيل للبيت مجاني إذا طلبنا دزينة.
examples.trans: Home delivery is free if we order a dozen.

meanings.note: Verbal noun from و-ف-ق; بالتوفيق! is the everyday Arabic way to say 'good luck!'.

examples.trans: Good luck in your new job, Nour!
Wish us luck before the municipality visit.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بتوفى, بيتوفى).

examples.trans: My grandfather passed away three years ago.

examples.text: ترك ذكرى طيبة بعد ما توفى.
examples.trans: He left warm memories after passing away.

meanings.note: The word 'توقعات' (توقعات) means 'توقعات'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: استنى—شيكت توقعات الجو للويكند تبعت عصر الجمعة والسبت يا مازن؟
examples.trans: Wait—have you checked the weekend weather forecast for Friday and Saturday afternoon, Mazen?
This is توقعات.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: تواقيع.

examples.text: الورقة ما عليها اسم ولا توقيع.
examples.trans: The paper has neither name nor signature.
The postman asked for my signature.

meanings.note: Common Levantine Arabic verb meaning 'to expect', with feminine ending -i.

examples.trans: We used the word توقّع.
This is another توقّع.

meanings.note: Affectionate Levantine family word for 'grandmother' (often used directly without a possessive suffix).

examples.text: وصفة شوربة العدس هاي تعلمتها من تيتا.
examples.trans: I learned this lentil soup recipe from my grandma.

examples.text: تيتا دايما بتحط قشر ليمون طازة مع الكيك.
examples.trans: Grandma always puts fresh lemon zest into her cakes.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: ثابتة, plural: ثابتين).

examples.trans: Hold the torch steady on the pipe.
The flame's color is steady blue.

meanings.note: A unit of time or the feminine ordinal for second.

examples.trans: Wait for me just one second.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على ثانية.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with ثانية.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بثبت, بيثبت).

examples.trans: Hold still a moment and listen to that sound!

examples.text: الكرسي ثبت بعد ما شدينا البرغي.
examples.trans: The chair held firm once we tightened the screw.

ثبّت.gloss: to fasten; seat firmly; fix in place

meanings.en: to fasten; seat firmly; fix in place
meanings.note: Form II verb meaning 'seat securely / hold steady'.

examples.text: طارق ثبت اللوحة النحاس ببراغي صغار.
examples.trans: Tariq fastened the brass plate with small screws.

examples.text: امسك السلم من تحت وثبته منيح.
examples.trans: Hold the ladder at the bottom and steady it well.

meanings.note: Refers to a large amount of money or resources.

examples.trans: He amassed a large wealth from his work.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على ثروة.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with ثروة.

meanings.note: Used for heavy weight or metaphorically for a dull person.

examples.text: هذا الصندوق ثقيل ما بقدر أرفعه.
examples.trans: This box is heavy, I can't lift it.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على ثقيل.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with ثقيل.

meanings.note: The standard or rural/Bedouin pronunciation of the number 3.

examples.trans: I have three children.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على ثلاثة.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with ثلاثة.

meanings.note: The number 30 with the "th" sound preserved.

examples.trans: He paid thirty dinars for the ticket.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على ثلاثين.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with ثلاثين.

meanings.note: The number 8.

examples.trans: The time became eight in the evening.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على ثمانية.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with ثمانية.

meanings.note: The word 'ثمنطعش' (thamanTa3sh) means 'eighteen'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: خمسة، عشرة، خمسطعش... ثمنطعش، تسعطعش، وعشرين خطوة عالرصيف بالزبط!
examples.trans: Five, ten, fifteen... eighteen, nineteen, and twenty paces right to the kerb!
This is ثمنطعش.

meanings.note: From ثنائي (two-part/duo), used in music for duets.

examples.trans: We used the word ثنائي.
This is another ثنائي.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بجيب, بيجيب).

examples.text: رح أجيب شراشف نظيفة من الخزانة.
examples.trans: I will bring clean sheets from the closet.

examples.text: أي علبة زبدة جبتي يا نور؟
examples.trans: Which tub of butter did you bring, Nour?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: جيران.

examples.trans: All the neighbours on the street are kind.
Good morning, dear neighbour.

meanings.note: Describes dry air, dry ingredients, or seasoned dry timber.

examples.text: خلينا نخلي كل المكونات الجافة عالرف العالي.
examples.trans: Let's keep all the dry ingredients on the upper shelf.

examples.text: المفصل بعد ما تدهنه زيت ما بيعود جاف.
examples.trans: Once you oil the hinge, it won't be dry anymore.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: جاكيتات.

examples.trans: The key is in the right jacket pocket.

examples.text: البس جاكيت دافي قبل ما تطلع.
examples.trans: Put on a warm jacket before you go out.

meanings.note: Feminine plural جامدات also appears in Jordanian speech for firm fruit (متل ليمونات جامدات).

examples.text: نقي ليمونات صفر وجامدات عشان تارت الليمون.
examples.trans: Pick firm yellow lemons for the lemon tarts.

examples.text: الكريمة بردت بالبراد وصارت جامدة ومتماسكة.
examples.trans: The curd chilled in the fridge and turned firm and set.

meanings.note: Feminine noun from جمع ('to gather'), standard throughout the Arab world for university.

examples.trans: My sister studies engineering at the University of Jordan.

examples.text: الطلاب راجعين من الجامعة الساعة تلاتة.
examples.trans: The students are coming back from university at three.

meanings.note: Relative adjective (nisba) from جانب ('side'), e.g. الباب الجانبي ('the side door'), القفل الجانبي ('the side latch').

examples.text: افتح الشباك الجانبي عشان يفوت الهوا.
examples.trans: Open the side window so fresh air comes in.

examples.text: في ممر جانبي صغير ورا المطبخ.
examples.trans: There is a small side passage behind the kitchen.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: جاهزة, plural: جاهزين).

examples.trans: The desk is clean and the keys are ready.
Breakfast is ready in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Active participle of إجا ('to come'): means 'on the way / arriving' (جايين 'they are coming') and after a time noun 'next' (الأسبوع الجاي 'next week').

examples.trans: The guests are coming down the stairs now.
We will see you next week!

meanings.note: Active participle of جاب (to bring); Jordanian Arabic prefers participles for ongoing or resultant states.

examples.trans: We used the word جايب.
This is another جايب.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: جبانة, plural: جبناء).

examples.trans: It was a cowardly plan of mine.
Do not be timid, speak honestly.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb meaning to bring something. Can also mean 'you (m) brought'.

examples.trans: I brought a gift with me for you.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على جبت.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with جبت.

meanings.note: Means 'mountain' and also names Amman's historic hilltop quarters (جبل اللويبدة, جبل عمان).

examples.text: الهوا على راس الجبل دايما نضيف ومنعش.
examples.trans: The air on top of the mountain is always clean and crisp.

examples.text: بيت الياسمين قريب من درج الجبل القديم.
examples.trans: Jasmine Courtyard House is near the old Jabal stairway.

meanings.note: Nisba adjective from جبل ('mountain'); عسل جبلي ('mountain honey') is dark, aromatic wildflower honey.

examples.text: العسل الجبلي لونه غامق وطعمه غني.
examples.trans: Mountain honey has a dark colour and a rich taste.
The mountain air in Amman cools down at night.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: أجبان.

examples.trans: White cheese is tasty with mint.
We bought cheese and olives for breakfast.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أجبنة.

examples.trans: Your glasses are pushed up on your forehead!
He wiped the rain off his forehead.

meanings.note: Extremely common Jordanian expression to express surprise or ask for confirmation, like 'really?' or 'seriously!'.

examples.trans: Are you talking seriously?

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على جد.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with جد.

meanings.note: The word 'جداتنا' (جداتنا) means 'جداتنا'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: جداتنا كانوا يدهنوا عسل على معجنات المكسرات من قبل ما يكون في إشي اسمه سكر فانيليا!
examples.trans: Our grandmothers brushed honey over nut pastries long before vanilla sugar existed!
This is جداتنا.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: جداول.

examples.trans: I read the bus timetable at the station.
The week's schedule is neat and clear.

meanings.note: The word 'جدي' (جدي) means 'جدي'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: وهادا القاضي مازن لابس نظارات القراءة تبعونه، ومبين جدي كتير الصراحة.
examples.trans: And here is Judge Mazen with his reading glasses on, looking very serious indeed.
This is جدي.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: جديدة, plural: جداد).

examples.trans: I am Nour, the new receptionist.
I installed a new lightbulb last week.

meanings.note: The word 'جذع' (جذع) means 'جذع'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: وشوفوا جذع شجرة الظل تبعت ساحتنا—في حلقة بتشبهها معلقة عالي!
examples.trans: And look at the trunk of our courtyard shade tree—a matching ring high up!
This is جذع.

meanings.note: The word 'جرب' (jarrab) means 'he tried'. It is a common verb in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: طولتوا—المدير جرب اختصاره المشهور بالزقاق اللي مارق من المطبخ؟
examples.trans: You took your time—did the boss try his famous alley shortcut past the kitchen?
This is جرب.

meanings.note: Imperative form of 'try' addressed to a single female.

examples.trans: Try this food, it's very delicious.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على جربي.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with جربي.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أجراس.

examples.trans: The gate bell rang twice.
Listen to the sound of the bell in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: جريئة, plural: جريئين).

examples.text: الأخ الكبير كان جريء وصوته عالي.
examples.trans: The older brother was bold and loud-voiced.
A bold and excellent idea!

meanings.note: Everyday word for a newspaper; broken plural in spoken Levantine is جرايد (jaraayid).

examples.text: عمي بيقرا الجريدة مع فنجان قهوة كل صبح.
examples.trans: My uncle reads the newspaper with a cup of coffee every morning.

examples.text: لف البياع الصحون بورق جرايد قديم.
examples.trans: The seller wrapped the plates in old newspaper.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بجرب, بيجرب).

examples.trans: This sweater is clean and new — try it on.
We tried the new recipe and it turned out delicious.

meanings.note: Standard word used in Jordanian Arabic for a part, portion, or section of something.

examples.trans: This is part of the problem.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على جزء.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with جزء.

meanings.note: The word 'جزدانك' (جزدانك) means 'جزدانك'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: خدي جزدانك يا نور! الدكانة اللي عالزاوية جنب برج الساعة بتبيع عسل بلدي!
examples.trans: Grab your purse, Nour! The corner shop next to the clock tower sells local honey!
This is جزدانك.

meanings.note: Collective noun جزر ('carrots') with singulative جزرة ('one carrot').

examples.text: فرمنا الجزر والبصل لمكعبات صغيرة ومتساوية.
examples.trans: We diced the carrots and onions into small, even cubes.

examples.text: الجزر المشوي بيعطي الشوربة حلاوة طبيعية.
