meanings.en: to whistle (of a person or the wind)
meanings.note: Form II verb (بصفّر / صفّر) used for human whistling or wind whistling through wires and alleys.

examples.trans: The wind is whistling between the ropes.

examples.text: طارق صفّر لما شاف الفانوس طار لفوق.
examples.trans: Tariq whistled when he saw the lantern fly upward.

meanings.note: Clap your hands, or clap for a performer at the end.

examples.trans: People clapped a lot after the song.
Clap twice and the lamp lights up.

meanings.note: Can mean solid, hard, or refer to steel (when used as a noun).

examples.trans: This metal is very solid.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على صلب.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with صلب.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بصلح, بيصلح).

examples.trans: I fix pipes and chairs.
Yesterday you fixed the old heater.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: صمامات.

examples.trans: We fitted a new brass valve on the boiler.
Make sure the valve is tightly shut.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بصمم, بيصمم).

examples.trans: Do you design concert and music halls?
He designed a quiet courtyard in the city centre.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: صناديق.

examples.trans: The screwdriver is inside the toolbox.
We moved four boxes out of the hallway.

meanings.note: Woodworker's word for sanding timber smooth; ورق صنفرة is sandpaper.

examples.text: خلصنا صنفرة الدرفات الأربعة قبل المغرب.
examples.trans: We finished sanding all four shutter panels before sunset.

examples.text: اشتريت ورق صنفرة ناعم للخشب القديم.
examples.trans: I bought fine-grit sandpaper for the old wood.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أصوات.

examples.trans: I heard the sound of rain on the window.
His voice is calm and polite on the phone.

meanings.note: Noun 'sawt' (voice) with a feminine possessive pronoun.

examples.trans: Her voice is beautiful when she sings.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على صوتها.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with صوتها.

meanings.note: Nisba adjective from صوت ('voice, sound'); رسالة صوتية means 'voice message'.

examples.trans: I left you a short voice message on the phone.
The acoustic insulation in the sunroom is excellent.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: صوتيات.

examples.trans: He works as an architectural acoustics engineer.
The acoustics of the old hall are excellent.

meanings.note: Any picture or photograph; صورة أبيض وأسود is a black-and-white photo.

examples.trans: I took a nice photo of you in the courtyard.
I have old photos of my grandmother.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أصواف.

examples.trans: This wool sweater is warm and soft.
A wool blanket is cosy in winter.

meanings.note: Arabic/French solfège name for the note G (دو، ري، مي، فا، صول، لا، سي).

examples.text: كورد صول الكبير طلع صافي ودافي بالغرفة.
examples.trans: The G major chord rang out clear and warm in the room.

examples.text: نغمة صول صارت متوازنة تماما مع باقي الأوتار.
examples.trans: The G note is now balanced perfectly with the other strings.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: The item is safe and sound with us.
The letter arrived safe and sound.

meanings.note: Plural of sayyad, context depends on whether it's near water.

examples.trans: The fishermen returned with a net full of fish.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على صيادين.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with صيادين.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun.

examples.trans: Regular maintenance protects the building.
We called the maintenance technician in the morning.

meanings.note: Masculine noun (feminine صيدلانية, plural صيادلة) from صيدلية ('pharmacy').

examples.text: زياد صيدلي شاطر وكل الحارة بتعرفه.
examples.trans: Ziad is a skilled pharmacist and the whole neighbourhood knows him.
I asked the pharmacist about medicine for a cold.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: صيدليات.

examples.trans: The green pharmacy is beside the overpass.
I walked past the pharmacy this morning.

meanings.note: The season of summer.

examples.trans: Summer in Jordan is usually hot.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على صيف.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with صيف.

meanings.note: Used as an adjective for things related to summer, or as a noun for summer clothing.

examples.trans: We need to buy summer clothes.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على صيفي.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with صيفي.

meanings.note: Broken plural صواني ('serving trays' or 'oven baking pans').

examples.text: جهزنا تلات صواني خبز عشان تدخل الفرن الفجر.
examples.trans: We prepped three trays of bread to go into the oven at dawn.

examples.text: نور حملت صينية الشاي بالنعنع للساحة.
examples.trans: Nour carried the mint tea tray out to the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بضيع, بيضيع).

examples.text: فكرت القطار ضاع لما بعنا البيت!
examples.trans: I thought the train got lost when we sold the house!
You will not get lost; the road is straight.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بضايق, بيضايق).

examples.trans: Do the extra stairs not bother you?
Sorry if we bothered you with the noise.

meanings.note: Active participle of ضل ('to remain'); standard Jordanian for 'there is ... left'.

examples.trans: He has two valves left on the shelf.
How much time is left until noon?

meanings.note: Everyday Levantine verb for packing things up; تضبي لسانك literally tells someone to pack their tongue away.

examples.trans: I packed my books into my bag.
Pack your things before we leave.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بضبط, بيضبط).

examples.trans: Set the alarm for six, Tariq.
The plan worked out one hundred percent!

meanings.note: Classic Jordanian Arabic verb ضبّ meaning 'to pack up', 'tidy away', or 'put into boxes'.

examples.trans: We used the word ضبّ.
This is another ضبّ.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun.

examples.trans: Outside on the main street there is noise.
Thick stone blocks traffic noise.

meanings.note: Everyday Form I verb (بضحك / ضحك) meaning 'to laugh' or 'grin playfully'.

examples.text: ليش عم بتضحك لجيبة الجاكيت تبعتك؟
examples.trans: Why are you grinning at your coat pocket?

examples.text: ضحكنا كلنا لما شفنا النظارة على جبينه.
examples.trans: We all laughed when we saw the glasses on his forehead.

meanings.en: huge; massive; large in scale or volume
meanings.note: Feminine ضخمة, plural ضخام. Used for big shapes, large crowds, or oversized objects.

examples.trans: They hung a huge lantern in the middle of the courtyard.

examples.text: موج البحر بالصورة كان ضخم كتير.
examples.trans: The sea wave in the picture was very massive.

meanings.note: Preposition meaning 'against' or 'resistant to / -proof' (ضد المي 'waterproof', ضد الهوا 'windproof').

examples.trans: We sealed the recipe in waterproof plastic.

examples.text: مشابك الغسيل الخشب ضد الهوا القوي.
examples.trans: The wooden clothespins are proof against strong wind.

ضرب.gloss: to hit; strike; (of a fuse) blow

meanings.en: to hit; strike; (of a fuse) blow
meanings.note: Basic meaning 'to hit'. In everyday Jordanian a fuse or a machine 'hits' when it blows or fails (الفيوز ضرب 'the fuse blew').

examples.trans: The ball hit the window.

examples.text: الفيوز ضرب لما شغلنا الفرن والغسالة مع بعض.
examples.trans: The fuse blew when we ran the oven and the washing machine together.

meanings.note: Instance noun of ضرب; ضربات الفرشاية means 'brushstrokes'.

examples.text: خلي ضربات الفرشاية طويلة وباتجاه عرق الخشب.
examples.trans: Keep the brushstrokes long and in the direction of the wood grain.

examples.text: سمعنا تلات ضربات خفيفة عالباب الخارجي.
examples.trans: We heard three light knocks on the outer door.

meanings.note: Spoken plural of ضريبة (tax).

examples.trans: We used the word ضريبة.
This is another ضريبة.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أضعاف.

examples.trans: Today we baked double the usual amount.
The courtyard holds twice this number.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: ضغوط.

examples.trans: The pressure valve on the boiler works.
Calm tea eases blood pressure.

meanings.note: Very common Levantine verb meaning to stay, remain, or keep doing something.

examples.trans: He stayed at home and didn't go out.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على ضل.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with ضل.

meanings.note: The word 'ضلك' (ضلك) means 'ضلك'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: ضلك اخبزي هيك يا سلمى، ونص عمان رح يصفوا طابور برا بوابتنا.
examples.trans: Keep baking like this, Salma, and half of Amman will line up outside our gate.
This is ضلك.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian verb ضلّ (to keep/stay), used before another verb to mean 'keep on doing'.

examples.trans: We used the word ضلّ.
This is another ضلّ.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian spelling/pronunciation (duhur) for midday (12:00 p.m.).

examples.text: الكافيه بيقدم شوربة سخنة من الضهر للمسا.
examples.trans: The café serves hot soup from noon until evening.

examples.text: الشمس بتكون عالية ودافية وقت الضهر.
examples.trans: The sun is high and warm at noon.

meanings.note: Colloquial pronunciation of the word for light.

examples.trans: Turn off the light before you sleep.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على ضو.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with ضو.

ضوّى.gloss: to light up; shine; switch on a light

meanings.en: to light up; shine; switch on a light
meanings.note: Used for a lamp that glows and for the person who switches it on (ضوي الضو 'turn on the light').

examples.trans: The new lamp gives good light.
Turn the light on, the room is dark.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun.

examples.trans: You have a real gift for hospitality!
Warm hospitality opens hearts.

meanings.note: The word 'ضيع' (nDayye3) means 'we miss/lose'. It is a common verb in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: اقرأي كرت الدليل الأول بصوت عالي يا نور، عشان ما نضيع ولا كلمة.
examples.trans: Read Clue Card One aloud, Nour, so we do not miss a single word.
This is ضيع.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: ضيوف.

examples.trans: The guests are coming down to breakfast now.
We welcomed every guest with a smile.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: ضيقة, plural: ضيقين).

examples.trans: The attic stairs are a bit narrow.
Do not enter the narrow alley.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بضيع, بيضيع).

examples.text: الورق لسه بيشتغل لما بتنقطع الكهربا.
examples.trans: Paper still works when the power goes out.
Mazen always misplaces his glasses!

meanings.note: Form II verb disambiguated with shadda from adjective ضيق ('narrow').

examples.text: الخط كبير وواضح، ما حدا رح يضيق عيونه.
examples.trans: The lettering is big and clear—nobody will squint their eyes.

examples.text: مازن ضيق عيونه وهو يقرأ الرقم من آخر الساحة.
examples.trans: Mazen squinted as he read the number from across the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: طوابق.

examples.trans: Your room is on the second floor on the right.
The building has three storeys.

meanings.note: The word 'طابور' (طابور) means 'طابور'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: ضلك اخبزي هيك يا سلمى، ونص عمان رح يصفوا طابور برا بوابتنا.
examples.trans: Keep baking like this, Salma, and half of Amman will line up outside our gate.
This is طابور.

meanings.en: to fly; soar; blow away in the wind
meanings.note: Hollow verb (بطير / طار). Used both for birds/aircraft flying and light objects blowing away in a gust.

examples.trans: The sheet of paper flew away with the gust of wind.
The birds flew off from the top of the tree.

meanings.note: Male given name of the veteran handyman.

examples.trans: We used the word طارق.
This is another طارق.

meanings.note: Used for fresh food, produce, or bread.

examples.trans: The bread today is fresh.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على طازة.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with طازة.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: طازجة, plural: طازجين).

examples.trans: Morning bread is fresh and hot!
Fresh orange juice and fresh cake.

meanings.note: The word 'طاغي' (طاغي) means 'طاغي'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: ممم. كيكة إسفنجية منيحة كتير، بس سكر الفانيليا طاغي على أساس اللوز الخفيف.
examples.trans: Mmm. A very decent sponge cake, but vanilla sugar overpowers the subtle almond base.
This is طاغي.

meanings.note: Everyday Levantine noun طاقية for a hat or cap.

examples.trans: We used the word طاقية.
This is another طاقية.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian hollow verb (بطال / بنطال) meaning 'reach a high shelf or latch'.

examples.text: ما بقدر أطال الرف الفوقاني بدون سلم.
examples.trans: I can't reach the top shelf without a ladder.

examples.text: بعدنا الغصن وهلا بنطال الشنكل بسهولة.
examples.trans: We moved the branch aside and now we can reach the hook easily.

meanings.note: Masculine noun (feminine طالبة, broken plural طلاب), from طلب ('to seek knowledge').

examples.text: الطالب الجديد سأل عن قاعة المحاضرات.
examples.trans: The new student asked about the lecture hall.
The students are reviewing their lessons in the library.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: طالعة, plural: طالعين).

examples.trans: Count on me, I am heading right out!
We are going up to the third floor.

meanings.note: Common everyday word for table.

examples.trans: Put the things on the table.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على طاولة.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with طاولة.

meanings.note: Collective masculine noun for blackboard/signboard chalk (single stick: حبة طباشير).

examples.text: كتب البياع الأسعار بالطباشير الأبيض عاللوحة.
examples.trans: The vendor wrote the prices in white chalk on the board.

examples.text: امسحي لوحة الطباشير واكتبي قائمة اليوم.
examples.trans: Wipe the chalkboard and write today's menu.

meanings.note: Expressive quadriliteral verb (بطبطب / طبطب) meaning 'to pat' a pocket, shoulder, or back.

examples.text: طبطب على جيبة الجاكيت عشان يطمّن.
examples.trans: He patted his coat pocket to reassure himself.
She patted her brother's shoulder with a smile.

meanings.note: Warm, reassuring 'of course! / naturally!'.

examples.trans: Of course, Tariq, your secret is safe with us!
Of course I came when I got your card.

meanings.note: Warm or emphatic 'of course', used seriously or playfully between friends.

examples.trans: Of course I'll help you.
Of course I know the answer.

meanings.note: The word 'طبقات' (طبقات) means 'طبقات'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: لا تخاف يا مدير؛ احنا بنعرف أساس الكيكة، عشان هيك مطبخي رح يختبر تلات طبقات تلميع!
examples.trans: Do not panic, boss; we know the cake base, so my kitchen will test three glazes!
This is طبقات.

meanings.note: Used for a coat of paint (طبقة دهان), a layer of pastry, or a building storey.

examples.text: الطبقة الأولى نشفت وصارت جاهزة للطبقة التانية.
examples.trans: The first coat has dried and is ready for the second coat.

examples.text: دهان المي بيكفيه طبقتين رقيقتين عشان يطلع ناعم.
examples.trans: Water-based paint only needs two thin coats to come out smooth.

meanings.note: Everyday Levantine household word for a low wooden step-stool or small low table.

examples.text: طلعت عالطبلية الصغيرة عشان أوصل الرف العالي.
examples.trans: I stepped onto the low stool to reach the top shelf.

examples.text: حط الطبلية بالزاوية بعيد عن الممر.
examples.trans: Tuck the low stool into the corner out of the walkway.

meanings.note: In تصرفي بطبيعتك, means 'act like your normal self / act naturally'.

examples.trans: Just be yourself.
Nature is lovely in spring.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: طبيعية, plural: طبيعيين).

examples.trans: Great service is a natural thing at our inn.
Natural juice without sugar.

meanings.note: The word 'طرد' (Truud) means 'packages'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: صارت الضهر تقريبا! خلينا نسأل مازن إذا وصل أي طرود.
examples.trans: It is almost noon! Let us ask Mazen if any packages arrived.
This is طرد.

meanings.en: splash! splat! (sound of liquid hitting a surface)
meanings.note: Expressive onomatopoeic interjection imitating water splashing or paint splattering.

examples.trans: Splash! The water spilled onto the apron.

examples.text: سمعنا صوت طرش لما الحبر انكب عالورق.
examples.trans: We heard a splash sound when the ink spilled onto the paper.

meanings.note: The word 'طرطش' (yTarTshoo) means 'they splash'. It is a common verb in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: شوفوا قدام—عصفورين عم يطرطشوا على حفة نافورة الحجر!
examples.trans: Look ahead—two sparrows are splashing on the rim of the stone fountain!
This is طرطش.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أطراف.

examples.trans: Pull the edge of the sheet tight.

examples.text: حط الكاسة بعيد عن طرف الطاولة.
examples.trans: Set the glass away from the edge of the table.

meanings.note: Everyday food adjective for soft, tender bread or fresh dough.

examples.trans: We used the word طري.
This is another طري.

meanings.note: Feminine adjective used for food (like meat) or soft materials.

examples.trans: The meat is tender and delicious.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على طرية.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with طرية.

meanings.note: Used in عالطريق ('on the way') and طول الطريق ('all the way').

examples.trans: The hot tea is on the way right now!
I repeated the sentence all along the way.

meanings.note: Used for a method of doing something, or sometimes a physical path.

examples.text: كل واحد إله طريقة في الشغل.
examples.trans: Everyone has their own way of working.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على طريقة.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with طريقة.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: طعوم.

examples.trans: The exact same delicious taste!
The fresh lemon flavour stands out in the cake.

meanings.note: A light or fire goes out (الضو طفى 'the light went out'); with a person as subject, to switch something off.

examples.trans: The power went out for a whole hour.
Switch off the light before you sleep.

meanings.note: Sound word for a sharp noise: a click, a pop or a crack.

examples.trans: I heard a pop from the kitchen.
Crack! The glass broke.

meanings.note: Instance noun (اسم مرة) from onomatopoeic طق ('pop, click').

examples.text: سمعنا طقة خفيفة لما فتح القفل النحاس.
examples.trans: We heard a soft click when the brass lock opened.

examples.text: اشتغلت اللمبة بهدوء بدون ولا طقة.
examples.trans: The lamp came on quietly without a single pop.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: The weather in Amman is mild in spring.
I looked out the window to check the weather.

meanings.en: to peek; to look out; to drop by briefly
meanings.note: Geminate verb (بطل / طليت) from root ط-ل-ل meaning to peer out or pop in.

examples.trans: The drawings peek out from the edge of the envelope.

examples.text: طل علينا شوي قبل ما تسافر.
examples.trans: Drop by to see us briefly before you travel.

meanings.note: Masculine noun used for sugar glaze on pastries as well as paint or enamel on surfaces.

examples.text: طلاء السكر بيعطي لمعان حلو للمعجنات.
examples.trans: The sugar glaze gives a nice shine to the pastries.
We painted the door with a fresh white coat.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بطلب, بيطلب).

examples.trans: The postman just asked for my signature.

examples.text: طلبت منه يقابلك هون يوم الجمعة؟
examples.trans: Did you ask him to meet you here on Friday?

meanings.note: Past tense verb with a third-person plural object pronoun.

examples.trans: The items I ordered have arrived.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على طلبتهم.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with طلبتهم.

meanings.note: Noun 'talabiyya' (an order/request) with a first-person possessive pronoun.

examples.trans: When will my order arrive?

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على طلبيتي.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with طلبيتي.

طلع.gloss: to go up; go out; come out; turn out

meanings.en: to go up; go out; come out; turn out
meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بطلع, بيطلع).

examples.text: لفائف القرفة هلا طلعت من الفرن!
examples.trans: The cinnamon rolls just came out of the oven!
Go up the stairs to the third floor.

meanings.note: To paint a wall, door or shutter with a brush; the paint itself is دهان.

examples.trans: We painted the door blue last year.
We want to paint the children's room yellow.

meanings.note: Form II طلّع means both 'look!' (طلّع بالمراية) and 'bring/carry up' (رح أطلّع الشنتة).

examples.text: طلع بالمراية ورا المكتب يا معلم!
examples.trans: Look in the mirror behind the desk, boss!
I will carry the blue suitcase up for you.

طمّن.gloss: to reassure; tell how things went

meanings.en: to reassure; tell how things went
meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بطمن, بيطمن).

examples.trans: Tell me, how did the room go?
He put our minds at ease with a kind word.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian number 12; gains the -ر ending when directly preceding a counted noun.

examples.trans: We used the word طناعش.
This is another طناعش.

meanings.note: Standard Levantine kitchen noun for a cooking pot or saucepan.

examples.trans: We used the word طنجرة.
This is another طنجرة.

meanings.note: The word 'طنين' (طنين) means 'طنين'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: طنين طنين بيوم أحد هادي—هاد الرنين المزدوج أكيد غرفة أربعة.
examples.trans: Buzz-buzz on a quiet Sunday—that double ring is definitely Room Four.
This is طنين.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: طوارئ.

examples.trans: We have a small emergency in the kitchen!
The emergency key hangs beside the door.

meanings.note: Used for giving directions (straight ahead) or referring to time (immediately).

examples.trans: Walk straight ahead then turn right.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على طوالي.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with طوالي.

meanings.note: Collective noun for bricks or building blocks; حيط طوب is a brick wall.

examples.trans: The house is built of brick and stone.
They brought new bricks for the wall.

meanings.note: Plural of ṭūba, referring to building bricks.

examples.trans: They brought bricks to build the wall.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على طوبات.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with طوبات.

meanings.note: Can refer to physical length, height, or duration of time (e.g., all day).

examples.trans: He stayed asleep all day long.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على طول.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with طول.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بطوي, بيطوي).

examples.trans: Fold this sheet and put it in your pocket.
She folded the clean towels in the closet.

meanings.note: Used to describe a tall person or a long object.

examples.trans: This street is very long.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على طويل.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with طويل.

طوّل.gloss: to take long; be patient (طول بالك take it easy)

meanings.en: to be patient (طول بالك take it easy)
meanings.note: طوّل بالك ('lengthen your patience' = take it easy, hold on!) is a classic Levantine expression.

examples.text: طول بالك يا أستاذ، اقرأ الصفحة التانية!
examples.trans: Hold on, sir, read the second page!
I did not take long at the market; I came right back.

meanings.note: Describes kind-hearted people (ناس طيبين) and pleasant smells/tastes (ريحة طيبة); standalone طيب means 'alright / well then'.

examples.trans: You are very kind people.
The coffee smells wonderful in the morning!

meanings.note: The word 'طية' (el-Tayye) means 'the flap'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: افتحي الطية بلطف يا نور؛ هالمغلف الصغير استنى بصبر من شهر خمسة.
examples.trans: Open the flap gently, Nour; that little envelope has waited patiently since May.
This is طية.

meanings.note: The word 'طير' (Tyoor) means 'birds'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: الكرت الأول بقول: عشرين خطوة للشرق وين المي الباردة الصافية بتستقبل طيور الصبح.
examples.trans: Card One says: Twenty paces east where cool clear water greets the morning birds.
This is طير.

meanings.note: Verbal noun (masdar) of طار ('to fly'). Used for the sensation of flying as well as airlines.

examples.trans: The best thing about an aeroplane is the moment of flying.

examples.text: القمر كأنه في رحلة طيران بين الغيوم.
examples.trans: The moon looks as if it's on a flight through the clouds.

meanings.note: Material noun naming potter's clay (طين الفخار) as well as wet earth after rain.

examples.text: فناجين الطين السميك بتخلي الشاي سخن.
examples.trans: Thick clay cups keep the tea hot.

examples.text: ريحة الطين بعد المطر بتنعش الحارة كلها.
examples.trans: The scent of earth after rain refreshes the whole neighbourhood.

طيّر.gloss: to blow away; make fly; knock off

meanings.en: to make fly; blow away; send flying
meanings.note: Form II causative of طار ('to fly'): الهوا طيّر الورقة ('the wind blew the paper away').

examples.text: هبة الهوا طيّرت الورق عن الطاولة.
examples.trans: The gust of wind blew the papers off the table.

examples.text: الولد عم بيطيّر طيارته الورق عالسطح.
examples.trans: The boy is flying his paper kite on the roof.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بطل, بيطل).

examples.text: مازن بيطل من ورا الستارة كل دقيقة!
examples.trans: Mazen peeks from behind the curtain every minute!
The window overlooks the courtyard and the tree.

meanings.note: Masculine noun for shade under trees or an awning (تحت الظل 'in the shade'). Plural: ظلال.

examples.trans: We watched the sun behind the shade.
Sit in the shade, the weather is hot today.

meanings.note: Central theme word of the show: يتحمل الظلم ('endure unfairness') and ظلمهم ('their mistreatment').

examples.trans: Injustice is hard for a person to bear.
We won't accept unfairness.

meanings.note: Geminate verb; أظن / بظن means 'I think / I reckon'.

examples.text: أظن رح يضل عنا دهان كفاية للوحة البوابة.
examples.trans: I think we'll have enough paint left over for the gate sign.

examples.text: ظنيت إن السكر بالمرتبان الكبير مش الصغير.
examples.trans: I thought the sugar was in the big jar, not the small one.

meanings.note: Pronounced duhur in everyday Jordanian: الظهر means 'at noon / midday'.

examples.trans: He will arrive Friday at noon.
The sun is high at midday.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: عائلية, plural: عائليين).

examples.trans: I came to the neighbourhood for an old family reason.
This is a quiet family hotel.

meanings.note: Active participle from عجل ('to hurry'): used for urgent dispatches, news, and calls.

examples.text: وصلنا خبر عاجل من مكتب المحطة.
examples.trans: Urgent news reached us from the station office.
There is an urgent call from the manager.

meanings.note: Nisba adjective from عاج ('ivory'), describing warm cream tones on paper or cloth.

examples.trans: Every envelope has ivory paper.
I chose a cream shirt for the party.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بعيد, بيعيد).

examples.trans: I will repeat the words the whole way!
Could you repeat the number, please?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: عادات.

examples.trans: Usually we open the gate at seven.
Drinking morning coffee is a nice habit.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: عادية, plural: عاديين).

examples.trans: Bread with jam needs regular unsalted butter.
A quiet, ordinary day in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Names the horizontal rung of a chair/table or the upper crossbar of a frame.

examples.text: سندت رجلي عالعارضة التحتانية تبع الكرسي.
examples.trans: I rested my foot on the lower rung of the chair.

examples.text: علقنا الفانوس بوسط العارضة الخشب فوق القوس.
examples.trans: We hung the lantern from the middle of the wooden beam over the arch.

meanings.note: Arabic very often uses the active participle عارف ('knowing') for the present 'I know'.

examples.trans: We used the word عارف.
This is another عارف.

meanings.note: Active participle of عزف ('to play an instrument'), used as a noun for someone playing music.

examples.trans: Finally we found a piano player!
The musician started playing the oud.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بعيش, بيعيش).

examples.trans: This house has lived through eighty winters!
They lived in our quarter for many years.

meanings.note: Strong wind-and-rain storm.

examples.text: دخلنا كل إشي جوا قبل ما تبلش العاصفة.
examples.trans: We brought everything indoors before the storm hit.

examples.text: هديت العاصفة الصبح وطلعت الشمس عالحجار.
examples.trans: The storm calmed in the morning and sunlight hit the stones.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: عواطف.

examples.trans: Good maintenance has nothing sentimental about it!
He spoke with his brother with genuine warmth.

meanings.note: Classic Jordanian/Levantine opposite of منيح or حلو in الخبر الحلو والخبر العاطل ('the good news and the bad news').

examples.text: احكيلي الخبر الحلو قبل الخبر العاطل!
examples.trans: Tell me the good news before the bad news!

examples.text: الجو مش عاطل أبدا لتمشاية الصبح.
examples.trans: The weather is not bad at all for a morning walk.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: عاقلة, plural: عاقلين).

examples.text: ما في حدا عاقل بيرفض خبز سخن!
examples.trans: No sensible person turns down hot bread!
Sensible, measured words.

meanings.note: The word 'عالأرض' (عالأرض) means 'عالأرض'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: اقلبوا الصفحات شوي شوي فوق نشافة المكتب عشان ما يوقع إشي ناشف عالأرض.
examples.trans: Turn the pages gently over the desk blotter so nothing dry slips onto the floor.
This is عالأرض.

meanings.note: The word 'عالاخر' (عالاخر) means 'عالاخر'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: تركتها من غير طبقة تلميع بالمرة! مرطبان العسل بالمونة كان فاضي عالاخر!
examples.trans: I left it completely unglazed! The honey jar in the pantry was totally empty!
This is عالاخر.

meanings.note: The word 'عالبلكونة' (عالبلكونة) means 'عالبلكونة'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: لعد يوم الجمعة الصبح بنطلع عالبلكونة بحبل متين وبنختبر كل عقدة!
examples.trans: Then Friday morning we climb onto that balcony with sturdy cord and test every knot!
This is عالبلكونة.

meanings.note: The word 'عالدرج' (عالدرج) means 'عالدرج'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: عالموعد بالزبط! شوفوا مين نازلة عالدرج مع كتاب أخضر!
examples.trans: Right on cue! Look who is coming down the stairs with a green book!
This is عالدرج.

meanings.note: The word 'عالزاوية' (عالزاوية) means 'عالزاوية'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: خدي جزدانك يا نور! الدكانة اللي عالزاوية جنب برج الساعة بتبيع عسل بلدي!
examples.trans: Grab your purse, Nour! The corner shop next to the clock tower sells local honey!
This is عالزاوية.

meanings.note: The word 'عالسطر' (عالسطر) means 'عالسطر'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: روعة! هادا مبين بسيط كتير—ليش رمشتي عينيكي عالسطر التحتاني يا سلمى؟
examples.trans: Wonderful! That sounds simple enough—why did you squint at the bottom line, Salma?
This is عالسطر.

meanings.note: The word 'عالطبقة' (عالطبقة) means 'عالطبقة'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: لأنه في قطرة مطر كبيرة خبطت الحبر الأزرق بالزبط عالطبقة الدافية السرية!
examples.trans: Because one big raindrop hit the blue ink right on the secret warm glaze!
This is عالطبقة.

meanings.note: The word 'عالغلاف' (عالغلاف) means 'عالغلاف'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: شوفوا ورقة الذهب المطبوعة عالغلاف الأخضر الباهت: أعشاب وزهور الساحة.
examples.trans: Look at the gold leaf stamped on the faded green cover: Courtyard Herbs and Blossoms.
This is عالغلاف.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: عالقة, plural: عالقين).

examples.text: فتحتي بابنا العالق من أول يوم!
examples.trans: You opened our sticking door on day one!
The key was stuck in the lock.

meanings.note: Preposition 'ala' + definite article + 'kamil' (complete).

examples.trans: The car veered off the road completely.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على عالكامل.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with عالكامل.

meanings.note: The word 'عالموعد' (عالموعد) means 'عالموعد'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: عالموعد بالزبط! شوفوا مين نازلة عالدرج مع كتاب أخضر!
examples.trans: Right on cue! Look who is coming down the stairs with a green book!
This is عالموعد.

meanings.note: The word 'عالوجه' (عالوجه) means 'عالوجه'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: شوفوا آخر كلمة مش ملطخة عالزاوية: رشي شرائح لوز محمصة عالوجه.
examples.trans: Look at the last unsmudged word at the corner: scatter toasted sliced almonds on top.
This is عالوجه.

meanings.note: Can mean physically high or loud (for a voice or sound).

examples.trans: The music volume is very high.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على عالي.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with عالي.

meanings.note: The word 'عالية' (عالية) means 'عالية'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: فوانيس عالية من السطح للشجرة بتضوي على التمنية وعشرين كرسي ليلة السبت!
examples.trans: High rooftop-to-tree lanterns shining down over all twenty-eight seats on Saturday night!
This is عالية.

meanings.note: The word 'عاليسار' (عاليسار) means 'عاليسار'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: صفوهم بانتظام على طاولة القهوة يا زياد—صينية رقم واحد عاليسار، وتنين بالنص.
examples.trans: Line them up neatly on the coffee table, Ziad—Tin One on the left, Two in the middle.
This is عاليسار.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: عامة, plural: عامين).

examples.text: عالشارع العام برا في ضجة سيارات.
examples.trans: Out on the main road there is traffic noise.
A public park near the quarter.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: عمال.

examples.trans: The movers carried out the furniture in the morning.
Every worker in the bakery knows his job.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بعبر, بيعبر).

examples.trans: Cross the overpass to downtown.
We crossed the street at the light.

meanings.note: Feminine عبقرية, plural عباقرة. Also used as a noun ('a genius').

examples.text: والله إنك فنان عبقري يا مازن!
examples.trans: Honestly you're a brilliant artist, Mazen!

examples.text: فكرة تعليق الفوانيس بالحبل كانت عبقرية.
examples.trans: The idea of hanging the lanterns with rope was brilliant.

meanings.note: Form II Jordanian verb for filling buckets, cups, or rooms with light.

examples.trans: We filled the two buckets with warm soapy water.
Morning sunlight fills the room with brightness.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: عتبات.

examples.trans: We found the suitcase on the doorstep.
We swept the stone threshold in the morning.

meanings.note: Everyday Levantine noun for darkness (related to معتم 'dark, unlit').

examples.text: شغل الفانوس عشان ما نمشي بالعتمة.
examples.trans: Turn on the lantern so we do not walk in the dark.

examples.text: راحت العتمة أول ما ضوت لمبة السقف.
examples.trans: The darkness vanished as soon as the ceiling lamp lit up.

meanings.note: Appreciative Levantine adjective for fine aged wood, stonework, or heritage objects.

examples.text: خشب الجوز العتيق بالبيانو صوته دافي وأصيل.
examples.trans: The vintage walnut wood in the piano has a warm, resonant tone.

examples.text: الباب العتيق رجع جديد بعد الصنفرة والدهان.
examples.trans: The old heritage door looked new again after sanding and painting.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: عجلات.

examples.trans: Turn the blue valve wheel slowly.

examples.text: القطار الصغير إله أربع عجلات خشب.
examples.trans: The little train has four wooden wheels.

meanings.note: Core bakery verb for kneading bread or pastry dough.

examples.text: طارق بيعجن عجينة التارت بإيدين ثابتة.
examples.trans: Tariq kneads the tart dough with steady hands.

examples.text: سلمى عجنت العجين بكير عشان يرتاح قبل الفجر.
examples.trans: Salma kneaded the dough early so it could rest before dawn.

meanings.note: Everyday baking noun for dough or batter, from عجن (to knead).

examples.trans: We used the word عجين.
This is another عجين.

meanings.note: Used for baking dough.

examples.trans: We need to let the dough rest.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على عجينة.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with عجينة.

meanings.note: Geminate verb (بعد / عدّيت) from root ع-د-د. Takes -ey- before consonant-initial past suffixes.

examples.trans: I can count them quickly.
I counted the envelopes twice.

meanings.note: The word 'عدا' (3ada) means 'except'. It is a common prep in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: ولا إشي! فاضية تماما ما عدا خط أزرق خفيف.
examples.trans: Nothing! It is completely blank except for a faint blue line.
This is عدا.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: عدد.

examples.trans: The screwdriver and wrench are in the toolbox.
He brought the tools to fix the boiler.

meanings.note: Collective noun; شوربة عدس ('golden lentil soup' with lemon and olive oil) is a beloved Jordanian staple.

examples.text: شوربة العدس مع عصرة ليمون أطيب غدا بالشتا.
examples.trans: Lentil soup with a squeeze of lemon is the best lunch on a rainy day.

examples.text: سلمى غسلت العدس الأصفر وحطته عالنار.
examples.trans: Salma rinsed the yellow lentils and set them on the stove.

meanings.note: Optical lens of eyeglasses or a camera (named after its lentil shape, عدس).

examples.text: مسحت العدسة اليسار من نظارتي بقماشة نضيفة.
examples.trans: I wiped the left lens of my glasses with a clean cloth.

examples.text: نقطة صغيرة عالعدسة بتخلي القراءة صعبة.
examples.trans: A tiny speck on the lens makes reading difficult.

meanings.note: Past tense verb for third person plural.

examples.trans: The boys counted the money.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على عدوا.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with عدوا.

meanings.note: Imperative feminine singular form for 'count'. Can also be the male name Oday (ʿUday), but verb is more common here.

examples.trans: Count from one to ten.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على عدي.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with عدي.

meanings.note: Plural command form from عدّ ('to count') with the 'them' ending.

examples.trans: We used the word عدّ.
This is another عدّ.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: عروض.

examples.trans: He measured the width of the courtyard.
The ring is twenty millimetres wide.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بعرف, بيعرف).

examples.trans: I recognized your neat handwriting in two seconds!
Do you know anyone here in Amman?

meanings.note: Slender climbing stem or root of jasmine, mint, or ivy ('iriq, pl. 'ruuq).

examples.text: حطيت عرق نعنع أخضر بكاسة الشاي السخن.
examples.trans: I put a sprig of fresh green mint into the glass of hot tea.

examples.text: عرق اللبلاب طلع عالحيط الحجر لحد الشباك.
examples.trans: The ivy vine climbed up the stone wall right to the window.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: عريضة, plural: عراض).

examples.trans: The wide desk under the window is comfortable.
There are wide wooden beams in the ceiling.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: Piano playing calms the nerves.
Whenever she finishes playing, she smiles.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb عزم means 'to invite' someone to an event, meal, or coffee.

examples.trans: We used the word عزم.
This is another عزم.

meanings.note: Plural of عزيز ('dear'), standard in Arabic letters and postcards.

examples.trans: We used the word عزيز.
This is another عزيز.

meanings.note: The word 'عزيزتي' (عزيزتي) means 'عزيزتي'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: شمي الورقة بالزبط محل ما كان الكرت محطوط لتلاتين سنة يا عزيزتي.
examples.trans: Smell the paper right where the card rested for thirty years, my dear.
This is عزيزتي.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: Here is mint tea with honey.
Mountain honey tastes wonderful.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: We booked a table for dinner tomorrow evening.
Dinner is ready at eight o'clock.

meanings.note: Extremely common colloquial conjunction used to indicate reason or purpose.

examples.trans: I went to the doctor because I am sick.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على عشان.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with عشان.

عشاني.gloss: for my sake / because of me

meanings.en: for my sake / because of me
meanings.note: Conjunction 'ashan' with a first-person pronoun suffix.

examples.trans: Do this thing for my sake.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على عشاني.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with عشاني.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أعشاب.

examples.trans: We sprinkled green herbs on top of the eggs.
Tariq grows fresh herbs in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Number ten, typically used before masculine plural nouns in classical, though usage varies colloquially.

examples.trans: I have ten dinars.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على عشر.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with عشر.

meanings.note: The standalone number ten.

examples.trans: The time is ten o'clock right now.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على عشرة.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with عشرة.

meanings.note: The number twenty.

examples.trans: He is twenty years old.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على عشرين.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with عشرين.

meanings.note: Mariam uses عصابة to describe how Layan's clique intimidates the whole school.

examples.trans: They act like a gang.
We aren't afraid of their gang.

meanings.note: Form II intransitive Levantine verb ('assab): قبل ما تعصب ('before she gets mad').

examples.trans: Ms. Abeer gets angry quickly.
Don't get upset, it's simple.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: عصور.

examples.trans: We arrived at the guesthouse Monday afternoon.
Late-afternoon tea in the courtyard is a daily ritual.

meanings.note: Cozy Levantine word for the pleasant late-afternoon tea/coffee hours.

examples.text: قعدة العصرية بالساحة مع الشاي ما بتتعوض.
examples.trans: Sitting in the courtyard in the late afternoon with tea is unbeatable.

examples.text: خبز محمص وشوربة دافية بعصرية ماطرة إشي رائع.
examples.trans: Crusty bread and warm soup on a rainy afternoon are wonderful.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: عصافير.

examples.trans: We hear the birds in the tree.
We set out water for the birds in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: عصاير.

examples.trans: Fresh orange juice is cold and tasty.
I poured two glasses of juice for breakfast.

meanings.note: Used literally or humorously (الزيت أول والعضلات تاني 'oil first, muscle second').

examples.text: فتح الشباك القديم بده نقطة زيت مش عضلات!
examples.trans: Opening the old window takes a drop of oil, not brute muscle!

examples.text: تعبوا عضلات إيدي من حمل السطول عالدرج.
examples.trans: My arm muscles got tired from carrying buckets up the stairs.

meanings.note: Any time off work or school; in Jordan the weekly break is Friday and Saturday.

examples.trans: Next holiday we are going to Aqaba.
Tomorrow is a day off, there is no work.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: عظيمة, plural: عظيمين).

examples.text: شوربة سخنة بالمطر؟ هاد شي عظيم!
examples.trans: Hot soup in the rain? That is splendid!
A great idea, everyone.

meanings.note: Jordanian everyday word for furniture and all your belongings when you move house.

examples.trans: We moved the furniture in a big truck.
The living-room furniture is old but comfortable.

meanings.note: Used both to get someone's attention politely ('excuse me') and to reply to شكرا ('you're welcome').

examples.trans: Excuse me, is the door locked?
Excuse me, Mr. Rami, sorry for the bother.

meanings.note: Polite Arabic expression used both for 'excuse me' to get attention and 'you're welcome'.

examples.trans: We used the word عفواً.
This is another عفواً.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: عقارات.

examples.trans: The letter came from the property department.
Property prices downtown are high.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: عقود.

examples.trans: The lease contract is protected by law.
He works at the municipal contracts office.

meanings.en: knot tied in rope or string
meanings.note: Feminine noun (plural عقد) from عقد ('to tie'). Used for literal rope knots and figurative complications.

examples.text: ربطت الحبل بعقدة مزدوجة عشان يثبت.
examples.trans: I tied the rope with a double knot so it stays firm.

examples.text: فكّينا العقدة بسهولة قبل ما الهوا يشد.
examples.trans: We untied the knot easily before the wind picked up.

meanings.note: Masculine noun (also feminine عكازة) used for a hiker's walking stick or a crutch.

examples.trans: My grandfather walks with an old wooden walking stick.
A hiking stick helps on the steep climb.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: علامات.

examples.trans: He got a score of ten out of ten.
There is a small mark on the wood.

meanings.note: Can refer to a cardboard box, a tin can, or a small container.

examples.trans: Open the can of tuna.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على علبة.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with علبة.

علطول.gloss: right away; straight; all the time

meanings.en: right away; straight; all the time
meanings.note: Contracted spoken spelling of على طول ('immediately / straight ahead / always').

examples.text: جيبي كيس تلج علطول وحطيه عالكاحل.
examples.trans: Grab an ice pack right away and put it on the ankle.

examples.text: امشي علطول لآخر الممر بتلاقي غرفة الشمس.
examples.trans: Walk straight down to the end of the hall and you'll find the sunroom.

meanings.note: Form I intransitive verb ('iliq / byi'laq) meaning 'get stuck or jammed'; contrast transitive علّق ('hang up / jam').

examples.text: المفتاح القديم علق بالقفل من الصدا.
examples.trans: The old key got stuck in the lock from rust.
The sheet of paper got wedged behind the wooden rest.

meanings.note: Contrasts with سفلي / تحتاني ('lower'): الشباك العلوي = 'the upper transom window'.

examples.text: الشباك العلوي فوق الباب مسكر ومحكم عالأخر.
examples.trans: The upper transom window above the door is shut snug and tight.
We lined up the clean glasses on the upper shelf.

meanings.note: Standard preposition for 'on', 'upon', or 'to'.

examples.trans: The book is on the table.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على على.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with على.

meanings.note: Intransitive verb ('ili / byi'la) describing a melody, voice, or price rising.

examples.text: بنص الأغنية، اللحن بيعلى شوي شوي.
examples.trans: In the middle of the song, the melody climbs bit by bit.
The sound of rain on the window grew louder at night.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: علالي.

examples.trans: The attic room on the third floor is sunny.
We brought the boxes down from the attic.

meanings.note: Preposition 'ala' with a third-person feminine pronoun suffix.

examples.trans: There is dust on it (the table).

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على عليها.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with عليها.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بعلق, بيعلق).

examples.trans: Where should I hang this round mirror?
We hung the lanterns in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بعلم, بيعلم).

examples.text: علمت بيانو ببيت قريب من هون.
examples.trans: I taught piano in a house near here.
I climbed these stairs to teach music.

meanings.note: Levantine progressive marker placed before a present-tense verb to show action happening right now.

examples.trans: The water is flowing inside the pipe right now!

examples.text: كنت عم بدور على دفتري هلا.
examples.trans: I was just looking for my notebook.

meanings.note: The word 'عمان' (عمان) means 'عمان'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: واصل على عمان السبت الجاي لذكرى شهر خمسة التلاتين بـ بيت الياسمين!
examples.trans: Arriving in Amman next Saturday for the thirtieth May anniversary at Jasmine Courtyard!
This is عمان.

meanings.note: Arabic distinguishes father's sister (عمة, feminine of عمّ) from mother's sister (خالة).

examples.text: عمتي كانت تعزف عالبيانو كل يوم جمعة.
examples.trans: My paternal aunt used to play the piano every Friday.

examples.text: هاد الدفتر الأخضر هدية من عمتي.
examples.trans: This green notebook is a gift from my aunt.

meanings.note: Aunt on the father's side.

examples.trans: My paternal aunt is going to visit us today.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على عمتي.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with عمتي.

meanings.note: Arabic expresses age with عمر + possessive suffix: عمره تمانين سنة ('its/his age is eighty years').

examples.trans: The building is eighty years old.
He has lived in this quarter all his life.

meanings.note: Can literally mean 'your age', but is often used idiomatically as 'have you ever'.

examples.trans: Have you ever traveled to Egypt?

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على عمرك.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with عمرك.

meanings.note: Idiomatically used for 'he has ever' or 'in his life'.

examples.trans: He has never lied to me in his life.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على عمره.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with عمره.

meanings.note: Idiomatically used for 'she has ever' or 'in her life'.

examples.trans: She has never seen snow in her life.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على عمرها.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with عمرها.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بعمل, بيعمل).

examples.text: اليوم رح نعمل بيض عالطريقة الفرنسية!
examples.trans: Today we will make French-style eggs!
What do we do now with the rain coming down?

meanings.note: Nisba adjective from عمل ('work/action'); describes someone focused on practical details.

examples.trans: Mazen is more practical than that.
This is a practical and quick solution.

meanings.note: Means both a stone/wooden architectural pillar and a vertical column in a ledger or timetable.

examples.text: قرا مازن العمود التاني بالدفتر بدون نظارة.
examples.trans: Mazen read the second column in the notebook without glasses.

examples.text: علقنا الفانوس جنب عمود الحجر بالساحة.
examples.trans: We hung the lantern beside the stone pillar in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: عميقة, plural: عميقين).

examples.trans: Take a deep breath and calm down.
The old well is very deep.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: عمام.

examples.trans: I visited my uncle's house on Friday.
My cousin helped me move the things.

meanings.note: Means 'about' (عن الزبدة), 'off / away from' (عن جبيني), and appears in عن جد ('really!') and عن إذنك ('excuse me').

examples.trans: I will carry the suitcase up for you.
I heard your voices about the butter!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: Three years of stubbornness was too long.
Stubbornness solves no problems.

meanings.note: Extremely common expression for 'really?' or 'seriously'.

examples.trans: Are you speaking seriously or joking?

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على عنجد.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with عنجد.

meanings.note: A very common preposition used to indicate location, possession, or presence.

examples.trans: The car is at the door.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على عند.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with عند.

meanings.note: The word 'عندك' (عندك) means 'عندك'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: مسا الخير يا رامي! بدي مرطبان من أحسن عسل ذهبي عندك، أسرع من البرق!
examples.trans: Good afternoon, Rami! I need a jar of your best golden honey, faster than lightning!
This is عندك.

meanings.note: The word 'عندنا' (عندنا) means 'عندنا'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: واو، قاسي! هلق ما ضل عندنا غير صينية رقم تلاتة اللي عليها طبقة العسل الدافي!
examples.trans: Wow, brutal! Now we only have Tin Three with the warm honey glaze left!
This is عندنا.

meanings.note: Common way to say 'I have' in Arabic, literally 'at me'.

examples.trans: I have a new car.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على عندي.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with عندي.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: عناوين.

examples.text: خد رقم النزل وعنواننا لو سمحت.
examples.trans: Take the guesthouse number and our address, please.
The address is written clearly on the card.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: عنيدة, plural: عنيدين).

examples.text: أخوي الكبير عنيد بس قلبه طيب.
examples.trans: My older brother is stubborn, yet kind-hearted.
Two stubborn brothers finally made peace.

meanings.note: Verbal noun from عاد ('to return'), used in phrases like حمد لله عالعودة or بعودتك.

examples.text: فرحنا كتير بعودتك بالسلامة يا طارق.
examples.trans: We were very happy at your safe return, Tariq.

examples.text: تذكرة الذهاب والعودة أوفر من المفرد.
examples.trans: A round-trip ticket is cheaper than a single.

meanings.note: Standalone عيب means 'it is rude / improper' (عيب نتفرج it is rude to snoop).

examples.text: عيب نفتح دفتر ضيف بدون إذنه.
examples.trans: It is rude to open a guest's notebook without permission.

examples.text: الخشب الأصلي ما فيه ولا عيب.
examples.trans: The solid wood has not a single flaw.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: عيل.

examples.trans: The whole family gathers on Friday.
My family lived near here.

meanings.note: A common way to say 'my family', referring to the immediate or extended family unit.

examples.trans: My family lives in Amman.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على عيلتي.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with عيلتي.

meanings.note: Feminine noun; also used in the delighted Jordanian exclamation يا عيني! ('oh my! / how lovely!').

examples.trans: Close your eyes and smell the coffee!
Oh my, look at that warm light in the courtyard!

meanings.note: The word 'عينيكي' (عينيكي) means 'عينيكي'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: روعة! هادا مبين بسيط كتير—ليش رمشتي عينيكي عالسطر التحتاني يا سلمى؟
examples.trans: Wonderful! That sounds simple enough—why did you squint at the bottom line, Salma?
This is عينيكي.

meanings.note: The word 'عيونك' (عيونك) means 'عيونك'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: غمضي عيونك وتنفسي: نعناع الحديقة، وبرش برتقال حلو، وعسل ذهبي!
examples.trans: Close your eyes and breathe in: garden mint, sweet orange zest, and golden honey!
This is عيونك.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بعين, بيعين).

examples.text: إذا ما عينتها، رح أعينها بمطبخي!
examples.trans: If you do not hire her, I will hire her in my kitchen!
They hired a new reception manager.

meanings.note: Verbal noun (masdar) vocalized to distinguish it from verb عجن ('to knead').

examples.text: طارق بلش بعجن الطحين والزبدة الباردة للتارت.
examples.trans: Tariq started kneading the flour and cold butter for the tarts.

examples.text: العجن الهادئ بيخلي قشرة التارت هشة ومقرمشة.
examples.trans: Gentle kneading keeps the tart crust tender and flaky.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بعزف, بيعزف).

examples.trans: I am still waiting for you to play the scale!

examples.text: الكبير كان يعزف بيانو كل جمعة.
examples.trans: The older boy used to play piano every Friday.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بعقد, بيعقد).

examples.trans: Why did you knit your eyebrows like that?
They concluded the agreement at the lawyer's office.

meanings.note: Vocalized with kasra to highlight 'grain of wood / vein in stone or leaf'.

examples.text: امشي بالفرشاية مع عرق الخشب مش عكسه.
examples.trans: Move the brush along the wood grain, not against it.

examples.text: خشب الجوز العتيق عروقه غامقة وحلوة كتير.
examples.trans: Vintage walnut wood has dark, beautiful grain lines.

meanings.note: Used in أخضر غابة / أخضر متل الغابة ('forest green') as well as pine/oak woods like Ajloun.

examples.text: اخترنا للشيش لون أخضر غامق متل الغابة.
examples.trans: We chose a deep forest-green colour for the shutters.

examples.text: غابات عجلون بتضل خضرا وحلوة طول السنة.
examples.trans: The forests of Ajloun stay green and lovely all year round.

meanings.note: In Jordanian homes and kitchens, الغاز routinely means 'the kitchen stove / range'.

examples.text: حطيت طنجرة الشوربة عالغاز على نار هادية.
examples.trans: I set the soup pot on the stove over a gentle flame.

examples.text: طفي الغاز لما يصفر المؤقت بعد عشر دقايق.
examples.trans: Turn off the stove when the timer rings in ten minutes.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: غازية, plural: —).

examples.trans: Cold sparkling water lifts stains right out.
Would you like still or sparkling water?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: غالية, plural: غاليين).

examples.trans: The wooden train is old and precious.
Welcome, my dear boys!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: غامضة, plural: غامضين).

examples.trans: Why did you leave a mysterious note on the door?
We finally found out who the mysterious guest is.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: غامقة, plural: غامقين).

examples.trans: The suitcase's color is dark blue.
A dark grey wool coat.

meanings.note: Colloquial Levantine noun describing hazy vision, mist, or blurred ink.

examples.text: الدنيا الصبح كانت كلها غباش من الضباب.
examples.trans: Everything this morning was blurry with fog.

examples.text: لو في غباش بالعدسة، امسحها بمنديل ناعم.
examples.trans: If there is haze on the lens, wipe it with a soft cloth.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun.

examples.trans: Wipe the dust off the brass plate.
The shelves are clean with no dust on them.

meanings.note: The main meal of the day in Jordan, usually eaten in the early afternoon.

examples.trans: What's for lunch today?
We have lunch together after work.

meanings.note: Everyday carpenter's word (ghira) for wood or craft glue.

examples.text: نقطة غرا خشب ناشف بتثبت اللباد بمكانه.
examples.trans: A dab of dry wood glue holds the felt right in place.

examples.text: سكر علبة الغرا منيح عشان ما تنشف.
examples.trans: Close the glue bottle tightly so it doesn't dry out.

meanings.note: Can mean a unit of mass (gram) or deep love/infatuation depending on context.

examples.trans: I want a hundred grams of cheese.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على غرام.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with غرام.

meanings.note: The word 'غرب' (lal-gharb) means 'to west'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: هادا مستحيل! لفينا للشمال، بعدين للغرب، بعدين...
examples.trans: This is impossible! We turned north, then west, then...
This is غرب.

meanings.note: The word 'غربي' (el-gharbi) means 'western'. It is a common adj in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: هون بالزبط تحت المصب! ورقة حجر بتأشر للشمال الغربي طالعة التلة الخفيفة!
examples.trans: Right here under the spout! A stone leaf pointing northwest up the gentle hill!
This is غربي.

meanings.note: Masculine noun whose plural أغراض ('things, belongings, groceries') is one of the commonest words in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Put your things in the cupboard beside the door.
I have a quick errand in the market and I'll be back.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for a room in a house or building.

examples.trans: The bedroom is very spacious.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على غرفة.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with غرفة.

meanings.note: Masculine verbal noun (from غرب 'to set/go west'). Commonly paired with وقت ('time') or قبل ('before'): قبل الغروب.

examples.trans: We need to finish a few minutes before sunset.

examples.text: السما بتصير وردية وقت الغروب بعمان.
examples.trans: The sky turns pink at sunset in Amman.

meanings.note: As an adjective غريب / غريبة means 'strange, odd'; as a noun (plural غرباء) it means 'stranger(s)'.

examples.trans: I heard a strange metallic knock at night.
Why would he leave his bag with strangers?

meanings.note: Standard collocation with rain: مطر غزير ('heavy downpour').

examples.text: نزل مطر غزير طول الليل وغسل الشجر.
examples.trans: Heavy rain fell all night and washed the trees clean.

examples.text: النشرة بتتوقع مطر غزير لبكرا الضهر.
examples.trans: The forecast predicts heavy rain until tomorrow noon.

meanings.note: Wash dishes, clothes, windows or your hands.

examples.trans: I washed the cups and put them on the shelf.
Wash your hands before eating.

meanings.note: The word 'غسلتوا' (غسلتوا) means 'غسلتوا'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: أهلا فيكم بمختبر كيكة التوت تبع يوم الأحد يا متدربين! غسلتوا إيديكم ورفعتوا أكمامكم؟
examples.trans: Welcome to the Sunday Berry Cake Laboratory, apprentices! Hands washed and sleeves rolled?
This is غسلتوا.

meanings.note: The word 'غسلناهم' (غسلناهم) means 'غسلناهم'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: غسلناهم مرتين يا شيف! جبت سلتين من التوت الأحمر المستوي واللوز الحلو.
examples.trans: Washed twice, Chef! I brought two baskets of ripe red berries and sweet almonds.
This is غسلناهم.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: The clean sheets are in the linen closet.
We hung the laundry in the morning sun.

meanings.note: Leafy branch of a tree or climbing shrub.

examples.text: رفعنا الغصن الأخضر عن شنكل الشباك بلطف.
examples.trans: We gently lifted the green branch off the window latch.

examples.text: عصفور صغير وقف على غصن شجرة الليمون.
examples.trans: A little bird perched on a branch of the lemon tree.

meanings.note: Refers to a lid, cover, or sometimes a blanket.

examples.trans: Where is the pot's lid?

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على غطا.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with غطا.

meanings.note: Form II verb meaning 'dip a sponge in water or dunk bread/biscuits in tea'.

examples.text: غطست الإسفنجة بالمي الدافية ومسحت اللوح.
examples.trans: I dipped the sponge in warm water and wiped the pane.

examples.text: بحب أغطس البسكوت بكاسة الشاي السخن.
examples.trans: I love dipping biscuits in a glass of hot tea.

meanings.note: The word 'غلب' (biyghleb) means 'he beats'. It is a common verb in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: أنا ساكن بشارع شارع الياسمين من عشرين سنة يا طارق، والزقاق بيغلب البوصلة!
examples.trans: I have lived on Jasmine Street for twenty years, Tariq, and alleys beat compasses!
This is غلب.

meanings.note: Very Jordanian polite apology: آسف عالغلبة ('sorry for the trouble/hassle').

examples.trans: Sorry for all the trouble today.

examples.text: ولا غلبة ولا شي، أهلا وسهلا!
examples.trans: No trouble at all, you are most welcome!

meanings.note: Used as noun in بالغلط ('by mistake') and عالغلط ('for the mistake'), and invariable predicate 'wrong' (في شي غلط something is wrong).

examples.trans: He took the other suitcase by mistake.
Sorry for the mistake, my apologies.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: غلطانة, plural: غلطانين).

examples.trans: Both of us were in the wrong back then.
Sorry, I had the wrong address.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: غلطات.

examples.trans: This is not your fault at all.
We fixed the slip-up in two minutes.

meanings.note: Everyday kitchen verb for boiling liquids.

examples.trans: We used the word غلى.
This is another غلى.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بغلب, بيغلب).

examples.trans: Please do not trouble yourself on our account!
Sorry if I put you to trouble today.

meanings.en: to wrap; to cover; to seal in a cover
meanings.note: Form II verb from root غ-ل-ف (same root as غلاف 'cover/envelope').

examples.trans: We wrapped it in wax paper.
We need to wrap the gift before the party.

meanings.note: The word 'غمضي' (غمضي) means 'غمضي'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: غمضي عيونك وتنفسي: نعناع الحديقة، وبرش برتقال حلو، وعسل ذهبي!
examples.trans: Close your eyes and breathe in: garden mint, sweet orange zest, and golden honey!
This is غمضي.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: The mystery story was finally solved!
I enjoy novels with a bit of mystery.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بغمض, بيغمض).

examples.trans: Close your eyes and taste the cake!
She closed her eyes and listened to the rain.

meanings.note: Describes a wealthy person as well as rich flavours, colours, or musical tones (طعم غني 'rich taste').

examples.text: عسل الجبل طعمه غني ودافي مع الشاي.
examples.trans: Mountain honey has a rich, warm taste with tea.

examples.text: خشب الجوز بيعطي البيانو صوت غني.
examples.trans: Walnut wood gives the piano a rich sound.

meanings.note: Everyday verb for singing; a song is أغنية.

examples.trans: My grandmother sings while she cooks.
We all sang at his birthday.

meanings.note: After negation, ما ... غير means 'only / nothing except'.

examples.text: ما معي غير المعطف اللي علي!
examples.trans: I have nothing with me except the coat I have on!
There are only two valves on the shelf.

meanings.note: Unit noun of collective غيم ('clouds'); plural غيوم. Frequently used in Levantine speech alongside سحابة.

examples.text: القمر عم بيطلع من ورا غيمة خفيفة.
examples.trans: The moon is peeking out from behind a light cloud.

examples.text: اليوم السما صافية وما فيها ولا غيمة.
examples.trans: Today the sky is clear with not a single cloud.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بغير, بيغير).

examples.trans: Rami changed his shirt three times!
We gave him a discount because we changed the room.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بغلط, بيغلط).

examples.text: لما يغلط بنغمة بيانو كان يكشر!
examples.trans: Whenever he missed a piano note, he would frown!

examples.text: كل واحد ممكن يغلط بأول يوم.
examples.trans: Anyone can make a mistake on the first day.

meanings.note: Used mostly in formal contexts, but occasionally spills into educated colloquial speech to mean 'then it is' or 'because it'.

examples.trans: If you study, then indeed you will succeed.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على فإنه.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with فإنه.

meanings.note: The Levantine everyday verb for entering a room or building (فوت! 'come in!'), where formal Arabic says دخل.

examples.trans: Come in, the door is open.
We went into the restaurant at eight.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: فواتير.

examples.trans: The shopkeeper gave me a receipt and change.
We sorted all the invoices in the drawer.

meanings.note: Feminine verb agreeing with non-human plural الدفاتر, from فاز ('to win').

examples.trans: We used the word فاز.
This is another فاز.

meanings.en: interval; gap; break or divider between items
meanings.note: Masculine noun (plural فواصل) from فصل ('to separate'). Used for regular spacing along a line or a short pause.

examples.text: اترك فاصل متساوي بين كل فانوس والتاني.
examples.trans: Leave an even interval between each lantern and the next.

examples.text: خدنا فاصل قصير قبل ما نكمل الشغل.
examples.trans: We took a short break before continuing the work.

meanings.note: Used to describe an empty container or a person who has free time.

examples.trans: I am free today in the afternoon.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على فاضي.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with فاضي.

meanings.note: Idiomatic Arabic colour modifier (أصفر فاقع 'bright lemon yellow', أخضر فاقع 'vivid green').

examples.text: لون الليمون الأصفر الفاقع طالع حلو جنب الأخضر.
examples.trans: The bright lemon-yellow colour looks great next to the green.

examples.text: ما بدنا لون فاقع، بدنا أخضر هادي متل الغابة.
examples.trans: We don't want a flashy shade—we want a calm forest green.

meanings.note: Active participle of فكر used as a stative predicate meaning 'remembers' (أنا فاكر 'I remember').

examples.trans: Do you remember where we put the keys?

examples.text: كلنا فاكرين القصة اللي حكيتها زمان.
examples.trans: We all remember the story you told back then.

meanings.note: Active participle of فلت ('to slip loose'): feminine فالتة, plural فالتين.

examples.text: انتبه، في حبل فالت من الجهة اليمين.
examples.trans: Careful, there is a loose rope on the right side.

examples.text: عقدنا كل الخيوط الفالتة قبل ما يطيروا.
examples.trans: We tied all the loose threads before they blew away.

meanings.note: Musical loanword (from French valse) for a triple-time piano or orchestral waltz.

examples.text: عزفت سعاد فالس هادي بغرفة القزاز.
examples.trans: Suad played a gentle waltz in the sunroom.

examples.text: عنوان الورقة القديمة هو فالس الساحة.
examples.trans: The title on the old sheet is Courtyard Waltz.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: فوانيس.

examples.trans: The golden lanterns are lit in the courtyard.
We hung a brass lantern by the entrance.

meanings.note: The word 'فانيليا' (فانيليا) means 'فانيليا'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: جداتنا كانوا يدهنوا عسل على معجنات المكسرات من قبل ما يكون في إشي اسمه سكر فانيليا!
examples.trans: Our grandmothers brushed honey over nut pastries long before vanilla sugar existed!
This is فانيليا.

meanings.note: Active participle of فات (to enter), agreeing with نسمة.

examples.trans: We used the word فايت.
This is another فايت.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بفتح, بيفتح).

examples.trans: The corner shop opens at seven.
Oh, the door finally opened!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: فتحات.

examples.trans: There is a small keyhole on the front.
Air is coming through the window opening.

فتحت.gloss: I opened / you (m) opened / she opened

meanings.en: I opened / you (m) opened / she opened
meanings.note: Past tense verb meaning 'opened', conjugated for 1st person, 2nd person masc, or 3rd person fem.

examples.trans: I opened the window so the house airs out.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على فتحت.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with فتحت.

meanings.note: With demonstrative هـ + الـ, هالفترة means 'during this period / right now'.

examples.trans: I'm very busy these days.
A hard period passed over us.

meanings.note: Charming colloquial Jordanian word for a tiny crumb or morsel.

examples.trans: We used the word فتفوتة.
This is another فتفوتة.

meanings.note: Sets up an unexpected turn in a story (فجأة ليان إجت).

examples.trans: Suddenly everyone in the classroom went quiet.
She appeared in front of me suddenly.

meanings.note: Early pre-sunrise morning (الفجر), prime baking hour in Levantine bakeries.

examples.text: الخبازين بيصحوا قبل الفجر عشان يخبزوا العجين.
examples.trans: Bakers wake up before dawn to bake the dough.

examples.text: هوا الفجر بعمان بيكون بارد ومنعش كتير.
examples.trans: Dawn air in Amman is crisp and deeply refreshing.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بفحص, بيفحص).

examples.trans: Tariq will inspect the cellar right away.
We checked the heater and pipes this morning.

meanings.note: Collective masculine noun for charcoal (for grilling or sketching); a single piece is فحمة.

examples.trans: A quick charcoal sketch will do.
We lit the charcoal for grilling in the garden.

meanings.note: Handcrafted fired clay vessels and cups, a staple of Jordanian and Levantine street markets.

examples.text: اشترينا إبريق وفناجين من بسطة الفخار.
examples.trans: We bought a pitcher and cups from the pottery stall.

examples.text: المي ببريق الفخار بتضل باردة بالصيف.
examples.trans: Water in a clay pitcher stays cool in summer.

meanings.note: Prepositional adverbial phrase meaning 'with pride / proudly'.

examples.trans: We used the word فخر.
This is another فخر.

meanings.note: Takes بـ ('proud of someone or something').

examples.text: أنا فخور فيكم واحد واحد عالشغل المتقن.
examples.trans: I'm proud of every single one of you for the careful work.

examples.text: نور كانت فخورة بلوحة البوابة اللي رسمتها.
examples.trans: Nour was proud of the gate sign she lettered.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun.

examples.trans: Strawberry jam is sweet and delicious.
We bought fresh strawberries from the market.

meanings.note: Idiomatic Jordanian exclamation فرجت! ('relief has arrived! / we are saved!').

examples.trans: We are saved! The hot water is back!
Things tighten up and then work out.

meanings.note: Classic Levantine everyday verb for 'to show' (فرجيني 'show me!').

examples.trans: Show the shopkeeper this brass valve.
Let me show you my real work!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بفرح, بيفرح).

examples.trans: Let the two brothers enjoy their Friday!
We were overjoyed at the good news.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: فرحات.

examples.trans: His eyes shone with joy!
The family's joy is beyond words.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بفرد, بيفرد).

examples.text: افرد كتافك يا رامي وخد نفس!
examples.trans: Square your shoulders, Rami, and take a breath!
We spread the white tablecloth over the table.

فرش.gloss: to spread; lay out (cloth or light)

meanings.en: to spread; lay out (cloth or light)
meanings.note: Used literally for spreading a tablecloth or rug and figuratively for warm light spreading across a room.

examples.text: فرشت سلمى شراشف بيضا عالطاولات الخشب.
examples.trans: Salma spread white cloths over the wooden tables.

examples.text: ضو الصبح بيفرش دفا حلو عالساحة.
examples.trans: Morning light spreads lovely warmth across the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Levantine word for a paintbrush, hairbrush, or pastry brush.

examples.text: غسلنا الفرشايات بمي دافية أول ما خلصنا دهان.
examples.trans: We washed the brushes in warm water right after finishing the painting.

examples.text: لا ترفع الإيد اللي ماسكة الفرشاية الخضرا!
examples.trans: Don't lift the hand that's holding the green paintbrush!

meanings.note: Masculine noun used both literally for tree branches and figuratively for shop branches. Plural: فروع.

examples.trans: Let's leave it by the almond branch.

examples.text: هاد الفرع قريب من وسط البلد.
examples.trans: This branch is close to downtown.

meanings.note: Everyday noun meaning 'difference' or 'gap' in time or amount.

examples.trans: We used the word فرق.
This is another فرق.

meanings.note: Everyday Levantine kitchen verb for chopping vegetables or herbs.

examples.text: زياد بيقشر البصل وبيفرم الجزر للشوربة.
examples.trans: Ziad peels the onions and chops the carrots for the soup.

examples.text: فرمت ضمة بقدونس طازة فوق الصحن.
examples.trans: I chopped a fresh bunch of parsley over the dish.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أفران.

examples.text: لفائف القرفة طلعت من الفرن هلا.
examples.trans: The cinnamon rolls just came out of the oven.
The bakery down the street bakes in the morning.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: فرنسية, plural: فرنسيين).

examples.trans: We made French-style eggs.
Hot French bread with butter.

meanings.note: The word for oven with the 1st person possessive suffix.

examples.trans: My oven is broken and I need to fix it.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على فرني.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with فرني.

meanings.note: Masculine Arabic noun for a team or crew.

examples.trans: We used the word فريق.
This is another فريق.

meanings.note: In Levantine Arabic, a noun for a neighbourhood baker, from فرن ('oven').

examples.trans: We used the word فرّان.
This is another فرّان.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: فساتين.

examples.trans: She folded the dresses and packed them in the suitcase.
The blue dress is neat and comfortable.
