Everyone agrees on the new idea.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: موافقات.

examples.trans: He nodded his head in agreement with a smile.
We received official municipal approval.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: موجودة, plural: موجودين).

examples.trans: Your glasses are right there on your forehead!
Tariq is down in the workshop.

meanings.note: The word 'موجودة' (موجودة) means 'موجودة'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: هيك البلكونة الخشب برا بسطة الطابق التاني—بالزبط محل ما النجمة الحمرا موجودة!
examples.trans: There is the wooden balcony outside the second-floor landing—right where the red star sits!
This is موجودة.

meanings.note: Form II passive participle from ورد ('rose/flower'): describes floral fabric or patterns.

examples.trans: She put a floral shawl over her shoulders.
The floral curtain brightened up the room.

meanings.note: Used for literal weight or metaphorically for a balanced, rational person or idea.

examples.trans: Her decisions are always balanced.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على موزونة.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with موزونة.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun.

examples.trans: We found an old music book in the suitcase.
Gentle music is soothing in the evening.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: موسيقية, plural: موسيقيين).

examples.trans: Play the musical scale slowly.
She has a sensitive musical ear.

meanings.note: Passive participle of وصل ('to connect, join').

examples.text: السلك النحاس موصول منيح بعلبة الكهربا.
examples.trans: The copper wire is firmly connected to the electrical box.
The sunroom is connected to the back hallway.

meanings.note: Feminine loanword used in everyday speech for clothing trends, hairstyles, or anything stylish.

examples.trans: That was the summer fashion back then.
She follows fashion every season.

meanings.note: Used for an issue under discussion (هاد الموضوع، أي موضوع بالضبط؟).

examples.trans: Let's close this topic.
The matter is more serious than I thought.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: موظفين.

examples.trans: I am the new receptionist at the guesthouse.
All the staff here are helpful and friendly.

meanings.note: Feminine form of موظف, revealing the municipal inspector is a woman.

examples.trans: We used the word موظفة.
This is another موظفة.

meanings.note: The word 'موظفين' (موظفين) means 'موظفين'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: بدون حكي من موظفين المطبخ، لو سمحتوا. التذوق المضبوط بده هدوء تام.
examples.trans: No talking from the kitchen staff, please. A proper tasting requires complete silence.
This is موظفين.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: مواعيد.

examples.trans: I always appreciate punctuality.

examples.text: عندنا موعد مهم يوم الجمعة الظهر.
examples.trans: We have an important appointment Friday at noon.

meanings.note: Form II passive participle of وقّع ('to sign a document, check, or letter'), root و-ق-ع.

examples.trans: The little notebook is signed by Suad.
The paper is signed and stamped, ready.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: مواهب.

examples.trans: She has a natural gift for cooking and hospitality.
Playing music takes talent and daily practice.

meanings.note: Universal Jordanian/Levantine word for water (feminine!). Before another noun in possession ('water of...'), becomes مية (mayyet): مية الدوش ('shower water'), مية الشتا ('winter water').

examples.trans: Please drink a glass of cold water.
The hot water is working again in the bathroom.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian numeral 'one hundred' (مية مرة 'a hundred times' — construct مية miyyet before a noun).

examples.trans: Yes, a hundred times yes!
I am one hundred percent sure.

meanings.note: Colloquial pronunciation of the dual form for 100.

examples.trans: I only have two hundred dinars.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على ميتين.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with ميتين.

meanings.note: The word 'ميداليات' (ميداليات) means 'ميداليات'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: يس! عشرة من عشرة بقلم مازن بتسوى تلات ميداليات ذهبية!
examples.trans: YES! Ten out of ten in Mazen pencil is worth three gold medals!
This is ميداليات.

meanings.note: The word 'ميز' (ymayyez) means 'he recognizes'. It is a common verb in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: مين بيحتاج نظارات قراءة عشان يميز دخلة حارة مستقيمة تماما؟
examples.trans: Who needs reading glasses to recognize a perfectly straight neighbourhood lane?
This is ميز.

meanings.note: From ميزان ('scales, balance'); everyday word for a household or project budget.

examples.text: اشترينا كل الأغراض وضلينا ضمن الميزانية.
examples.trans: We bought all the supplies and stayed within budget.
Nour worked out the café budget in the notebook.

meanings.note: Interrogative pronoun used for people.

examples.trans: Who rang the bell?

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على مين.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with مين.

meanings.note: Colloquial spelling of ميناء (masculine or feminine; plural موانئ / مينايات).

examples.text: سفينة الصيد رجعت عالمينا قبل الليل.
examples.trans: The fishing boat returned to the harbour before nightfall.

examples.text: رسمت قوارب صغيرة واقفة عند المينا.
examples.trans: I drew small boats docked by the harbour.

meanings.note: Form II verb ميّز means 'to distinguish' or 'tell apart'.

examples.trans: We used the word ميّز.
This is another ميّز.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بمنع, بيمنع).

examples.trans: The old stone keeps out street noise.
The awning kept the rain off the window.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بمشي, بيمشي).

examples.trans: I always walk fast on the first day.

examples.text: اسمع، المي عم بتمشي جوا الماسورة!
examples.trans: Listen, the water is flowing inside the pipe!

meanings.note: The word 'ناخده' (ناخده) means 'ناخده'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: خلينا ناخده طوالي لـ سلمى بغرفة تسعة قبل ما حدا يتنفس بقوة!
examples.trans: Let us carry it straight to Salma in Room Nine before anyone breathes too hard!
This is ناخده.

meanings.note: The word 'ناخذهم' (ناخذهم) means 'ناخذهم'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: رح ناخذهم التلاتة طوالي لـ مازن؛ ذوقه الصعب عمره ما بسامح أي غلطة.
examples.trans: We take all three straight to Mazen; his tough palate never forgives a mistake.
This is ناخذهم.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بنادي, بينادي).

examples.trans: Do we call each other by first name here?
Salma called everyone to breakfast.

meanings.note: Feminine noun (unmarked, without ة ending). Used both for campfires and a kitchen stove flame.

examples.trans: The kitchen stove fire is still a bit low.
Put the kettle on the fire.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: نازلة, plural: نازلين).

examples.trans: The guests are coming down the stairs for breakfast.

examples.text: مش مصدق إنك نازلة بنفس النزل!
examples.trans: I cannot believe you are staying at the same inn!

meanings.note: The word 'نازلة' (نازلة) means 'نازلة'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: عالموعد بالزبط! شوفوا مين نازلة عالدرج مع كتاب أخضر!
examples.trans: Right on cue! Look who is coming down the stairs with a green book!
This is نازلة.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: ناس.

examples.trans: You are kind, generous people.
Morning coffee brings people together in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Can refer to objects lacking moisture or metaphorically to a rude or blunt person.

examples.trans: The bread is dry, it can't be eaten.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على ناشف.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with ناشف.

meanings.note: Feminine adjective for dry objects.

examples.trans: The ground is dry, it needs water.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على ناشفة.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with ناشفة.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: ناعمة, plural: ناعمين).

examples.trans: I brought two soft pillows for the attic.
Lemon cake dusted with powdered sugar.

meanings.note: Used for decorative water fountains in parks or squares.

examples.trans: There is a beautiful fountain in the park.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على نافورة.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with نافورة.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: ناقصة, plural: ناقصين).

examples.trans: Tell me what is missing in the room?

examples.text: الأغراض كاملة ما فيها شي ناقص.
examples.trans: Everything is complete with nothing missing.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بنام, بينام).

examples.trans: I feel I will sleep well tonight.
Did you sleep well under the wooden ceiling?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بناول, بيناول).

examples.trans: Hand me the heavy iron wrench.
Pass me the teacup, please.

meanings.note: The word 'ناوليني' (ناوليني) means 'ناوليني'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: ناوليني دفتر الورق تبعي وقلم النجار الرصاص من جنب الإبريق يا نور.
examples.trans: Hand me my paper notebook and my carpenter pencil from beside the teapot, Nour.
This is ناوليني.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: ناوية, plural: ناويين).

examples.trans: Were you planning to watch from afar?
We intend to open the courtyard to the neighbours in the morning.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: نايمة, plural: نايمين).

examples.trans: The new guest is sleeping on the third floor.
The whole neighbourhood is asleep and quiet.

meanings.note: Verb for putting a picture or document in a frame.

examples.trans: We must frame this picture.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على نبروز.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with نبروز.

meanings.note: Formal word for a prediction of the future, often religious.

examples.trans: The ancient prophecy came true.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على نبوءة.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with نبوءة.

meanings.note: Used for physically following someone or metaphorically following rules/ideas.

examples.trans: We must follow the instructions.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على نتبع.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with نتبع.

meanings.note: Used for physical motion or starting to take action.

examples.trans: We are late, we need to move now.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على نتحرك.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with نتحرك.

meanings.note: Vivid Levantine word for a tiny pinch or scrap; ولا نتفة means 'not a single scrap / zero'.

examples.text: ما ضل ولا نتفة غبرة عالرفوف.
examples.trans: Not a single speck of dust is left on the shelves.

examples.text: حطي نتفة قرفة صغيرة فوق الكيك.
examples.trans: Put a tiny pinch of cinnamon on top of the cake.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: نجارين.

examples.text: النجار صنع الطاولة من خشب بلوط.
examples.trans: The carpenter built the table out of oak wood.
My grandfather was a master carpenter in the quarter.

نجح.gloss: to succeed; pass with flying colours

meanings.en: to succeed; pass with flying colours
meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بنجح, بينجح).

examples.trans: You passed the breakfast rush with flying colours, Nour!
The plan succeeded and we saved the house.

meanings.note: Everyday word for attempting something or tasting food.

examples.trans: Let's try this new restaurant.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على نجرب.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with نجرب.

meanings.note: Can be used for physical cuts or emotional hurt.

examples.trans: We don't want to hurt anyone's feelings.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على نجرح.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with نجرح.

meanings.note: Used for celestial stars, geometric shapes, or famous celebrities.

examples.trans: The sky is full of stars today.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على نجمة.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with نجمة.

meanings.note: Used for the metal or objects made of it.

examples.trans: This jug is made of copper.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على نحاس.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with نحاس.

meanings.note: Adjective indicating something is made of or related to copper.

examples.trans: He bought an old copper antique.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على نحاسية.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with نحاسية.

meanings.note: The word 'نحل' (نحل) means 'نحل'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: كيف رح نحل مشكلة الحبر الأزرق الملطخ من تحت يا سلمى؟
examples.trans: How are we going to solve the smudged blue ink at the bottom, Salma?
This is نحل.

meanings.note: The word 'نخبز' (نخبز) means 'نخبز'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: ولا واحد منهم! عم نخبز الكيكة الغامضة تبعت التلاتين سنة ومرطبان العسل فاضي!
examples.trans: Neither! We are baking the thirty-year-old mystery cake and the honey jar is empty!
This is نخبز.

meanings.note: In Levantine Arabic, a noun for a sharp twinge or sudden prick of pain.

examples.trans: We used the word نخزة.
This is another نخزة.

meanings.note: The word 'نخليلك' (نخليلك) means 'نخليلك'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: إنت منقذ يا رامي! رح نخليلك شقفة إذا مازن ما أكلها كلها!
examples.trans: You are a lifesaver, Rami! We will save you a slice if Mazen does not eat it all!
This is نخليلك.

meanings.note: Most common verb for searching ('ndawwir 'ala') or turning something around.

examples.trans: We have been looking for you for an hour.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على ندور.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with ندور.

meanings.note: Used for lifting objects, raising voices, or uploading files.

examples.trans: We have to raise the volume to hear.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على نرفع.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with نرفع.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: نزل.

examples.text: نزل الساحة فيه تمن غرف هادية.
examples.trans: The courtyard guesthouse has eight quiet rooms.
Welcome to our small guesthouse.

meanings.note: Imperative addressed to a female to take something down, drop off, or lower a price.

examples.trans: Put the bag down on the floor.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على نزلي.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with نزلي.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بنزل, بينزل).

examples.trans: Let us bring the suitcase down into the light.
Let me lower my glasses from my forehead!

meanings.note: Common Arabic phrase بالنسبة لـ meaning 'as for' or 'what about'.

examples.trans: We used the word نسبة.
This is another نسبة.

meanings.en: to copy; trace a drawing; transcribe text
meanings.note: Form I verb (بنسخ / نسخ) used both for hand-copying drawings and copying text or files.

examples.text: نسخت الرسمة القديمة على ورقة نظيفة.
examples.trans: I copied the old drawing onto a clean sheet.

examples.text: ممكن تنسخ لي الوصفة على دفتري؟
examples.trans: Could you copy the recipe into my notebook for me?

meanings.note: Feminine noun from نسخ ('to copy'); used for photocopies, spare keys, or book editions. Plural: نسخ.

examples.trans: There's a second copy inside the house.
Make me a copy of the key.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: نسمات.

examples.trans: There is a pleasant breeze in the courtyard.
The boy is as quiet as a breeze.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بنسى, بينسى).

examples.trans: You forgot the notebook beside the soup bowl.
With all the rush, I completely forgot!

meanings.note: Masculine noun (plural نسمات / أنسام) for a pleasant light breeze, especially in the evening.

examples.text: في نسيم بارد لطيف عالسطح بالليل.
examples.trans: There is a pleasant cool breeze on the roof at night.
The sea breeze moved the lanterns gently.

meanings.note: Used for wood shavings left after carpentry.

examples.trans: The floor is full of sawdust.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على نشارة.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with نشارة.

meanings.note: The word 'نشافة' (نشافة) means 'نشافة'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: اقلبوا الصفحات شوي شوي فوق نشافة المكتب عشان ما يوقع إشي ناشف عالأرض.
examples.trans: Turn the pages gently over the desk blotter so nothing dry slips onto the floor.
This is نشافة.

نشر.gloss: to spread out; hang out (laundry/lanterns); publish

meanings.en: to spread out to dry; hang along a line; publish
meanings.note: Form I verb (بنشر / نشر). Classic Levantine verb for hanging laundry or paper decorations along a rope.

examples.text: نشرنا الفوانيس على طول الحبل بين العواميد.
examples.trans: We hung the lanterns along the length of the rope between the posts.
My mother hung the laundry out on the roof in the morning.

meanings.note: Short for نشرة الطقس / النشرة الجوية ('weather forecast').

examples.text: نشرة يوم التنين بتقول في مطر غزير الصبح.
examples.trans: Monday's forecast says heavy rain in the morning.

examples.text: خليني أشوف نشرة الطقس قبل ما ندهن برا.
examples.trans: Let me check the weather forecast before we paint outside.

meanings.note: The word 'نشطة' (نشطة) means 'نشطة'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: سما صافية، ليالي دافية، وهبات هواء ربيعية نشطة رح تضرب البلد يوم الجمعة.
examples.trans: Clear skies, warm evenings, and brisk spring wind gusts sweeping across town on Friday.
This is نشطة.

meanings.note: Form I intransitive verb (nishif / byinshaf) meaning 'dry out'.

examples.text: لما تطلع الشمس، الحجار بتنشف بسرعة.
examples.trans: When the sun comes out, the stones dry quickly.

examples.text: استنينا ساعتين لحد ما ينشف الدهان.
examples.trans: We waited two hours until the paint dried.

meanings.note: The word 'نشم' (نشم) means 'نشم'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: رجعت! هادا هو العسل—بس رامي حكى نشم صفحة الكتاب القديم بالأول!
examples.trans: I am back! Here is the honey—but Rami said to smell the old book page first!
This is نشم.

meanings.note: Form II transitive counterpart of نشف ('to become dry'): used for drying berries, dishes, or towels.

examples.text: اغسل التوت ونشفه منيح بفوطة نضيفة.
examples.trans: Wash the berries and dry them well with a clean towel.

examples.text: نشفي إيديكي قبل ما تفتحي الدفتر.
examples.trans: Dry your hands before opening the notebook.

meanings.note: Extremely common word used in time (e.g., 3 and a half) and measurements.

examples.trans: The time is five and a half (half past five).

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على نص.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with نص.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: نصانية, plural: —).

examples.trans: The notebook opened to the middle page.
I picked the middle table in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Noun 'half' with the feminine 3rd person singular pronoun suffix.

examples.trans: I ate half of it and left the rest.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على نصها.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with نصها.

meanings.note: The word 'نصين' (نصين) means 'نصين'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: كل ألياف الورق الصغيرة بتطابق متل نصين فنجان شاي مكسور!
examples.trans: Every tiny paper fibre lines up like two halves of a broken teacup!
This is نصين.

meanings.note: In Levantine Arabic, a noun for eyeglasses (usually plural in Arabic), with 'my'.

examples.trans: We used the word نضارة.
This is another نضارة.

meanings.note: Colloquial Levantine spelling of نظافة (standard dental ظ -> alveolar ض in Amman speech).

examples.text: شوف نضافة الشرفة بعد ما مسحنا الدرابزين.
examples.trans: Look at the cleanliness of the terrace after we wiped the railing.
Cleanliness is the most important thing in the kitchen and workshop.

meanings.note: The word 'نضطر' (نضطر) means 'نضطر'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: إنتي شجاعة يا سلمى. إذا عمل كشرة تلميع النحاس، رح نضطر نعيد كل شي من أول وجديد!
examples.trans: You are brave, Salma. If he makes the brass-polish face, we start all over again!
This is نضطر.

meanings.note: Natural spoken Levantine pronunciation of نظيف ('clean'), broken plural نضاف.

examples.text: مسحنا الفرشاية بقماشة نضيفة ومي دافية.
examples.trans: We wiped the brush with a clean cloth and warm water.

examples.text: المطبخ صار نضيف ومرتب وجاهز لبكرا الصبح.
examples.trans: The kitchen is spotless, tidy, and ready for tomorrow morning.

meanings.note: Geminate verb (ن-ط-ط) for jumping or hopping over an obstacle.

examples.text: القطة نطت عن الحيط للجنينة بهدوء.
examples.trans: The cat jumped quietly off the wall into the garden.

examples.text: ما بدنا الضيوف ينطوا فوق الكراسي بالممر!
examples.trans: We don't want guests climbing over chairs in the hallway!

meanings.note: Colloquial verb for bending metal or denting a car.

examples.trans: Be careful so we don't dent the car.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على نطعج.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with نطعج.

meanings.note: The word 'نظارات' (نظارات) means 'نظارات'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: وهادا القاضي مازن لابس نظارات القراءة تبعونه، ومبين جدي كتير الصراحة.
examples.trans: And here is Judge Mazen with his reading glasses on, looking very serious indeed.
This is نظارات.

meanings.note: Plural noun with second person masculine singular suffix.

examples.trans: Where did you put your glasses?

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على نظاراتك.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with نظاراتك.

meanings.note: Plural noun with first person singular suffix.

examples.trans: My glasses broke yesterday.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على نظاراتي.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with نظاراتي.

meanings.note: Singular نظارة means one pair of glasses in Arabic (نظارتي my glasses); dual نظارتين means two pairs of glasses!

examples.trans: I cannot find my glasses on the desk!
He pulled his glasses down off his forehead and laughed.

meanings.note: Used for rules, computer systems, or political regimes.

examples.trans: We must follow the system.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على نظام.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with نظام.

meanings.note: In نلفت نظرهم ('draw their eyes/attention'), pairs with لفت.

examples.trans: We don't want to catch the teacher's eye.
Your point of view is clear.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: نظرات.

examples.trans: Let me take a quick look at the letter.
He spotted the problem at first glance.

meanings.note: The word 'نظف' (نظف) means 'نظف'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: حلو كتير! ماشي يا مدير، نظف تمك بشاي أسود وجرب صينية رقم تنين!
examples.trans: Too sweet! Okay, Boss, wash your palate with black tea and try Tin Two!
This is نظف.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for clean or tidy.

examples.trans: The house is clean after the deep cleaning.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على نظيف.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with نظيف.

meanings.note: Clear, polite 'yes' (slightly warmer and more formal than casual آه).

examples.trans: Yes, room four is on the second floor!
Yes, a hundred times yes!

meanings.note: The word 'نعناع' (نعناع) means 'نعناع'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: استنوا—الكتاب عم يفتح لحاله قريب من الفصل السابع عن نعناع الصيف!
examples.trans: Wait—the book falls open all by itself near chapter seven on summer mint!
This is نعناع.

meanings.note: A very common herb used in Levantine tea and cuisine.

examples.trans: I want a cup of tea with mint.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على نعنع.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with نعنع.

meanings.note: Feminine abstract noun from ناعم ('soft/smooth'). Common phrase: بنعومة ('gently / softly').

examples.trans: The lanterns sway gently with the breeze.

examples.text: مسكت الفرشاية بنعومة عشان ما تسيح الألوان.
examples.trans: I held the brush gently so the colours wouldn't run.

meanings.note: The word 'نعيد' (نعيد) means 'نعيد'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: إنتي شجاعة يا سلمى. إذا عمل كشرة تلميع النحاس، رح نضطر نعيد كل شي من أول وجديد!
examples.trans: You are brave, Salma. If he makes the brass-polish face, we start all over again!
This is نعيد.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: نغمات.

examples.text: سمع كل نغمة من البيانو بهدوء.
examples.trans: He listened quietly to every note of the piano.
The chime of the bell is gentle, not harsh.

meanings.note: Describes wood swelling from dampness as well as blowing air.

examples.text: الخشب القديم نفخ شوي من رطوبة الشتا.
examples.trans: The old wood swelled slightly from the winter damp.
The pastry puffed up in the oven and turned golden.

meanings.note: Often used to mean 'the same' when followed by a noun, or as a reflexive.

examples.trans: We live in the same building.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على نفس.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with نفس.

meanings.note: Reflexive pronoun for third person feminine.

examples.trans: She herself told me this.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على نفسها.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with نفسها.

meanings.note: Can refer to a physical dot, a score point, or a drop of liquid.

examples.trans: I just want a drop of water.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على نقطة.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with نقطة.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: We read the property transfer paper.
Moving the boxes took five minutes.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بنقط, بينقط).

examples.text: آسف نقطت مي على أرضكم النظيفة.
examples.trans: Sorry I dripped water on your clean floor.
The pipe stopped dripping.

meanings.note: The word 'نكهة' (نكهة) means 'نكهة'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: ورشة من قشر البرتقال المبروش بتعطي نكهة لتوت الصيف من غير ما تخلي مازن يكشر!
examples.trans: And a pinch of grated orange peel brightens the summer berries without puckering Mazen!
This is نكهة.

meanings.note: First person plural present verb.

examples.trans: Maybe we will find a solution to the problem.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على نلاقي.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with نلاقي.

meanings.note: Standard first person plural verb often used in colloquial speech.

examples.trans: When will we meet again?

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على نلتقي.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with نلتقي.

meanings.note: Commonly used for turning a vehicle or wrapping food.

examples.trans: Let's turn from this street.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على نلف.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with نلف.

meanings.note: Contrasts with ليل ('nighttime'): بنور النهار = 'in broad daylight'.

examples.text: الشيش الأخضر طالع أحلى بكتير بنور النهار!
examples.trans: The green shutters look even lovelier in daylight!

examples.text: شتغلنا طول النهار وبالمسا شربنا شاي بالنعنع.
examples.trans: We worked all day long and in the evening had mint tea.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: نهايات.

examples.trans: There is a new booking for the weekend.

examples.text: بالنهاية كل شي انحل على خير.
examples.trans: In the end everything worked out well.

meanings.note: Standard word for a river.

examples.trans: We sat next to the Jordan River.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على نهر.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with نهر.

نوتة.gloss: sheet music; musical score; pocket notepad

meanings.en: sheet music; musical score; pocket notepad
meanings.note: Used across the Levant for printed or handwritten musical notation (نوتة موسيقية).

examples.text: فتحت سعاد نوتة البيانو القديمة عالصفحة الأولى.
examples.trans: Suad opened the old piano score to page one.

examples.text: كتب المؤلف النوتة بحبر أسود واضح.
examples.trans: The composer wrote the score in clear black ink.

meanings.note: Appears in صباح النور ('morning of light', the standard reply to صباح الخير) and نور الشمس ('sunlight').

examples.trans: Good morning and welcome!
We read the card in the sunlight.

meanings.note: The word 'نور—بعد' (نور—بعد) means 'نور—بعد'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: راقبي الساعة يا نور—بعد أربعين دقيقة من هلق، لازم هدول الكيكات الصغيرة التلاتة يكونوا مثاليين.
examples.trans: Watch the clock, Nour—forty minutes from now, these three mini cakes must be perfect.
This is نور—بعد.

meanings.note: Masculine noun (plural أنواع). Extremely common: شو نوع الحبل؟ ('what kind of rope?').

examples.trans: Which type of paper is best for lanterns?

examples.text: عنا أنواع كتيرة من الخيوط والألوان.
examples.trans: We have many kinds of strings and colours.

meanings.note: Colloquial contraction of على النوم, used briskly to send everyone to bed.

examples.trans: We used the word نوم.
This is another نوم.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: نومات.

examples.trans: I had the best sleep in a month!
A quiet room makes for a restful sleep.

meanings.note: The word 'نية' (نية) means 'نية'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: ول يا نور! عم تلحقي حرامي، ولا حدا أكل فليفلة حارة نية بالغلط؟
examples.trans: Whoa, Nour! Are you chasing a thief, or did someone accidentally eat a raw hot pepper?
This is نية.

meanings.note: Vocalized lemma distinguishing the verb 'to move/relocate' from the noun نقل ('transport').

examples.trans: We moved the piano to the dry corner of the room.

examples.text: نور نقلت المواعيد من الدفتر للوح الأبيض.
examples.trans: Nour copied the dates from the notebook onto the whiteboard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بنزل, بينزل).

examples.trans: The guests will come down at half past seven.
I came down to ask about the sink water.

meanings.note: Lively conversational exclamation of triumph or attention ('ha! / there!').

examples.text: ما صاب قميصي ولا نقطة دهان، ها!
examples.trans: Not a single drop of paint touched my shirt—ha!

examples.text: ها، شو رأيكم باللون الأخضر تحت الشمس؟
examples.trans: Well, what do you think of the green colour in the sunshine?

meanings.note: Imperative-only verb in everyday Arabic, inflected for gender and number: هات (to a man), هاتي (to a woman), هاتوا (plural).

examples.text: هات السلة التقيلة عنك يا أستاذ مازن.
examples.trans: Give me that heavy basket for you, Mr Mazen.

examples.text: هاتي القلم الرصاص من على المكتب يا نور.
examples.trans: Hand me the pencil from the desk, Nour.

meanings.note: Everyday demonstrative pronoun for masculine singular objects.

examples.trans: This boy is very smart.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على هاد.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with هاد.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian spelling/pronunciation of هذا ('this/that').

examples.trans: We used the word هادا.
This is another هادا.

meanings.note: Masculine هادي ('quiet') is homographic with the feminine demonstrative هادي ('this'); context and agreement distinguish them cleanly.

examples.trans: The spot above the tree is very quiet.
We prepared the quiet attic room for you.

meanings.note: Jordanian spoken feminine distal demonstrative ('that one over there'), matching masc. هداك.

examples.trans: Open the drawer under that screen.
That table is close to the window.

meanings.note: The word 'هادي—هاد' (هادي—هاد) means 'هادي—هاد'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: طنين طنين بيوم أحد هادي—هاد الرنين المزدوج أكيد غرفة أربعة.
examples.trans: Buzz-buzz on a quiet Sunday—that double ring is definitely Room Four.
This is هادي—هاد.

meanings.note: Combination of demonstrative prefix and plural noun.

examples.trans: How beautiful these colors are together.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على هالألوان.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with هالألوان.

meanings.note: Used to point out a specific group of four things.

examples.trans: You must read these four books.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على هالاربع.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with هالاربع.

meanings.note: Demonstrative attached to a loanword.

examples.trans: This portrait was painted by a famous artist.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على هالبورتريه.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with هالبورتريه.

meanings.note: Demonstrative attached to the word for compass.

examples.trans: This compass will help you on the way.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على هالبوصلة.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with هالبوصلة.

meanings.note: Commonly used when referring to potholes on the road.

examples.trans: Watch out for this pothole.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على هالجورة.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with هالجورة.

meanings.note: Demonstrative phrase pointing out a rock.

examples.trans: Throw this stone far away.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على هالحجر.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with هالحجر.

meanings.note: Used extensively to refer to preceding statements, rumors, or ongoing discussions.

examples.trans: This talk is not correct at all.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على هالحكي.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with هالحكي.

meanings.note: Points out an aroma or odor.

examples.trans: Where is this nice smell coming from?

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على هالريحة.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with هالريحة.

meanings.note: Used to describe an echoing sound.

examples.trans: Do you hear this echo in the valley?

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على هالصدى.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with هالصدى.

meanings.note: Refers to a container or can.

examples.trans: Open this box and take some biscuits from it.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على هالعلبة.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with هالعلبة.

meanings.note: The word 'هالقوام' (هالقوام) means 'هالقوام'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: عم يقطع صينية رقم واحد اللي عليها طبقة سكر وفانيليا. شوفوا هالقوام الهش!
examples.trans: He is slicing Tin One with the vanilla sugar glaze. Look at that crumbly texture!
This is هالقوام.

meanings.note: Demonstrative phrase for a book.

examples.trans: This book is very useful for the exam.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على هالكتاب.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with هالكتاب.

meanings.note: The word 'هالكيكة' (هالكيكة) means 'هالكيكة'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: وهلق يا مازن؟ احكيلنا بصراحة—هل هالكيكة بتستاهل تنحط على طاولة الذكرى يوم السبت؟
examples.trans: Well, Mazen? Tell us honestly—is that worthy of our Saturday anniversary table?
This is هالكيكة.

meanings.note: Points out a written piece.

examples.trans: This text is long and needs time to read.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على هالنص.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with هالنص.

meanings.note: Everyday demonstrative pronoun for feminine singular objects.

examples.trans: This girl is very smart.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على هاي.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with هاي.

meanings.en: to blow suddenly (of wind); spring up
meanings.note: Geminate verb (بهب / هب). Used especially for sudden gusts of wind: الهوا هب فجأة ('the wind blew suddenly').

examples.trans: The wind blew hard and scattered the papers.

examples.text: كل يوم العصر بيهب نسيم حلو بالجبل.
examples.trans: Every afternoon a nice breeze blows on the hill.

meanings.note: Noun of instance (مرة) from هب ('to blow'): هبة هوا ('a gust of wind'). Plural هبات.

examples.text: إجت هبة هوا قوية على الشرفة.
examples.trans: A strong gust of wind came onto the terrace.
The gusts of wind in autumn cool the weather down.

meanings.note: Contracted phrase pointing out a card or ticket.

examples.trans: Take this card so you can enter.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على هبطاقة.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with هبطاقة.

meanings.note: Used chiefly in the idiomatic Levantine adverbial phrase عالهدا ('gently, slowly, carefully').

examples.text: حركي أصابع رجلك عالهدا وخدي نفس عميق.
examples.trans: Wiggle your toes gently and take a deep breath.

examples.text: نزلنا السلم عالهدا خطوة خطوة بالساحة.
examples.trans: We brought the ladder down gently step by step in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian distal demonstrative ('that over there / that past...'); feminine هديك (hadiik), plural هدولاك.

examples.text: بتذكر هداك الربيع لما فتحنا النزل؟
examples.trans: Do you remember that spring when we opened the inn?

examples.text: حط الصندوق على هداك الرف العالي.
examples.trans: Put the box on that high shelf.

meanings.note: Everyday Levantine feminine noun from هدي ('to calm down'). بهداوة means 'gently / calmly / take it easy'.

examples.text: امشي بهداوة يا سيدي، معنا وقت.
examples.trans: Walk gently, sir—we have time.
With calmness, every knot untangles.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: The morning quiet of the courtyard is very peaceful.
We talked the matter through calmly and patiently.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian plural demonstrative ('these / those') for people or things.

examples.trans: Whose are these brass keys?
I have grown fond of those two rings!

meanings.note: Feminine past tense of هدي ('to calm down/go quiet'), agreeing with الغرفة.

examples.trans: We used the word هدي.
This is another هدي.

meanings.note: Standard Arabic word for 'gift' or 'present'.

examples.trans: We used the word هدية.
This is another هدية.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بهدي, بيهدي).

examples.text: هدي بالك يا مازن، الغرفة جاهزة.
examples.trans: Calm down, Mazen, the room is ready.
A cup of anise tea calms the nerves.

meanings.note: MSA feminine demonstrative used in Mazen's stiff written draft.

examples.trans: We used the word هذه.
This is another هذه.

meanings.note: Feminine demonstrative used more in formal speech or by older/Bedouin speakers.

examples.trans: This car is new.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على هذي.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with هذي.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بهرب, بيهرب).

examples.trans: Why did the person run off without his bag?
You left the bag on the doorstep and bolted!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بهز, بيهز).

examples.trans: My brother nodded his head in agreement!
The breeze shook the jasmine branches.

meanings.note: Very common adverb denoting the current time in Jordan and Palestine.

examples.trans: I want to go now.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على هسا.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with هسا.

meanings.note: The word 'هل' (هل) means 'هل'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: العسل الدافي مبين دبق وبلزق بطريقة بتجنن، بس هل هو وصفة محلية قديمة؟
examples.trans: Warm honey sounds delightfully sticky, but is it an old-fashioned local recipe?
This is هل.

meanings.note: High-frequency Levantine word for 'now' (contracted from هاد الوقت).

examples.trans: We have to go to class right now.
I feel a bit relieved now.

meanings.note: Signature Levantine word for 'now / right now' (pronounced halla' in Amman).

examples.trans: A taxi just stopped at the door now.
We will check the tag right now.

meanings.note: The word 'هلق' (hallaq) means 'now'. It is a common adv in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: هلق شوفوا منيح عالكرت الأول عشان نشوف شو الرمز اللي لازم نلاقيه.
examples.trans: Now look closely at Card One to see what symbol we need to find.
This is هلق.

هم.gloss: to matter; worry (ولا يهمك never mind / do not worry)

meanings.en: to matter; worry (ولا يهمك never mind / do not worry)
meanings.note: Used especially in the warm Jordanian reassurance ولا يهمك! ('never mind! / do not worry at all!').

examples.trans: Do not worry at all, sir, it is nothing!
What matters to us is the guests' comfort.

meanings.note: Sound Form I verb (بهمس / همست) from root ه-م-س ('soft sound/whispering').

examples.trans: Word whispered to me that you opened the box.

examples.text: همست بإذنها عشان ما حدا يسمع.
examples.trans: She whispered in her ear so nobody would hear.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian pronoun 'they' for people or things.

examples.trans: Are they in your jacket pocket?
They live at the end of the street.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: Enjoy your tea and cake!
May the home be filled with goodness and joy.

meanings.note: Everyday word for 'there / over there' (لهناك 'over there').

examples.trans: Mazen has put old boxes over there.
Can you run over there and back?

meanings.note: Refers to the field of engineering or geometry.

examples.trans: He is studying engineering at the university.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على هندسة.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with هندسة.

meanings.note: The word 'هنيك' (hneek) means 'there'. It is a common adv in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: هادا سهل؛ أقدم شجرة زيزفون موجودة هنيك بالنص.
examples.trans: That is easy; the oldest linden tree is right there in the centre.
This is هنيك.

meanings.note: Third person masculine pronoun.

examples.trans: He is the one who said so.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على هو.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with هو.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: A little air got into the old pipes.
Morning air in Amman is crisp and clean.

meanings.note: The word 'هواء' (هواء) means 'هواء'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: سما صافية، ليالي دافية، وهبات هواء ربيعية نشطة رح تضرب البلد يوم الجمعة.
examples.trans: Clear skies, warm evenings, and brisk spring wind gusts sweeping across town on Friday.
This is هواء.

meanings.note: Feminine noun (plural هوايات) from هوى ('to be fond of / love').

examples.text: الرسم بالألوان المائية أحلى هواية عندي.
examples.trans: Watercolour painting is my favourite hobby.
What are your favourite hobbies in your free time?

meanings.en: whoosh! phew! (sound of blowing air or a gust passing)
meanings.note: Expressive sound word imitating wind rushing or a sigh of relief.

examples.text: هوف! والله الورقة كانت رح تطير.
examples.trans: Phew! Honestly the sheet was about to fly away.

examples.text: سمعنا هوف الهوا لما فتحنا باب السطح.
examples.trans: We heard the whoosh of the wind when we opened the roof door.

meanings.note: Standard adverb for physical location.

examples.trans: Put the things here, please.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على هون.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with هون.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian pronoun 'she' or 'it' (feminine).

examples.trans: Take a piece of bread while it is hot.
Family is what remains.

meanings.note: Extremely common adverb used to express similarity or concluding a statement.

examples.text: هيك الحياة، يوم الك ويوم عليك.
examples.trans: Such is life, one day for you and one day against you.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على هيك.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with هيك.

meanings.note: Colloquial attention-getting exclamation, used playfully among friends or family.

examples.trans: Hey! Tariq drove the bus himself!
Hey, where are you going so fast?

meanings.note: Presentative pronoun used to point out a group of people or objects.

examples.trans: Where are the kids? Here they are playing outside.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على هيهم.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with هيهم.

meanings.note: The word 'هيو' (هيو) means 'هيو'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: هيو القاضي مازن أخد الشوكة الأولى—ولا حدا يحكي ولا كلمة!
examples.trans: Here goes Judge Mazen with forkful number one—nobody say a word!
This is هيو.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian presentative word ('here is! / look!') pointing to someone or something right now; takes suffixes (هيهم hayy-hum 'here they are!').

examples.text: هي تاكسي وقف عند الباب هلا!
examples.trans: Look, a taxi just stopped at the door!
Here they come down the stairs!

meanings.note: The universal coordinating conjunction.

examples.trans: I bought bread and milk.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على و.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with و.

meanings.note: Conjunction and indefinite noun.

examples.trans: Bring a thread and a needle with you.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على وإبرة.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with وإبرة.

meanings.note: Conjunction attached to the first person plural pronoun.

examples.trans: A problem happened while we were going home.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على وإحنا.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with وإحنا.

meanings.note: Introduces a playful warning or consequence ('or else…').

examples.trans: Drink your coffee now or else it'll go cold!

examples.text: خبي قطعة تارت لطارق وإلا بيزعل منا!
examples.trans: Save a slice of tart for Tariq or else he'll be cross with us!

meanings.note: Refers to the front of a building or a digital interface.

examples.trans: The building's facade is built of stone.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على واجهة.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with واجهة.

meanings.note: Cardinal number or used as an indefinite pronoun.

examples.trans: There is someone asking about you.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على واحد.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with واحد.

meanings.note: The word 'واحدة' (واحدة) means 'واحدة'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: كبست الجرس مرة واحدة فوق يا مازن، وسلكك اللطيف رن مرتين متل العادة.
examples.trans: I pressed the bell once upstairs, Mazen, and your friendly wire rang twice as usual.
This is واحدة.

meanings.note: The word 'واخبزيه' (واخبزيه) means 'واخبزيه'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: اطوي التوت الكامل شوي شوي بخليط اللوز واخبزيه أربعين دقيقة ليصير لونه ذهبي.
examples.trans: Fold whole berries gently into the almond batter and bake forty minutes until golden.
This is واخبزيه.

meanings.note: Conjunction attached to a feminine imperative verb.

examples.trans: Hold the box and lift it up.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على وارفعي.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with وارفعي.

meanings.note: Active participle of ورم ('swell up').

examples.text: كويس إن كاحلك مش وارم، التلج فاد علطول.
examples.trans: It's good that your ankle isn't swollen—the ice helped right away.

examples.text: إذا ضلت الرجل وارمة الصبح منروح عالدكتور.
examples.trans: If the foot is still swollen in the morning, we'll see the doctor.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: واسعة, plural: واسعين).

examples.trans: Careful, the pitcher's spout is wide!
The house's courtyard is spacious and sunny.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: واصلة, plural: واصلين).

examples.text: ريحة القرفة الدافية واصلة للطابق التاني!
examples.trans: The warm cinnamon scent reaches all the way to the second floor!
The bus is pulling into the station now.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: واضحة, plural: واضحين).

examples.trans: A sincere, clear sentence from the heart.
The address is clear on the card.

meanings.note: Feminine adjective used for clarity in speech or vision.

examples.trans: The picture is not very clear.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على واضحة.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with واضحة.

meanings.note: Feminine command to push or press.

examples.trans: Enter the password and press enter.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على واضغطي.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with واضغطي.

meanings.note: Refers to retrieving or pulling out an object.

examples.trans: I want to open the bag and take it out.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على واطولها.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with واطولها.

meanings.note: Command used for folding clothes or paper.

examples.trans: Wash the clothes and fold the garments.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على واطوي.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with واطوي.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: واطية, plural: واطيين).

examples.text: انتبه على راسك من الخشب الواطي.
examples.trans: Watch your head on the low wooden beam.
They spoke in a low voice for the guests' sake.

meanings.note: Form III verb from و-ف-ق; takes على for the thing agreed to.

examples.text: وافق مازن عالخطة أول ما شاف الأرقام.
examples.trans: Mazen agreed to the plan as soon as he saw the numbers.

examples.text: كل الجيران وافقوا يحضروا حفلة الشاي.
examples.trans: All the neighbours agreed to attend the tea concert.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: واقفة, plural: واقفين).

examples.trans: There is nobody standing in the courtyard.
They stood face to face under the tree.

meanings.note: The word 'واقية' (واقية) means 'واقية'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: لاحظوا كيف الشوكة بتدخل دغري من غير شاكوش أو نظارات واقية.
examples.trans: Notice how the fork glides straight through without a hammer or safety goggles.
This is واقية.

meanings.note: Refers to a ticket or a bank card.

examples.trans: I took the passport and the card.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على والبطاقة.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with والبطاقة.

meanings.note: Usually refers to mobile network coverage.

examples.trans: The internet is excellent and the coverage is strong here.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على والتغطية.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with والتغطية.

meanings.note: Refers to something feminine colored gold.

examples.trans: I took the silver and the golden medal.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على والذهبية.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with والذهبية.

meanings.note: The word 'والسبت' (والسبت) means 'والسبت'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: استنى—شيكت توقعات الجو للويكند تبعت عصر الجمعة والسبت يا مازن؟
examples.trans: Wait—have you checked the weekend weather forecast for Friday and Saturday afternoon, Mazen?
This is والسبت.

والشمال.gloss: and the left / and the north

meanings.en: and the left / and the north
meanings.note: Can refer to the left direction or northern region.

examples.text: اطلع دغري وبعدين لف يمين والشمال.
examples.trans: Go straight and then turn right and left.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على والشمال.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with والشمال.

meanings.note: Refers to the morning meal.

examples.trans: We drank coffee and the breakfast was delicious.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على والفطور.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with والفطور.

meanings.note: Everyday oath used earnestly to swear one is telling the truth (والله ما حكيت إشي) or surprisedly in والله جد؟ ('oh really?').

examples.trans: I swear I'm telling the truth.
Honestly, I'm glad to see you.

meanings.note: Refers to the nut, also used metaphorically for something excellent.

examples.trans: We ate fruits and green almonds.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على واللوز.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with واللوز.

meanings.note: The word 'والمليسة' (والمليسة) means 'والمليسة'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: شوفوا بالزبط بين هدول الغصنين الناشفين تبعون نعناع الحديقة والمليسة.
examples.trans: Look right between these two dry sprigs of garden mint and lemon balm.
This is والمليسة.

meanings.note: The word 'واو' (واو) means 'واو'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: واو، قاسي! هلق ما ضل عندنا غير صينية رقم تلاتة اللي عليها طبقة العسل الدافي!
examples.trans: Wow, brutal! Now we only have Tin Three with the warm honey glaze left!
This is واو.

meanings.note: The word 'وبرش' (وبرش) means 'وبرش'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: غمضي عيونك وتنفسي: نعناع الحديقة، وبرش برتقال حلو، وعسل ذهبي!
examples.trans: Close your eyes and breathe in: garden mint, sweet orange zest, and golden honey!
This is وبرش.

meanings.note: The word 'وبلزق' (وبلزق) means 'وبلزق'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: العسل الدافي مبين دبق وبلزق بطريقة بتجنن، بس هل هو وصفة محلية قديمة؟
examples.trans: Warm honey sounds delightfully sticky, but is it an old-fashioned local recipe?
This is وبلزق.

meanings.note: The word 'وبنختبر' (وبنختبر) means 'وبنختبر'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: لعد يوم الجمعة الصبح بنطلع عالبلكونة بحبل متين وبنختبر كل عقدة!
examples.trans: Then Friday morning we climb onto that balcony with sturdy cord and test every knot!
This is وبنختبر.

meanings.note: Refers to flapping wings or hovering. The spelling appears to be a colloquial variant or typo for بيرفرف.

examples.trans: The bird is flying and fluttering its wings.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على وبيرفوف.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with وبيرفوف.

meanings.note: The word 'وبيلمع' (وبيلمع) means 'وبيلمع'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: أكيد! العسل الدافي بضل طري وبيلمع من غير ما يحمض أو يصير قاسي متل الحجر!
examples.trans: Of course! Warm honey stays soft and glossy without turning sour or rock hard!
This is وبيلمع.

meanings.en: peg; wooden or metal stake; cleat for tying rope
meanings.note: Masculine noun (plural أوتاد) used for tent pegs, wall pegs, and posts for securing ropes.

examples.text: لف الحبل حوالين الوتد الثابت بالزاوية.
examples.trans: Wrap the rope around the sturdy peg in the corner.

examples.text: دقّينا أوتاد الخيمة بالأرض قبل الغروب.
examples.trans: We drove the tent pegs into the ground before sunset.

meanings.note: Stretched wire or gut string on a piano, oud, or violin.

examples.text: المطرقة بتضرب الأوتار التلاتة فبيطلع صوت صافي.
examples.trans: The hammer strikes the three strings and produces a clear note.

examples.text: كل وتر بالبيانو مشدود بدقة عالية.
examples.trans: Every string inside the piano is tensioned with great precision.

meanings.note: The word 'وترفض' (وترفض) means 'وترفض'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: معنا عشر دقايق بالزبط قبل ما تبرد الكيكة وترفض أي طبقة تلميع دافية!
examples.trans: We have exactly ten minutes before the cake cools down and rejects any warm glaze!
This is وترفض.

meanings.note: The word 'وتنفسي' (وتنفسي) means 'وتنفسي'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: غمضي عيونك وتنفسي: نعناع الحديقة، وبرش برتقال حلو، وعسل ذهبي!
examples.trans: Close your eyes and breathe in: garden mint, sweet orange zest, and golden honey!
This is وتنفسي.

meanings.note: The word 'وتنين' (وتنين) means 'وتنين'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: صفوهم بانتظام على طاولة القهوة يا زياد—صينية رقم واحد عاليسار، وتنين بالنص.
examples.trans: Line them up neatly on the coffee table, Ziad—Tin One on the left, Two in the middle.
This is وتنين.

meanings.note: Refers to mulberries or any kind of berries.

examples.trans: We brought strawberries and berries from the market.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على وتوت.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with وتوت.

meanings.note: The word 'وثقي' (وثقي) means 'وثقي'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: وثقي فيي! قولي لـ سعاد تشم الورقة محل ما كان كرت الوصفة محطوط!
examples.trans: Trust me! Tell Suad to smell the paper where the recipe card rested!
This is وثقي.

meanings.note: The word 'وجديد' (وجديد) means 'وجديد'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: إنتي شجاعة يا سلمى. إذا عمل كشرة تلميع النحاس، رح نضطر نعيد كل شي من أول وجديد!
examples.trans: You are brave, Salma. If he makes the brass-polish face, we start all over again!
This is وجديد.

meanings.note: The word 'وجرب' (وجرب) means 'وجرب'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: حلو كتير! ماشي يا مدير، نظف تمك بشاي أسود وجرب صينية رقم تنين!
examples.trans: Too sweet! Okay, Boss, wash your palate with black tea and try Tin Two!
This is وجرب.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أوجاع.

examples.trans: Tiny numbers give me a headache!

examples.text: راح وجع الراس بعد فنجان القهوة.
examples.trans: The headache went away after a cup of coffee.

meanings.note: Common expression indicating spatial proximity to a masculine object.

examples.trans: Put the chair and beside it the table.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على وجنبه.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with وجنبه.

وجه.gloss: face; top surface (وجه لوجه face to face)

meanings.en: face; top surface (وجه لوجه face to face)
meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: وجوه.

examples.trans: They stood face to face under the tree.
The top of the cake turned golden in the oven.

meanings.note: Verbal noun: وجود نوف معهم ('Noaf's presence / having Noaf with them').

examples.trans: Having you with us makes us happy.
Thank you for being by my side.

meanings.note: Form II verb disambiguated with shadda from noun وجه ('face').

examples.text: خلينا نوجه المروحة لباب الساحة عشان الهوا يتحرك.
examples.trans: Let's point the fan toward the courtyard door so the air circulates.

examples.text: وجه الضو عاللوحة عشان نشوف الحروف بوضوح.
examples.trans: Point the light at the sign so we can see the letters clearly.

meanings.note: Feminine counterpart of الواحد when speaking generically about a girl or woman (لازم الوحدة تشوفه بعينها).

examples.trans: A girl has to stand up for herself.
Each one of us has a role.

meanings.note: Can be used as a noun meaning 'and a stamp' or a verb in the past tense 'and he stamped/sealed'.

examples.trans: He gave me a paper and stamped on it.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على وختم.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with وختم.

meanings.note: Imperative verb used to instruct a group of people to take something.

examples.trans: Come and take your belongings.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على وخذوا.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with وخذوا.

meanings.note: Used to describe something feminine that is light in weight or mild in intensity.

examples.trans: The bag is small and light.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على وخفيفة.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with وخفيفة.

meanings.note: Everyday item, combined with the conjunction 'wa' (and).

examples.trans: I brought a pen and a notebook.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على ودفتر.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with ودفتر.

meanings.note: Very common spatial preposition in Jordanian Arabic.

examples.trans: The car is behind the house.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على ورا.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with ورا.

meanings.note: Preposition with a 3rd person masculine singular pronoun suffix.

examples.trans: Walk behind him.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على وراه.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with وراه.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: ورد.

examples.trans: We walked past the flower stall.
The scent of roses and jasmine filled the courtyard.

meanings.note: Singular form for a flower, highly used in everyday speech.

examples.trans: I picked a rose from the garden.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على وردة.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with وردة.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: ورشات.

examples.trans: There is a brass lamp in my workshop downstairs.
The old bag is from my grandfather's workshop.

meanings.note: The word 'ورفعتوا' (ورفعتوا) means 'ورفعتوا'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: أهلا فيكم بمختبر كيكة التوت تبع يوم الأحد يا متدربين! غسلتوا إيديكم ورفعتوا أكمامكم؟
examples.trans: Welcome to the Sunday Berry Cake Laboratory, apprentices! Hands washed and sleeves rolled?
This is ورفعتوا.

meanings.note: Collective noun used for paper material or leaves of a tree.

examples.text: جيب لي شوية ورق أكتب عليهم.
examples.trans: Bring me some paper to write on.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على ورق.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with ورق.

meanings.note: The word 'ورقائق' (ورقائق) means 'ورقائق'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: معلقتين من العسل الدافي، وبرش برتقال، ورقائق لوز محمصة!
examples.trans: Two spoons of warm honey, grated orange zest, and toasted almond flakes!
This is ورقائق.

meanings.note: One sheet of paper or one leaf; the collective ورق means paper in general.

examples.trans: Write your number down for me on a piece of paper.
The tree leaf turns yellow in autumn.

meanings.note: Masculine word formed from ورق ('paper'), meaning 'made of paper'.

examples.trans: We used the word ورقي.
This is another ورقي.

meanings.note: Medical/everyday noun for swelling or a bump.

examples.trans: We used the word ورم.
This is another ورم.

meanings.note: Masculine singular loanword for wood varnish, with the Arabic definite article.

examples.trans: We used the word ورنيش.
This is another ورنيش.

meanings.note: Refers to a scent, often used when describing food or perfume.

examples.trans: The food is delicious and the smell is appetizing.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على وريحة.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with وريحة.

meanings.note: Form II verb for distributing flyers, portions, or kitchen tasks.

examples.text: سلمى قعدت عالكرسي ووزعت الشغل عالكل.
examples.trans: Salma sat in the chair and assigned tasks to everyone.

examples.text: نور وزعت كروت الدعوة عجيران الحارة.
examples.trans: Nour handed out invitation cards to the neighbourhood.

meanings.note: Used for physical weight on a foot, scale measurements, or poetic meter.

examples.text: لا تحطي أي وزن عكاحلك اليوم أبدا.
examples.trans: Don't put any weight on your ankle at all today.

examples.text: قيس وزن الطحين والسكر بالميزان قبل العجن.
examples.trans: Weigh the flour and sugar on the scale before kneading.

meanings.note: The word 'وزهور' (وزهور) means 'وزهور'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: شوفوا ورقة الذهب المطبوعة عالغلاف الأخضر الباهت: أعشاب وزهور الساحة.
examples.trans: Look at the gold leaf stamped on the faded green cover: Courtyard Herbs and Blossoms.
This is وزهور.

meanings.note: Arabic verb وزّع meaning 'to distribute' or 'hand out'.

examples.trans: We used the word وزّع.
This is another وزّع.

meanings.note: The word 'وسجل' (وسجل) means 'وسجل'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: كول قد ما بدك يا مازن، وسجل أربع كيكات كاملات ليوم السبت!
examples.trans: Eat all you want, Mazen, and write down four full cakes for Saturday!
This is وسجل.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أوساط.

examples.trans: We went down to downtown in the morning.
The table is right in the middle of the courtyard.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian adjective from وسط ('middle'); pairs naturally with المفتاح الوسطاني and ري الوسطى.

examples.text: المفتاح الوسطاني بالبيانو كان عالق من الرطوبة.
examples.trans: The middle key on the piano was stuck from dampness.

examples.text: الطاولة الوسطانية بالساحة بتاخد أحلى شمس.
examples.trans: The middle table in the courtyard catches the nicest sunshine.

وسع.gloss: to fit; hold; have room for

meanings.en: to fit; hold; have room for
meanings.note: Says how much a place holds: السيارة بتوسع خمس أشخاص 'the car fits five people'. Related to واسع, wide.

examples.trans: The bag doesn't hold all the books.
The table easily fits six.

meanings.note: The word 'وسلكك' (وسلكك) means 'وسلكك'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: كبست الجرس مرة واحدة فوق يا مازن، وسلكك اللطيف رن مرتين متل العادة.
examples.trans: I pressed the bell once upstairs, Mazen, and your friendly wire rang twice as usual.
This is وسلكك.

meanings.note: Classic adjective on the فَعِيل pattern from root و-س-م ('mark of beauty').

examples.trans: The young man in the photo is very handsome.
His clothes were neat and he looked handsome.

meanings.note: Everyday Levantine pronunciation of وجه (wajh, 'face'), heard constantly in Amman speech.

examples.trans: His face was beaming in the photo.
Wash your face with cold water.

meanings.note: Often used when describing the weather.

examples.trans: Today the weather is nice and the sun is out.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على وشمس.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with وشمس.

meanings.note: Third person plural past tense, describing the act of speaking softly.

examples.trans: The students whispered in the classroom.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على وشوشوا.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with وشوشوا.

meanings.note: The word 'وشوفوا' (وشوفوا) means 'وشوفوا'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: وشوفوا جذع شجرة الظل تبعت ساحتنا—في حلقة بتشبهها معلقة عالي!
examples.trans: And look at the trunk of our courtyard shade tree—a matching ring high up!
This is وشوفوا.

meanings.note: Used for both a doctor's prescription and a cooking recipe.

examples.trans: The doctor gave me the medicine prescription.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على وصفة.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with وصفة.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بوصل, بيوصل).

examples.trans: Our guest arrived right on the second!
An official letter arrived at noon.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: وصلات.

examples.trans: Shine the flashlight on the pipe joint.
We tightened the brass fitting with the wrench.

meanings.note: Depending on context, it can mean 'she arrived' or 'I arrived'. Most commonly 'she arrived' with 'wislet'.

examples.trans: She arrived on time.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على وصلت.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with وصلت.

meanings.en: arrival; reaching a place or time
meanings.note: Masculine verbal noun (masdar) of وصل ('to arrive/reach').

examples.text: لازم نخلص كل شي قبل وصول الضيوف.
examples.trans: We need to finish everything before the guests' arrival.
Thank God for your safe arrival.

meanings.note: The word 'وصينية' (وصينية) means 'وصينية'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: بالزبط يا زياد. وصينية رقم تلاتة رح تاخد الورقة الرابحة تبعتي: دهنة خفيفة من العسل الدافي.
examples.trans: Exactly, Ziad. And Tin Three gets my wild card: a thin brush of warm honey.
This is وصينية.

meanings.note: هاد الوضع refers to an awkward or tense arrangement.

examples.trans: The situation at school is tense today.
I'm not comfortable with this situation.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: I can hear you clearly on the phone now.
He explained the idea with complete clarity.

meanings.note: The word 'وطابقوا' (وطابقوا) means 'وطابقوا'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: اوقفوا بالزبط جنب طاولة رقم واحد وطابقوا رسمة الكروت الأربعة مع حيطنا اللي فوق.
examples.trans: Stand right beside table one and match the four-card drawing to our upstairs wall.
This is وطابقوا.

meanings.note: Past tense verb combined with 'and', directed at a group.

examples.trans: Did you finish the work and go out early?

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على وطلعتوا.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with وطلعتوا.

meanings.en: to lower; to turn down (heat, volume)
meanings.note: Form II defective verb (بوطّي / وطّيت) from root و-ط-أ; used for turning down a stove flame or voice.

examples.trans: Turn down the gas a little under the pot.
Lower the volume, the baby is sleeping.

meanings.note: In Levantine school talk, وظيفة means 'homework' (كنت بعمل وظيفة) — a false friend if you only know its adult meaning 'job'!

examples.trans: We have math homework for tomorrow.
I finished the homework before bed.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: وعود.

examples.trans: We will come next week, promise!
He kept his promise and arrived on time.

meanings.note: The word 'وعسل' (وعسل) means 'وعسل'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: غمضي عيونك وتنفسي: نعناع الحديقة، وبرش برتقال حلو، وعسل ذهبي!
examples.trans: Close your eyes and breathe in: garden mint, sweet orange zest, and golden honey!
This is وعسل.

meanings.note: Used in compound numbers (e.g., twenty-one, twenty-two).

examples.trans: He is twenty-five years old.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على وعشرين.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with وعشرين.

meanings.note: Preposition used to indicate position or direction, attached to 'and'.

examples.text: حطيت الكتاب ع الطاولة وعلى الكرسي.
examples.trans: I put the book on the table and on the chair.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على وعلى.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with وعلى.

meanings.note: The word 'وعمته' (وعمته) means 'وعمته'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: هادا الكتاب كان أصلا لـ رامي وعمته قبل ما يوصل لرف الإعارة!
examples.trans: This book actually belonged to Rami and his aunt before it reached the lending shelf!
This is وعمته.

meanings.note: Common noun for room, prefixed with 'and'.

examples.trans: The house has a living room and a bedroom.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على وغرفة.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with وغرفة.

meanings.note: The word 'وفانيليا' (وفانيليا) means 'وفانيليا'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: استنتاج بسيط! صينية رقم واحد رح تاخد طبقة سكر وفانيليا دافية؛ هادا تشطيب كلاسيكي.
examples.trans: Simple deduction! Tin One gets a warm vanilla sugar glaze; that is a classic finish.
This is وفانيليا.

meanings.note: The word 'وفى' (boofi) means 'I keep/fulfill'. It is a common verb in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: شوفوا: راقبوا بريد المكتب الأمامي هالاسبوع، لأني بوفي بوعودي!
examples.trans: Look: Watch your front-desk mail this week, because I keep my promises!
This is وفى.

meanings.note: Can mean 'and in' or 'and there is' depending on context.

examples.text: رحنا على السوق وفي ناس كثير.
examples.trans: We went to the market and there are many people.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على وفي.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with وفي.

وفيه.gloss: and in it / and there is in it

meanings.en: and in it / and there is in it
meanings.note: Refers to something containing another thing, or simply 'and there is'.

examples.trans: The box is big and there are things in it.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على وفيه.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with وفيه.

meanings.note: Form II verb from و-ف-ر; active participle موفر / موفرين ('saving, ahead on budget').

examples.text: خصم الدزينة وفر علينا مبلغ حلو.
examples.trans: The dozen discount saved us a nice amount.

examples.text: لما ندهن الشيش بإيدنا بنوفر بالميزانية.
examples.trans: When we paint the shutters ourselves, we save on the budget.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: He greeted the guests with calm dignity.
His speech carries wisdom and poise.

meanings.note: General term for time or duration.

examples.trans: I don't have time to go out today.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على وقت.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with وقت.

meanings.note: Time possessed by a second person masculine.

examples.trans: Take your time and don't rush.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على وقتك.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with وقتك.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بوقع, بيوقع).

examples.text: نظارتك وقعت عن أنفك من الفرحة!
examples.trans: Your glasses fell off your nose for joy!

examples.text: أي نزل سحري هاد اللي وقعت فيه؟
examples.trans: What magical inn is this that you stumbled into?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بوقف, بيوقف).

examples.trans: A yellow taxi stopped outside the gate!
My heart stopped at page one!

meanings.note: Past tense, second person feminine singular.

examples.trans: Why did you stop in the middle of the road?

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على وقفتي.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with وقفتي.

meanings.note: The word 'وقلم' (وقلم) means 'وقلم'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: ناوليني دفتر الورق تبعي وقلم النجار الرصاص من جنب الإبريق يا نور.
examples.trans: Hand me my paper notebook and my carpenter pencil from beside the teapot, Nour.
This is وقلم.

meanings.note: Intensive adjective (فَعُول) from وقار ('dignity/calm poise'), describing quiet grace and gravitas.

examples.trans: That young man with the dignified appearance.
The professor is dignified and everyone respects him.

meanings.note: The word 'وقولي' (وقولي) means 'وقولي'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: أنا راكضة! دفي الكيكة يا سلمى، وقولي لـ مازن يستنى بصبر!
examples.trans: I am running! Keep the cake warm, Salma, and tell Mazen to wait patiently!
This is وقولي.

meanings.note: Past tense Arabic verb meaning 'to sign' a contract or lease.

examples.trans: We used the word وقّع.
This is another وقّع.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بوقف, بيوقف).

examples.text: وقفوا كل شي، قديش الساعة هلا؟
examples.trans: Stop everything — what time is it right now?
The driver pulled the car up by the kerb.

meanings.note: The word 'وكيكتنا' (وكيكتنا) means 'وكيكتنا'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: نشم صفحة قديمة ومغبرة وكيكتنا الممتازة عم تبرد؟ هادا جنون رسمي.
examples.trans: Smell an old dusty page while our best cake goes cold? That is absolute madness.
This is وكيكتنا.

meanings.note: The word 'ول' (ول) means 'ول'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.
