examples.text: ول يا نور! عم تلحقي حرامي، ولا حدا أكل فليفلة حارة نية بالغلط؟
examples.trans: Whoa, Nour! Are you chasing a thief, or did someone accidentally eat a raw hot pepper?
This is ول.

meanings.note: Used in negative constructions or as a strong negative emphasis.

examples.trans: Not even one of them came.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على ولا.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with ولا.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: ولاد.

examples.trans: The two boys learned piano together.
May you be blessed, my dear boys.

meanings.note: Used to describe a group of people holding something.

examples.trans: The kids are playing and holding each other's hands.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على وماسكين.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with وماسكين.

meanings.note: The word 'ومبين' (ومبين) means 'ومبين'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: وهادا القاضي مازن لابس نظارات القراءة تبعونه، ومبين جدي كتير الصراحة.
examples.trans: And here is Judge Mazen with his reading glasses on, looking very serious indeed.
This is ومبين.

meanings.note: The word 'ومرطبان' (ومرطبان) means 'ومرطبان'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: ولا واحد منهم! عم نخبز الكيكة الغامضة تبعت التلاتين سنة ومرطبان العسل فاضي!
examples.trans: Neither! We are baking the thirty-year-old mystery cake and the honey jar is empty!
This is ومرطبان.

meanings.note: Indicates association or possession related to a feminine entity.

examples.trans: She went to the market and her mother was with her.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على ومعها.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with ومعها.

meanings.note: The word 'ومغبرة' (ومغبرة) means 'ومغبرة'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: نشم صفحة قديمة ومغبرة وكيكتنا الممتازة عم تبرد؟ هادا جنون رسمي.
examples.trans: Smell an old dusty page while our best cake goes cold? That is absolute madness.
This is ومغبرة.

meanings.note: Passive participle feminine form, often used for gifts or food.

examples.trans: The gift is ready and wrapped.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على ومغلفة.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with ومغلفة.

meanings.note: Can mean a desk or an office room.

examples.trans: We rented an apartment and an office.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على ومكتب.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with ومكتب.

meanings.note: Used to describe something that lacks moisture.

examples.trans: The bread is old and dry.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على وناشف.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with وناشف.

meanings.note: Used heavily in telling time (e.g., 'and a half' for 30 minutes past the hour).

examples.trans: The time is five and a half (five thirty).

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على ونص.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with ونص.

meanings.note: Refers to half of a feminine object or quantity.

examples.text: أكلت التفاحة ونصها الثاني لسه موجود.
examples.trans: I ate the apple and the other half is still there.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على ونصها.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with ونصها.

meanings.note: The word 'وهادا' (وهادا) means 'وهادا'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: وهادا القاضي مازن لابس نظارات القراءة تبعونه، ومبين جدي كتير الصراحة.
examples.trans: And here is Judge Mazen with his reading glasses on, looking very serious indeed.
This is وهادا.

meanings.note: Demonstrative pronoun used for masculine objects.

examples.trans: This is my friend and this is his brother.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على وهاذ.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with وهاذ.

meanings.note: The word 'وهبات' (وهبات) means 'وهبات'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: سما صافية، ليالي دافية، وهبات هواء ربيعية نشطة رح تضرب البلد يوم الجمعة.
examples.trans: Clear skies, warm evenings, and brisk spring wind gusts sweeping across town on Friday.
This is وهبات.

meanings.note: The word 'وهلق' (وهلق) means 'وهلق'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: وهلق يا مازن؟ احكيلنا بصراحة—هل هالكيكة بتستاهل تنحط على طاولة الذكرى يوم السبت؟
examples.trans: Well, Mazen? Tell us honestly—is that worthy of our Saturday anniversary table?
This is وهلق.

meanings.note: Used as a collective noun for paper or leaves.

examples.trans: He gave me a pen and paper.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على وورق.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with وورق.

meanings.note: The word 'ويختار' (ويختار) means 'ويختار'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: أنا متوترة! مين رح يذوقهم ويختار الفايز المطلق؟
examples.trans: I am nervous! Who is going to taste-test them and pick the absolute winner?
This is ويختار.

meanings.note: Appears in the dramatic warning يا ويل البنت اللي... ('woe to the girl who... / heaven help the girl who...').

examples.text: يا ويل اللي بيتأخر عن الحصة.
examples.trans: Woe to whoever is late to class.
We're in trouble if the teacher heard us.

meanings.note: The standard interrogative adverb for location in the dialect.

examples.trans: Where are you going?

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على وين.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with وين.

meanings.note: Present tense verb, also used for future with the prefix 'b'.

examples.text: رح يطلع من الشغل وييجي عندنا.
examples.trans: He will leave work and come to us.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على وييجي.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with وييجي.

meanings.note: Takes ب- for the thing promised: وعدته بغرفة 'I promised him a room'.

examples.text: خليني أحزر. وعدت حدا بغرفة مش موجودة عندنا؟
examples.trans: Let me guess. You promised somebody a room we do not have?
I promised you lemon cake on Friday.

meanings.note: Vocative particle used when addressing someone directly.

examples.trans: Oh Ahmed, come here.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على يا.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with يا.

meanings.note: Third person masculine singular verb with a first person plural object pronoun.

examples.trans: I want the bus to take us to the university.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على ياخذنا.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with ياخذنا.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: ياسمين.

examples.trans: The jasmine vine climbs above the door.
The evening scent of jasmine lifts the spirit.

meanings.note: Collective masculine noun (unit noun ياقوتة 'one ruby'). Used metaphorically for deep ruby-red colour in berries or glaze.

examples.trans: The colour of the red berries is like ruby.

examples.text: عندها خاتم فضة عليه حجر ياقوت.
examples.trans: She has a silver ring with a ruby stone on it.

meanings.note: Often means to quit doing something or to stop functioning.

examples.trans: He must quit smoking.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على يبطل.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with يبطل.

meanings.note: The word 'يتخانق' (يتخانق) means 'يتخانق'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: لا. الليمون عم يتخانق بقوة مع التوت المستوي. لازم يكونوا بكيكات مختلفة.
examples.trans: No. The lemon fights aggressively with the ripe berries. They belong in different cakes.
This is يتخانق.

meanings.note: Refers to abandoning or leaving a feminine object or person.

examples.trans: He decided to leave it and go.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على يتركها.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with يتركها.

meanings.note: Colloquial verb meaning to trip over something or for a plan to fall apart.

examples.trans: Careful that he doesn't trip on the stairs.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على يتفركش.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with يتفركش.

meanings.note: The word 'يتنفس' (يتنفس) means 'يتنفس'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: خلينا ناخده طوالي لـ سلمى بغرفة تسعة قبل ما حدا يتنفس بقوة!
examples.trans: Let us carry it straight to Salma in Room Nine before anyone breathes too hard!
This is يتنفس.

meanings.note: The word 'يحكي' (يحكي) means 'يحكي'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: هيو القاضي مازن أخد الشوكة الأولى—ولا حدا يحكي ولا كلمة!
examples.trans: Here goes Judge Mazen with forkful number one—nobody say a word!
This is يحكي.

meanings.note: The word 'يحمض' (يحمض) means 'يحمض'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: أكيد! العسل الدافي بضل طري وبيلمع من غير ما يحمض أو يصير قاسي متل الحجر!
examples.trans: Of course! Warm honey stays soft and glossy without turning sour or rock hard!
This is يحمض.

meanings.note: The word 'يختبر' (يختبر) means 'يختبر'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: لا تخاف يا مدير؛ احنا بنعرف أساس الكيكة، عشان هيك مطبخي رح يختبر تلات طبقات تلميع!
examples.trans: Do not panic, boss; we know the cake base, so my kitchen will test three glazes!
This is يختبر.

meanings.note: For door handles and bag handles, Jordanian speakers often say يد الباب / عاليد alongside إيد for the human hand.

examples.text: ارفعي يد الباب أول وبعدين ادفعي.
examples.trans: Lift the door handle first, then push.

examples.text: في بطاقة مربوطة على يد الشنتة.
examples.trans: There is a tag tied to the handle of the bag.

meanings.note: Standard verb for entering.

examples.trans: Let him enter the room.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على يدخل.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with يدخل.

meanings.note: The word 'يدهنوا' (يدهنوا) means 'يدهنوا'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: جداتنا كانوا يدهنوا عسل على معجنات المكسرات من قبل ما يكون في إشي اسمه سكر فانيليا!
examples.trans: Our grandmothers brushed honey over nut pastries long before vanilla sugar existed!
This is يدهنوا.

meanings.note: Nisba adjective from يد ('hand') using the glide -aw- before -ي; used for crafts and handmade notebooks.

examples.trans: Also the little notebook is handmade.
We love handmade embroidery work.

meanings.note: The word 'يذوقهم' (يذوقهم) means 'يذوقهم'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: أنا متوترة! مين رح يذوقهم ويختار الفايز المطلق؟
examples.trans: I am nervous! Who is going to taste-test them and pick the absolute winner?
This is يذوقهم.

meanings.note: 'yruh' means 'he goes', 'yrawweh' often means 'he goes home'.

examples.trans: He wants to go to the market.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على يروح.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with يروح.

meanings.note: The word 'يس' (يس) means 'يس'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: يس! عشرة من عشرة بقلم مازن بتسوى تلات ميداليات ذهبية!
examples.trans: YES! Ten out of ten in Mazen pencil is worth three gold medals!
This is يس.

meanings.note: The word 'يسار' (yasaar) means 'left'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: يسار بعد قواوير الورد، ويسار كمان مرة بعد السور الأخضر—لوين رايحين؟!
examples.trans: Left past the flower pots, left again past the green fence—where are we going?!
This is يسار.

meanings.note: The word 'يستنى' (يستنى) means 'يستنى'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: أنا راكضة! دفي الكيكة يا سلمى، وقولي لـ مازن يستنى بصبر!
examples.trans: I am running! Keep the cake warm, Salma, and tell Mazen to wait patiently!
This is يستنى.

meanings.note: Warm Jordanian/Levantine thank-you when someone hands you food, tea, or help (short for يسلموا إيديك 'may your hands be blessed').

examples.trans: Thank you, Salma, for the hot tea!
Thank you, it smells wonderful!

meanings.note: The word 'يصفوا' (يصفوا) means 'يصفوا'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: ضلك اخبزي هيك يا سلمى، ونص عمان رح يصفوا طابور برا بوابتنا.
examples.trans: Keep baking like this, Salma, and half of Amman will line up outside our gate.
This is يصفوا.

meanings.note: The word 'يصير' (يصير) means 'يصير'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: أكيد! العسل الدافي بضل طري وبيلمع من غير ما يحمض أو يصير قاسي متل الحجر!
examples.trans: Of course! Warm honey stays soft and glossy without turning sour or rock hard!
This is يصير.

meanings.note: The word 'يعلقوا' (يعلقوا) means 'يعلقوا'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: هلق ملاحظة راسم الخريطة إلها معنى تام: كانوا يعلقوا فوانيس المهرجان فوق بين هدول الحلقات!
examples.trans: Now the mapmaker note makes total sense: they strung festival lanterns overhead between those rings!
This is يعلقوا.

meanings.note: Everyday conversational bridge introducing an inference ('so that means...'), clarification, or gentle pause ('I mean...').

examples.trans: So the house says hello by itself?
Does that mean there is no heating tonight?

meanings.note: The word 'يفتح' (يفتح) means 'يفتح'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: استنوا—الكتاب عم يفتح لحاله قريب من الفصل السابع عن نعناع الصيف!
examples.trans: Wait—the book falls open all by itself near chapter seven on summer mint!
This is يفتح.

meanings.note: The word 'يقربوا' (يقربوا) means 'يقربوا'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: عم يمضغ ببطء كتير... أوف لا، حواجبه عم يقربوا من بعض.
examples.trans: He is chewing very slowly... oh no, his eyebrows are moving closer together.
This is يقربوا.

meanings.note: The word 'يقطع' (يقطع) means 'يقطع'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: عم يقطع صينية رقم واحد اللي عليها طبقة سكر وفانيليا. شوفوا هالقوام الهش!
examples.trans: He is slicing Tin One with the vanilla sugar glaze. Look at that crumbly texture!
This is يقطع.

meanings.note: The word 'يكتب' (يكتب) means 'يكتب'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: عم يكتب بحروف كبيرة... عشرة من عشرة، لا تغيروا ولا إشي!
examples.trans: He is writing in capital letters... TEN OUT OF TEN, DO NOT CHANGE A THING!
This is يكتب.

meanings.note: The word 'يكتبوا' (يكتبوا) means 'يكتبوا'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: افحصوا جوا الغلاف الأمامي بالأول—الجيران القدام كانوا دايما يكتبوا رقم شارعهم هنيك.
examples.trans: Check inside the front cover first—old neighbours always wrote their street number there.
This is يكتبوا.

meanings.note: The word 'يكشر' (يكشر) means 'يكشر'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: ورشة من قشر البرتقال المبروش بتعطي نكهة لتوت الصيف من غير ما تخلي مازن يكشر!
examples.trans: And a pinch of grated orange peel brightens the summer berries without puckering Mazen!
This is يكشر.

meanings.note: The word 'يكون' (يكون) means 'يكون'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: جداتنا كانوا يدهنوا عسل على معجنات المكسرات من قبل ما يكون في إشي اسمه سكر فانيليا!
examples.trans: Our grandmothers brushed honey over nut pastries long before vanilla sugar existed!
This is يكون.

meanings.note: The word 'يكونوا' (يكونوا) means 'يكونوا'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: راقبي الساعة يا نور—بعد أربعين دقيقة من هلق، لازم هدول الكيكات الصغيرة التلاتة يكونوا مثاليين.
examples.trans: Watch the clock, Nour—forty minutes from now, these three mini cakes must be perfect.
This is يكونوا.

meanings.note: Very common interjection used to urge action or to say goodbye ('yalla bye').

examples.trans: Come on let's go, we're late.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على يلا.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with يلا.

meanings.note: Verb indicating physical contact.

examples.trans: No one is allowed to touch the things.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على يلمس.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with يلمس.

meanings.note: The word 'يمضغ' (يمضغ) means 'يمضغ'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: عم يمضغ ببطء كتير... أوف لا، حواجبه عم يقربوا من بعض.
examples.trans: He is chewing very slowly... oh no, his eyebrows are moving closer together.
This is يمضغ.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for 'maybe, perhaps'.

examples.trans: He is maybe thirty-five years old.
Perhaps he got delayed in downtown traffic.

meanings.note: Used for forbidding or stopping something from happening.

examples.trans: The law forbids smoking here.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على يمنع.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with يمنع.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: The green pharmacy is on your right.
We hung the board to the right of the desk.

meanings.note: Passive/Reflexive verb often used for electricity or water being cut off.

examples.trans: The electricity might get cut off today.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على ينقطع.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with ينقطع.

meanings.note: The word 'يوصل' (يوصل) means 'يوصل'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: هادا الكتاب كان أصلا لـ رامي وعمته قبل ما يوصل لرف الإعارة!
examples.trans: This book actually belonged to Rami and his aunt before it reached the lending shelf!
This is يوصل.

meanings.note: Used for a person or thing falling down.

examples.trans: Be careful the boy doesn't fall.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على يوقع.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with يوقع.

meanings.note: Very common colloquial verb for eating.

examples.trans: He wants to eat an apple.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على يوكل.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with يوكل.

meanings.note: Standard noun for day, often used in expressions like 'el-yom' (today).

examples.trans: Today is a long day.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على يوم.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with يوم.

meanings.note: Adverb 'on a daily basis, every day'.

examples.trans: The ground floor serves the neighbours daily.
We bake fresh bread daily.
